venues.name: Dishoom Covent Garden
venues.description: Buzzy destination for Indian street food in Bombay-style digs with vintage decor & upscale touches.

reviews.text: A modern restaurant in a great central location serving excellent quality Indian dishes. Pretty huge menu can be quite overwhelming but does offer plenty of choice. Fantastic curries including mutton which was excellent and monkfish as well as the classic Chicken Ruby. The Biryani was great with a jackfruit option for the non meat eaters and the black daal was amazing! Some excellent drink options too with refreshing lassis, trendy cocktails and the classic Kingfisher beer and Thums Up Asian cola. Would recommend booking in advance as gets very busy with queues often spanning round the block. Service can be touch and go particularly during busy periods where you’re often fighting to get someone’s attention but overall a great experience with delicious food.

Dishoom doesn’t need a critical review. It’s buzzing like the AI boom. Always has a line out the door, especially this original location. They dine you fast so don’t be discouraged by the long lines. We walked in on a busy Saturday evening & managed to snag a table in 30 mins. The vibe of the restaurant is electric, two floors packed with customers & waiters running around harmoniously. It’s really a well run restaurant with top customer service. The menu is intriguing & drool worthy. We tried a bunch of the things - pav bhaji, house chaat, chicken ruby, garlic naan & Kashmiri Chili ice cream. All taste good, but not out of this world good. They do the nail that Bombay Irani cafe vibe & overall it’s a crowd pleaser of a place. Dishoom is an impressive place to visit but isn’t necessarily a memorable one. Again, it doesn’t need this critique as it does a commendable job and it’s gonna thrive for years to come.

WORTH. THE. HYPE.  This was the best Indian food we've had since...being in India and it's not even close.  We waited maybe 20 minutes for a table for 6 (5 humans and a toddler) which wasn't bad in my opinion.  Our waiter insanely attentive.  We ordered drinks and I wanted to try their chai, but he said I should have something fun so he made it a ~naughty chai~ but then also brought me a regular chai just to try it too.  He brought out a milk for our toddler and it was just slightly warmed (nice touch).  We talked about how we went to Dehli a few years ago and that's where our waiter was from originally, so he brought us out a local dish that we didn't try while we were there.. very thoughtful!  You name it, we got it to try.. vegetable samosas, chili chicken, butter chicken, chicken biryani (the cranberries were actually a surprisingly great touch), the House Black Daal, the broccoli salad, cheese naan, garlic naan, raita.. nothing missed.  We stuffed ourselves silly.  We also came here to celebrate my mother-in-law's birthday and at the end he brought out THREE desserts for her which was insanely nice.  I swear it was the most welcoming restaurant and atmosphere.  I wish I could come back every month.

From the moment we walked in we were welcomed and sat. A lovely dining experience with a great server.
Chicken ruby, lamb chops and jackfruit Biryani were all 10/10
Hiding in that menu is Chilli Chicken which was 12/10. I could eat it everyday.
Excellent dining experience with superior flavors

Dishoom Covent Garden was lively and packed, but our reservation made things seamless. The staff were welcoming and explained the menu clearly, which made ordering easy. Every dish we had was bursting with flavour and beautifully cooked.

We enjoyed the prawn pathia, black daal, cheese naan, mango & fennel lassi, and watermelon sharbat. On our second visit, we tried the chicken berry Britannia, okra fries, raita, and fish - all delicious. The berry crumble with coconut was a standout for me.

Despite the queues, the service was smooth and well-organised. The warm atmosphere, great food, and thoughtful touches made it a fantastic experience. We’ll definitely be back!

venues.name: Gymkhana
venues.description: Tandoor oven roasts, sigri charcoal grills and seasonal curries at Raj-era themed Indian restaurant.

reviews.text:
We visited Gymkhana for lunch and opted for the lunch set menu for two. The portions were generous and perfect for sharing, which is clearly the core part of the lunch set menu concept.

The butter chicken was rich and flavourful, and the bread basket complemented everything beautifully. The aloo chaat starter was another highlight incredibly tasty and the perfect way to start the meal.

We also tried the Goat Methi Keema and Salmon Tikka, which were slightly saltier than our preference not bad by any means, but we personally prefer a milder seasoning. The Falooda dessert was decent but not particularly memorable compared to the rest of the dishes. For that reason, we would rate the food 4/5 overall, while still acknowledging that several dishes were outstanding.

The atmosphere was warm and inviting, and the staff were exceptionally friendly and attentive. They took the time to explain each dish as it was served, which added a thoughtful touch to the whole experience. We were there for a birthday celebration and to our surprise, they brought out a birthday cake and a greeting card such a lovely gesture!

Overall, we left very happy. Great food, great service and a memorable experience. It is slightly on the expensive side, but definitely worth trying at least once. Highly recommended!

We had an absolutely wonderful experience! The food was simply amazing — every dish was full of flavor and beautifully presented. The ambiance made the whole experience even better, with a warm and inviting atmosphere that felt both elegant and comfortable. What truly stood out was the service — the staff were attentive, friendly, and went out of their way to make sure everything was perfect. A truly memorable dining experience that I’d love to repeat! A very special thank you to Kishor, who made our dining experience truly memorable and worth visiting the restaurant.

Gymkhana was a good experience and some food items were really tasty as well. Loved their beet root pao and aloo chaat. The desserts were delicious too. Loved the kheer.

We were seated in the Vault dining area and the service was top notch. Vaibhav
was an amazing host and took great care of us and offered valuable recommendations too.
The quantity of the portions was also great. I did not expect the portions to be this bigat a Michelin restaurant, but was pleasantly surprised.

Why the 4 stars?

I was expecting a bit more visual appeal from both the food and drinks, especially considering the two-star rating. The plating felt quite ordinary to me.
Also, didn't feel value for money given their expensive prices.

Overall a good experience though and would recommend everyone to try once at least.

We visited on London's hottest weekend as a treat for my son's birthday and it was our first ever visit to a 2 star Michelin restaurant.
We wasn't disappointed and it was an amazing experience from the moment we walked through the door.

Service was 5⭐, attentive, but not over intrusive. We were offered to have the menu explained to us, but we all ready knew what we would order.

We ordered Gol Guppas to share and for main, it was signature Butter Chicken, Lamb Chops, Boiled Rice & Onion & Chilli Salad.

The food overall was amazing especially the Lamb Chops, which were medium cooked and so tender. Butter Chicken was mild, so we would have preferred a little more "spice heat" but that's our personal preference. Rice was just normal boiled plain rice but was okay and the Onion & Chilli Salad was fantastic too.

A big thanks for the complementary Venison Keema Naan, again lovely but very rich taste as you would expect from venison.

It was a lovely surprise at the end when my son received a Happy Birthday treat, which made our night more special.

I've seen other reviews about people saying they felt they were being rushed. But for us, that was not the case, even though it was a busy early evening service, so we felt relaxed with very friendly and knowledgeable staff 😊

We had an exceptional meal and were throughly looked after from pre dinner drinks at 42 to the full dining experience as well as a thoughtful dessert brought out as a surprise for my wife’s birthday . Our waiter helped us order the perfect amount of food, whilst making sure we had a rounded variety of dishes. We were blown away with the flavour in the dishes and also the generosity of the portions.

The sommelier was equally excellent at providing help if needed and ensuring our glasses were never empty.

The overall ambience of the restaurant was perfect,  there was a real buzz and energy to the restaurant

The Lasooni Wild Tiger Prawns and the Tandoori Chicken were exceptional

venues.name: Maharaja - SoHo
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

address.formatted: Cafe Espana, 63 Old Compton St, London

venues.vicinity: Cafe Espana, 63 Old Compton St, London

reviews.text: Found this place on Apple Maps, and best Indian I’ve ever had. Service was amazing and super fast, staff were so friendly and kind. 10/10 highly recommend

I visited this restaurant last night on a friend’s recommendation, and it truly exceeded my expectations. The food was absolutely delicious, and the overall atmosphere was warm and welcoming.  The staff were incredibly friendly, and I really enjoyed chatting with them. I’ll definitely be coming back! I recommend everyone to come to this restaurant.

I’ve been craving good Indian food since I landed in London last week. Went to a few “ fancy” places and they were all bad. THIS PLACE IS THE REAL DEAL!!!! Incredible service and delicious AUTHENTIC INDIAN FOOD. I enjoyed every bite and finished everything up until the last crumb. Highly recommend.

If you‘re looking for some really good indian food, this is the place to be! We had a lovely time and went home with our bellies fulled with joy!
The food is fantastic and we will be back surely, Allans service was five stars, thank you for the great time!

What a lovely and delicious experience! I had the Special Thali so I could try a bunch of things and it was all super tasty—I especially liked the naan 🫓

Definitely worth stopping in! The service was also wonderful and kind!

venues.name: Kricket Soho
venues.description: A classic & creative selection of Indian-inspired dishes & cocktails in a contemporary eatery.

reviews.text: Absolutely love this busy but tasty Indian in soho.  Don’t miss out on their rotating list of curries, mains, starters and sides.  Each bite was better than the one before.  Had the venison curry which was absolutely remarkable. I want to go back immediately.
It was a lovely dinner, we had a great time. The mix of flavours and textures was incredible. It wasn't our first time eating Indian food, but these dishes were delicious.

Husband and I had a wonderful experience here sitting at the Chef’s Counter. The server assisted with the number of dishes to ensure we didn’t over order. Had amazing , krispy,  deliciously seasoned Kerlan Fried Chicken and a tender, flavorful Venison Lal Maas. We added cucumber Raita and it was the perfect bite to accompany the venison. Leek and potato Paratha was the best bread to eat with the venison and raita. Wonderful meal!

Kricket Soho is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic and delicious Indian food. The restaurant takes a small, tapas-style approach, which is fantastic for sharing and trying a variety of dishes. The menu changes frequently, so there's always something new to discover, though a few of their main dishes remain as constants.
While some of the newer dishes may not always hit the mark—I didn't find the recent Pani Puri as good as the previous rasam version—the highlights here are truly exceptional. The Keralan fried chicken, chicken gassi, and especially the tadka dal are all incredible. The tadka dal, in particular, tastes so close to what you'd find in a typical Indian home that it feels like a genuine tribute to the cuisine. Hats off to the chef!
Want to know a secret?

Family of four (2 adults and 2 kids). We stopped here for linner  and were seated right away. I was worried that with the social media buzz it would be crowded.

I’ve never heard of a thali before and am so happy to have tried it here. There was so much food that we were able to share and still feel so full. Everything was so well seasoned and the spice level was perfect. The staff were welcoming and really attentive.

venues.name: Maharaja of India
venues.description: Traditional Indian cuisine and tandoori specialities served in a contemporary room in neutral tones.

reviews.text:
⭐ 5

Absolutely incredible experience! This Indian restaurant exceeded all my expectations. The butter chicken,Shashlik Roshila,Garlic Chilly Chicken was rich and flavorful, and the garlic naan was perfectly crisp and soft at the same time.Tandoori Chicken was nicely cooked and juicy.Everything tasted fresh and was beautifully presented.

The staff were warm, welcoming, and happy to make recommendations (which were spot-on). The service was quick but never rushed. The ambiance is cozy and inviting, with traditional decor that adds to the overall experience.

There are tons of vegetarian options too, which is a big plus. Pricing is very reasonable for the quality you get.

Definitely one of the best Indian meals I’ve had—will be back soon and recommending it to everyone.

I visited this restaurant after seeing many great reviews, but my experience didn’t really match the expectations. I arrived at 1:30 PM and the place was nearly empty, yet it took around 35 minutes for our food to arrive, even though we only ordered two curries.

Many reviews mentioned friendly service, but we were served by a different staff member who was just average, not particularly warm or attentive. The butter chicken was a little bland and average, and the other curry tasted just average or even a lil below. Quite overpriced as well considering the portion.

Nayem was an excellent host!! (More than a waiter) he was a teacher of indian cuisine!! Im traveling from Mexico and people told me i MUST try indian food in london, specifically CHICKEN BIRYANI. Nayem even gave me a special yoghurt sauce for my biryani! Gave me a great indian beer!! MAHA RAJA is your best option! A few steps from Trafalgar Square!!

Excellent food! We got served right away, and received our food incredibly fast. Most of us ordered butter chicken with garlic naan, and it was delicious as is visible with the picture below☺️. We had Nayem as our waiter, and were extremely pleased with the serviced we received. His professionalism along with his humour made our visit extra special and memorable!!! Would definitely visit again😊😊

Nayem (our server) was amazing from start to finish and really made our overall experience that much better! He was so polite and helpful with our questions and really made us feel welcome! The food was phenomenal - I totally recommend the chicken 95 and the butter chicken and chicken dansak were out of this world! This is a must when you visit London!

venues.name: The India - Fleet Street
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Had a fabulous time at the restaurant. Khalid provided great service. The food was tasty and served on time. I liked the portions. And the taste is very close to authentic. Will definitely come back
I really enjoyed my time in the restaurant. Khalid and his team were very kind and they gave me great recommendations. I really appreciated the great service!

We had a wonderful dinner here! The tandoori starters were smoky and full of flavor, the lamb shank was tender and fell off the bone, the chicken paprikash was rich and comforting, and the onion bhaji was perfectly crisp without being greasy. The poppadoms were light and crunchy, served with tasty dips to start the meal off just right. Every dish was fresh, well-seasoned, and beautifully presented.

The service was impeccable, friendly, attentive, and very accommodating, which made the whole experience even better.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for authentic, flavorful Indian cuisine with top-notch hospitality. We will definitely be back!
Excellent Indian food in a nice environment with great service. We loved it and will be back!

Hands down the best food I’ve ever tasted. Every bite was full of flavor and cooked perfectly. The customer service was a solid 10/10 friendly, fast, and super welcoming. I’ll definitely be returning again. Highly recommend

venues.name: Chettinad Restaurant
venues.description: Tamil food with many vegetarian options, served in an understated dining room with Indian touches.

reviews.text: Chettinad Restaurant offers a vibrant taste of South India. The Kappa Mincurry blends spicy minced meat with soft tapioca bold and earthy. Chicken Biryani is fragrant, with tender chicken and rich spices. The Masala Dosa is crisp, filled with flavourful potato, and paired with fresh chutneys and sambar. Warm service and authentic ambience elevate the experience. A perfect spot for those craving traditional Chettinad flavours with a touch of finesse.

Best Indian food in town. It serves especially southern Indian food, which suits my taste more as I love hot food. The lamb madras and the house special king prawn, sooooo nice!!!! The service is good, and the decor is very fancy. Defo 5 star review!

We walked past this place and decided to pop in for lunch. We were initially the only guest and another table came later. Service was good. I had the prawn curry which had a heavy tomato base that I wasn’t keen on. This wasn’t mentioned in the menu and I was a little disappointed as I had avoided another dish because it mentioned tomatoes in the description. My paratha was lovely. Restaurant clean and well presented.

(Please note this is a independent and unbiased review based on my personal experience alone and not sponsored of any sort)

Have had this on my list for a while now. I wanted to try this restaurant based on the top
Reviews rated in Google. So went here for a family lunch.

Ambience: The ambience is simple yet cool reflecting the true Chettinad culture. Place is clean and again too small or massive just right in other words.

Service: had only few people considering the people in there which made us wait for your turn to be served but no complaints other than that. Probably good to serve people with water before asking and it’s one of the important cultural habit of Tamil Nadu to serve water first when the guests are allowed to choose the menu.

Food: 5 stars straight. The food tasted fresh, full of flavour and fantastic from the moment you taste it enjoying them all the way in.

Portions were small but then it’s central London so that’s expected. I think if you are going in a group or as family platters were a good option in terms of selection and quantity.

I am posting here photos from what we had to help you understand better.

Party venue: Also, enquired this place for a work dinner and the menu sounded promising for the price and knowing the food tastes good. We didn’t end up booking here as our group size increased where this place wouldn’t fit anymore but otherwise if you are looking for places for small work gatherings in central London, definitely try !

The guy working here gave all necessary details clearly and patiently forgot his name else worth a mention.

Thanks Chettinad for successfully bringing back the authentic taste of Chettinad in London!

This was a pleasant surprise! I had one of the yummiest lamb biriyanis ever. I was never a fan of the curry we used to get as a side in TN but theirs blew my mind away! They also had “walls chai” which I have never heard of before which seems to be a chai liqueur kind of like Baileys/ coffee liqueur! It was just awesome 🤩

venues.name: The India - Cannon Street
venues.description: Classic Indian dishes served in 3 candlelit underground rooms with whitewashed, vaulted ceilings.

reviews.text: Totally deserves 5 stars, food was delicious fresh, beautiful and with a decent price. The stuff was efficient friendly and nice. I took one star from the atmosphere even that the place has good music and very nice look since it's underground, and a vent was missing.

We loved the express lunch sets ~£14 for 2 courses (starter & main).  The veggie samosas were hot, crispy and comforting. The mains come with rice and naan (which was the most delicious naan I've ever had - soft, thin and fluffy). Recommend the chicken jalfrezt and chicken madras (great if you like spicy food).

The Cannon Indian Street is a great spot to enjoy authentic flavors. The food was really good, well-prepared, and full of taste. The ambiance was lively and welcoming, making the overall dining experience even better. A nice place to go for Indian street-style food with a modern touch.

We went for the set menu, the starters were good, but the main course needs alot of improvement. The Chicken jalfrezi and the daal tadka lacked flavours and tasted watery, whereas the prawn saag was good also the starters were flavourful.

Great little find. Googled quirky Indian restaurants with good reviews.  Would never have found this lovely restaurant off the main streets. Very cosy atmospheric setting in a low vaulted ceiling in the basement.  Great food, good service and reasonably priced. Would recommend trying out

venues.name: Aladin Brick Lane
venues.description: Bangladeshi, Indian and Pakistani curries, baltis and grills in small, bring-your-own restaurant.

reviews.text:
Mediocre at best, and as others have said a lot of the reviews are not real. Lacking flavor and spice, and everything served warm.

Lamb samosa were dry and lacked flavor. Shrimp "Blast" was not fresh, and had a strong smell and was mealy - this was supposed to be thier award winning dish. Lamb kurma was gritty and way too sweet. The naan was quite good, but the paratha was gummy. Veggie biryani was decent.  Best part of the meal was the pappadums - although menu says thet are .75p/ea, but somehow got charged £6 for 5 (we made sure to count).

I am sure that they were well reviewed in the past, but thier best days are long behind them. Service was really lacking, and they constantly seem put out just to get us water. Too bad we didn't have Jack serve us, who seems to be mentioned the exact same way in soooo many reviews.

Finally, make sure to check your bill, they seem to just tack on charges. Our bill came to £88.65, but adding it I can't understand how.

I do not recommend at all.

Best  meal ever, lamb bouzjon was fabulous as was everything.  Dudu, Manna and Kawsar  and Abdul were wonderful. Great service, great food, everyone should try this place. Jen and John from Australia 🇦🇺  5 stars 🌟 🌟🌟🌟🌟

Went here yesterday as a birthday treat given to me by my wife.
Food was excellent , service was very good and attentive decor a little dated but not an issue, would come here again.
Atmosphere i marked down simply because we were the only ones in there as it was early.

My sister and I had a lovely time at Aladin tonight for dinner. Jack was our server and he was polite and very friendly. The food was incredible- I have come here a few times before and I am always happy. Will definitely be back!

Maybe there are hidden gems on brick lane but in 2025 it seems that, like this place, they have all become tourist traps. The food was average at best. Also be weary you can be seated in the windowless basement which is not appealing.

venues.name: Dishoom Kensington
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

address.formatted: Barkers Shopping Arcade, 4 Derry St, London

venues.vicinity: Barkers Shopping Arcade, 4 Derry St, London

reviews.text:
This place offers a unique dining experience with its retro-inspired interior and welcoming atmosphere. The service was excellent—friendly waiters. 🍳
The filled breakfast naan was a perfect start, and the chocolate lava dessert with vanilla chili ice cream was simply divine. A must-try spot for great food and warm service!

Went here based on YouTube travel videos.

Also, made a reservation ahead of time because of its popularity.

If you like spicy food, this is the place for you.

We've had spicy food in Southern California, but in comparison to how it was here, what we had before was toned down. There's no holding back at this restaurant.

I wondered why the portions seemed small and just contributed it to European culture until I realized the food is so spicy that we could only eat so much in one sitting.

The servers were friendly enough, although I wish they had left the pitcher of water on our table instead of us waiting for them to refill our cups. Better yet, milk might have been better.

As for the restaurant itself, it's a mix of retro and modern.

The bathrooms were really retro, like the toilets had the pull chain and the sink had the 2 different faucets for hot and cold.

It's a nice restaurant, just know that eating the food here is like being on an episode of "Hot Ones".

Just love Dishroom. A chain overall the London, but consistent good quality food, great service, and beautiful ambiance. We tried what the waiter recommended. The are all good. Even the dessert - rice pudding is good not so sweet. This place is definitely one of the best restaurants in London.

Such an amazing atmosphere! The wait for a walk-in for 2 Monday at 6PM was an hour. We had the option of waiting at the bar so we ordered a drink and were able to sit and wait.

Once seated, we were there for about an hour. The food came out fast, but we ended up waiting for our check for about 15 minutes.

The food was great, but honeslty the Chicken Ruby was too sweet for my liking.

They also charged us for our anniversary cake/ice cream that we didn't order and assuming was a gift. Im sure it was a mistake they would have corrected if we mentioned it, but we were both so jet lagged we just wanted to go back to our hotel after waiting for the check.

Ruth and Beth are such lovely people and made the place very welcoming. The food is phenomenal. The atmosphere is amazing. They allowed my dog (outside seating) and everyone was so sweet towards him! I really like that the restaurant is sustainable and generous.

venues.name: Brigadiers
venues.description: The military bars of India inspired this lively spot with exotic BBQ, full bar, TV sports & pool.

reviews.text:
The day after, and I’m still thinking about how good this food was. I’ve been getting used to eating Asian cuisine, so some flavors don’t surprise me the way they did when I first started exploring food tasting. Brigadiers, however, did the trick. Every dish was extremely flavorful and well-balanced. You could distinguish each ingredient, and none overpowered the other. That applied to everything we ordered.

The service was excellent too: fast even on a packed night. Our waiter was incredibly knowledgeable, and thanks to her recommendations, we were able to make better pairings that elevated the whole experience.

As for the atmosphere, it’s a sports bar, which gave it a lively vibe, yet it still managed to feel cozy and intimate. Very versatile energy overall. The décor was also a nice surprise. I especially loved the hallway leading to the bathrooms.

Brigadiers is a solid Indian spot, buzzing with corporate & casual folks alike. The space is designed to give off an upscale yet relaxed Anglo Indian vibe. What really steals the show is the food. Absolutely delicious. You order their grilled meats or potatoes or even a humble daal and they season it with magical umami that results in a lip smacking, satisfying experience. Butter chicken wings are a tad overhyped- the flavors are lovely but it’s too rich on butter. The Achari paneer is amazing. Service is very good despite how busy they are. I highly recommend Brigadiers for a remarkable gastronomic experience.

Booked us a reservation for two for a last-minute dinner. The ambiance and décor are wonderful. The food was delicious, and the staff were friendly. The restaurant and bar were packed, so making a reservation is a must. Our reservation was a little late; we arrived earlier in hopes that we could get in, but in the end, we ended up only getting our table at the designated time.

Deeply disappointed with the food.. the flavour is there the quality I want to say is there too but I can’t 100% say because the spice is very strong it could mask any food that may not be fresh, but this is not what I’m here for - I am here to talk about our experience the first time ever eating here.

The beef and marrow biryani - the beef was phenomenally spicy - my wife and I eat regularly Sichuan food so we know spicy. The beef was so spicy it wasn’t enjoyable at all..

The guinea fowl kebabs - these specific kebabs must have been 90% salt because we couldn’t taste anything else - each bite felt like a spoon full of salt - horrible.

The goat shoulder curry - goat has a taste I know this but this goat tasted proper nasty, very strong foul goat taste I though I was gonna throw up at the table we took one bite each and left it.

The bread was ok.

Extremely disappointed overall the chef was very heavy handed with the spices - not worth the money at all.

21st June 2025

Brigadiers shouldn’t be this good. One of nine “independent” restaurants - including BAO, Bleecker Burger and Homeslice; did they think we just wouldn’t notice? - among the units either side of a walkway bisecting Bloomberg’s billion-pound, two-building European headquarters smack in the middle of the City, each demarcated by homogeneous management consultancy beige-on-black signage, it offers commercial bookings for up to 200 people and private rooms complete with flat screens and Sky Sports. As much as a place can be “inspired by the army mess rooms of India”, you can’t really imagine the military regiments over there wearing chinos and light blue Charles Tyrwhitt shirts, lining their stomachs with self-pour espresso martinis from the tap and £9 popadoms while they watch the Club World Cup.

Mercifully, we went on a Saturday, and it was actually quite nice. We sat on the terrace, on the Bloomberg Arcade itself, which though not exactly charming, was quiet, and points vaguely west, meaning on the clear and balmy summer evening that it was, as the waiters were in no hurry to move us along, we saw the sky move slowly through the full first third of the colour spectrum as we perused the menu and chatted and ordered and drank and ate and chatted and ordered some more.

First up were the achari chicken skins, Afghani lamb and lasooni chicken skewers, and the Indo-Chinese paneer lettuce cups. I’m a sucker for anything “Indo-Chinese”, its appearance on a menu implying a kind of confident alchemic ability in the chefs through tireless trial and error in the kitchens of ancient multicultural kitchens to combine uncomplimentary ingredients into a coherent and delicious end product utterly unreplicable in my own ethnically homogeneous household. That’s would be a bit of a stretch here - the paneer had just been splashed with a bit of soy, but very skillfully and tastily - and so despite the high quality of the skewered meat and their thoughtful marinades and dipping sauces the chicken skins, crunchy vehicles for dollops of spiced minced glory, were my favourite.

In case you’ve not worked it out by now, Brigadiers is not your local curryhouse. In fact, there weren’t any curries on the menu at all - not a korma, jalfrezi or vindaloo in sight. Instead, after much deliberation, we got an aubergine biryani, tandoori lamb chops and wood-fired kid goat shoulder, as well as a dal markhani and naans between us. I don’t think any of them quite hit the same heights as the starters - although the silky, cumined, gingery goat came closest - but I’d have been happy with any of them as my own individual main. It all just felt like really high-quality cooking of high-quality ingredients in not overly complicated or complex but time-honoured and well-honed flavours , and the fact we were able to graze across all of them over a couple of hours - as well as the extremely decent cocktails too - made for a very pleasant evening indeed.

venues.name: Bengal Village - Best of Brick Lane
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Very beautiful place inside, with a jungle-inspired ambiance. Maybe too crowded seats.
Now let’s talk about the food: we ordered several dishes from the specialties.
GREAT FOOD! TASTEFUL!
Exceptional flavor, a bit spicy (just how I like it).
Meat is the true specialty of this cuisine, and this restaurant prepared and served it with great care and tradition. There’s also a WHOLE vegetarian menu, of course.
Very talented chefs – compliments to them! The waitstaff was extremely kind!
Go visit this place!
Had they same dishes compared to Aladin from across the street, the food was much better and the chapatti’s were made fresh and the lamb vindaloo was delicious, and they serve alcohol.

Visited here in a large group so will excuse the slow service of the food, but the staff were friendly enough and they remained proactive in getting additional drinks. Food was tasty enough and presented well without portion sizes being too large, and the spice levels were right for what the menu described. Toilets are down some very steep metal steps and while not amazing were clean enough. Overall it’s a good option for Indian food in the area at reasonable prices - I’d consider for a group meal again.

Lamb jeers was epic of you don’t want spicy. Full flavour. The chicken Cham Cham masala was great medium spice.

Tommy was a total gent - gave us free shots of brandy and great recommendations.

Amazing curry, amazing service. I had a curry I’d never tried before and it did not disappoint! Id recommend it to anyone :) only issue was the music was quite poor and the room is very echoey so the loud group of American lads were a bit overbearing!

Looking forward to going back soon.

venues.name: Cinnamon Bazaar
venues.description: Inventive Indian cuisine & innovative cocktails, served in a colorful, bazaar-themed space.

reviews.text: My boyfriend and I celebrated our 1 year anniversary here and it was such a wonderful experience! The service was warm and attentive from start to finish, the ambience was cozy and welcoming, and the food was absolutely amazing – some of the best Indian dishes we’ve ever had. To top it off, the staff surprised us with a little anniversary cake, which was such a sweet and thoughtful touch. Truly made our night special. Highly recommend – 10/10

Absolutely delicious Indian "high tea", fantastic service (shout-out to Tanvir), and nice atmosphere. We chose the masala chai ilas out pot of tea to go with the food, which consisted of various chaat dishes, a couple finger sandwiches, and creative fusion patisseries.

Highly recommend to anyone who is a fan of Indian food.

We stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant while exploring London, and it turned out to be the best decision of our trip. The ambiance was warm and cozy, with beautiful décor. The drinks were strong and well crafted, and the food was easily some of the best Indian cuisine we’ve ever had. We thoroughly enjoyed our experience here and already miss it dearly. Absolutely 100% recommended!

It’s our first time at the Cinnamon Bazaar. Everything we had was delicious and well balanced. Dominik and Sakshi were exceptionally welcoming and accommodating- full of smiles and energy! They made our dinner experience extra special! Thank you both!

An evening walk-in, we were seated quickly and then introduced to Dominik our waiter for the evening. Water was served almost as quick as we were seated, and followed up by our drinks. Food arrived hot with incredible flavours a particular mention to the pineapple dish.

Through the evening if a glass or plate was empty it was whisked away with no delay and for the drinks replaced when required. The service from Dominik was some of the best I’ve received within the area and he seemed to make the restaurant flow with no fuss.

I’ve found my new favourite restaurant and will be back with friends to try the taster menu.

venues.name: Dishoom Shoreditch
venues.description: Buzzy destination for Indian street food in Bombay-style digs with vintage decor & upscale touches.

reviews.text: This is a nice restaurant with very friendly staff. It seems to be quite popular, as it was really full and we had to make reservations a few days in advance. The food is good, however, the drinks and coffee were excellent. My friends ordered the chocolate pudding and really seemed to enjoy it. While the dishes aren’t quite as authentic as I expected—more tailored to the local community’s taste—I think it’s still worth experiencing for yourself. Overall, it’s a pretty okay restaurant.

I tried Indian food for the first time with my husband – a very special experience! Everything was different from what we know of Turkish or German cuisine, very flavoursome and interesting. Some dishes took a bit of getting used to, but we really enjoyed trying everything. The atmosphere was great, the staff very friendly and attentive, and we especially appreciated the dessert offered on the house. Definitely worth trying for anyone curious about Indian cuisine.

Wonderful food, venue and staff! We came with our 3 month old, was promptly seated with quick access to a baby change toilet. We had a great waitress who answered any questions we had, made recommendations and helped resolve a minor food 'issue' quickly. Plenty of staff on hand for all tables. Decor and vibe is lovely in here, chatted to other people on our long table too who were interested in the little one.

Food was excellent, as was the drink. We had a non alcoholic cocktail and a crumble sour, which was amazing! Sharing a photo of the food, it was all so excellent, you must try the chilli toast and any curry you fancy. Samosas are great too!

We paid and stayed at the table for a bit to feed the little one, no rush! The manager even helped fill our flask with boiling water before we left, which helped relax us for the next two hours before a feed was due.

Only minor downside would be I think north of £7 for a can of beer is extortionate.

Would come back again!
Brilliant experience. Lovely staff and amazing tasty food. Only fault was that the food all came in one go so it felt a bit rushed but otherwise really really great experience. Highly recommend!!

Everything was awesome! The bartenders were fantastic. Great conversation. The server was amazing and the food was top notch. Has the prawns and also the lamb chops. So flavorful and perfectly cooked. Will definitely be back next time in London!

venues.name: Dishoom Carnaby
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
I was wondering why so many people queueing to the place. It’s modern Indian cuisine.

Tasty, good price vs quality, but same time nothing beyond the universe.
Incredibly well organized the booking process and service in general.

I love open kitchen style, it builds the trust and confidence in a food.

Only one dish with prawns and it’s not the best which I tried. However lamb was delicious

We walked in from the street with no reservations and I feel we got the last table. We had such a good experience. With everything. The service was very friendly and helpful. The food was excellent and very delicious. Especially the salad we had was worth mentioning. I would eat that every day if possible 😍. I will work hard at home to try replicate that🫶🏻

Stopped by this Indian restaurant and was immediately taken by the great view — definitely a lovely setting. There was a long line, but they managed it well by seating us in the bar area while we waited, which was a nice touch. The service stood out — especially our server, who was fantastic and genuinely friendly, making us feel welcome throughout.

Unfortunately, the food didn’t quite live up to expectations and lacked the depth of flavour I was hoping for. That said, the prices were reasonable, and the overall experience was still enjoyable. Would consider giving it another try.

A lovely Indian cuisine restaurant in London that’s definitely worth a visit. The service was excellent, and the restaurant itself was clean, welcoming, and had a great ambiance. The food was of high quality, with rich, delightful flavors throughout. It's set in a very cool part of London, which adds to the experience. Prices were reasonable, making it a great value. Highly recommend!

Good food has always been a source of happiness, and after having some really comforting dishes with the added love and zing from the lovely wait staff, Sheri,(MAJOR SHOUTOUT TO HER!!) this evening—I’m left without words to describe how happy and content I feel walking out of this place.

As a chef and someone from the hospitality industry myself, it makes me truly happy to see and experience such joyful food spaces. A 10/10 recommendation to anyone visiting or living in London who wants soulful food with a touch of Bombay love.

Food: 10/10
Ambiance: 10/10
Service: 100/10

venues.name: Paro - Covent Garden & Strand - Best Indian Restaurant London
venues.description: From royal kitchens to London tables - Indian cuisine elevated to an art form. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

attributions: Paro - Covent Garden & Strand - Best Indian Restaurant London
Paro - Covent Garden & Strand - Best Indian Restaurant London

reviews.text:
Had a fantastic experience at Paro Indian Restaurant in Covent Garden! The food was absolutely amazing — full of flavour, beautifully presented, and clearly made with care. We went for the pre-theatre menu, which was not only delicious but also very reasonably priced and great value for central London.
The atmosphere was warm, welcoming, and vibrant — perfect for a relaxed evening out before a show.
A special shout-out to Joy, our server, who made the experience even better. He was incredibly attentive, friendly, and happy to help with anything we needed. Such lovely service really added to the overall experience.
Highly recommend this spot if you're in the area — we'll definitely be back!

I recently came here with my family, we had a 3pm booking. Pre-booking is kinda essential, the place gets really busy. The interior is lovely, very unique and really adds to the vibe. Staffs were very friendly and helpful too.

Food wise, I’d give it maybe 6/10. Felt like something was missing. One of the starters my sister ordered came a bit undercooked, but once we said it, they did bring out a fresh plate which was nice.

For families coming with a stroller, just to note there’s only a small area at reception where you leave the stroller. They also have a nappy changing room which is handy.

Overall, good restaurant and worth a visit, just food could be little better.

I was absolutely blown away by my experience at Paro in London! Our server Joy was incredibly friendly, attentive, and truly made the evening special. The food was simply outstanding – the best Indian cuisine I’ve ever had! Every dish was perfectly spiced, fresh, and full of flavor. You can really taste the passion and care that goes into the cooking.

Lovely experience. Service was quick and smooth, Sam was attentive and polite. Food was delicious and we loved the flavours, portions were large too. Venue decor was lovely, very cosy. Couple of downsides were the noise levels, it was rather loud, you can still talk but it wasn't always easy to hear. I did feel a little uncomfortable when a qr code was shown to me basically telling me to do a google review there and then, and then the staff member coming back to tell me how to fill it in didn't impress me, if I think something is outstanding I will do a review when I'm ready, which is why I waited until I left the restaurant to do my review. Encourage your customers to do a review, but don't force it on them, it's not professional, this is why I took a star off.

The food was absolutely amazing — truly one of the best dining experiences of our lives. The staff was very kind and welcoming. The dishes were so delicious that we honestly didn’t know which one to try first. We ordered a variety of plates to taste a little bit of everything, and every single dish was outstanding. The naan, especially the garlic bread, was incredibly tasty, as were the samosas. Both the beef and the chicken in sauce were cooked to perfection.

Not long ago, we visited another Indian restaurant outside of London, which had very good reviews, but the food there simply doesn’t compare to what we had today.

5 out of 5 stars — a must-visit! If we are back in London anytime soon, we will definitely return.

venues.name: Pravaas - South Kensington
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Absolutely delish, more modern take on Indian cuisine. Every dish was delicious and elevated from the version I had before. My favourite would be the lamb fillet rogan josh with potato dauphinoise. The chicken mangalorean was really nice with a flavourful and creamy sauce. Staff very friendly and attentive and we enjoyed sitting downstairs with a glass window into the kitchen.

Absolutely mind-blowing food experience! The flavours were outstanding — truly some of the best Indian food I’ve ever had. Every dish was beautifully prepared, rich in taste, and perfectly balanced. The ambience added to the experience — warm, inviting, and elegant, set in a lovely spot in South Kensington. It was my first time visiting, and I went based on a special recommendation — so glad I did! I’ll definitely be coming back very soon. A must-visit for anyone who loves authentic Indian cuisine with a refined touch.

Starters were excellent and the selection of pappadum was nice but very small, chutneys were served in tiny ramekins. I don’t think is appropriate to charge £4.50 for additional chutney so we skipped that. Mains were good as it was the service, perhaps a bit too much, over attentive in an artificial way, sometimes people like to be left alone. Lighting was too bright and the toilets lacked the finesse of a fine dining restaurant. Overall, a very nice experience that I recommend but I won’t return. I will discover a new place next time I’m looking for a fancy Indian!

grabbed dinner at this restaurant with a friend last week! was highly recommended by my aunt who went for dinner with a couple work friends previously in the summer. service was impeccable ✨ thank you for pouring my bubble tea into a restaurant glass (even though it was completely my fault for bringing in an outside drink). the entrees were so delicious. we got the duck and lamb for our mains. lamb was 10/10, duck 8/10. highly recommend in my books

An absolute hidden gem in South Kensington. I visited Pravaas with 14 of my teammates and the entire experience was outstanding from start to finish. Pre-ordering was seamless, the service on the day was warm, attentive, and genuinely personal, and the food, just incredible. Beautifully presented, packed with flavour, and very reasonably priced for the quality. My whole team was thoroughly impressed. Thank you, Pravaas, for a fantastic meal. I don’t give out 5-star reviews often, but this one is well deserved. Highly recommended.

venues.name: The India - City Road
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Hussain and Pavlu are awesome attentive fabulous waiters!! They took great care of us and we enjoyed a spectacular meal of salmon tikka  and duck jalfrezi, garlic naan,  pulao rice and mango lassi! Both the duck and the salmon were cooked to perfection melt in your mouth, delicious!! The mango lassi were absolutely fabulous, too. If you ate in London, you must try this wonderful restaurant on City Road! Pavlu will give you five star service with a five star meal!

Came here for a post birthday meal. From the outset the place looked nice. We had a waiter place us in a nice spot, take our orders & suggest dishes for our aquired tastes. The grill was done to perfection, not too dry or hard with plenty of flavour. In fact all the dishes served with special salad & sauces were lovely. My only slight niggling point was the noise from other tables which meant we often had to talk louder to hear each other. Overall all the dishes had unique flavours & were prepared fantastically. The service from the staff was excellent. Will certainly return back here totally recommend to others.

Food, atmosphere and service was great! Mabzi was friendly and helped enhance our experience at the restaurant from helping us navigate the menu to surprising us with chocolates (and shots!) at the end of our meal. Huge thanks to the team for their amazing hospitality and tasty food!

reviews.author_name: wellen b. c. v. a. de souza
reviews.text:
The food was great, there’s loads of options for choose from and if you like media spicy definitely recommend the one I had which was one of the chef specials, if that’s not for you then I’m sure there’s something else that’s less spicy or spicier.

Mabzi was great at making sure my food was correct and that I was enjoying everything, if you love Indian food I definitely recommend this place!!

Found this great restaurant via The Fork app and was impressed with the positive reviews.
It lived up to expectations with delicious food and excellent service. We started with the pappadams and assorted sauces. So tasty we demolished a double serve. They were perfectly crisp and melted in your mouth. Minted yoghurt and tangy onion tomato condiments were excellent accompaniments.
Mains were from the Chefs special page: a creamy coconut prawn dish that the waiter advised wd be better for us than the much spicier one we had chosen. Serving size equalled 2-3 butterflied prawns each. The other lamb shank dish was very generous and tasty. Lemon rice was a good side.
Seating was comfortable and even with others either side not too noisy or cramped.
Excellent value for money with attentive waiters and food delivered fast. A great choice. Thank you to all who served us!

venues.name: Dishoom King's Cross
venues.description: Buzzy destination for Indian street food in Bombay-style digs with vintage decor & upscale touches.

reviews.text: It had been ten years since the last time I visited the King’s Cross location and it was just as good as I remembered. Every dish was full of flavor and perfect for sharing. Since we didn’t have a reservation, glad we showed up early for a blue hair dinnertime as the line was long outside when we left. So be prepared to wait during busy times, but it’s worth the wait.

It was my first time trying Indian food, and it was absolutely delicious! The flavors were rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and even though the restaurant was quite busy, the food came out quickly. Such a wonderful experience — I’m really impressed!

Visiting Dishoom King’s Cross for the first time was a real treat, and it certainly lived up to its reputation. My wife had been before, so she already knew what to expect, but for me it was something completely new. We were slightly pressed for time as we had a train to catch back up north, so I was a little worried about queues and delays. Sure enough, when we arrived there was already a queue forming outside, and the weather looked like it was about to turn. Thankfully, the team at Dishoom were quick to act – we were seated outside almost immediately, and service began straight away. That efficiency made a big difference, as it meant we could relax and enjoy the meal without clock-watching.

The setting itself was welcoming, even outdoors. Despite the looming rain, the atmosphere carried the lively, bustling energy that Dishoom is known for. There’s a sense that you’re part of something bigger than just a restaurant – more like a communal dining experience where everyone is there for the same reason: good food and a warm vibe. By the time we were leaving, the rain had just started to fall, which made the timing feel almost perfect.

As for the food, it really was excellent. Everything we ordered arrived quickly and was cooked to perfection. Dishoom has a reputation for bold, flavourful Indian dishes that balance authenticity with modern touches, and that was exactly what we experienced. From the seasoning to the presentation, nothing felt rushed despite our limited time. It’s rare to feel both unhurried and well-looked after in such a busy spot, but the staff managed it brilliantly.

Overall, Dishoom King’s Cross was a fantastic first-time experience for me. Efficient service, delicious food, and great timing meant we left full, happy, and on schedule for our train.

Very good Indian food!! The cocktails were delicious and the chicken ruby was one of the best butter chickens I’ve ever had. I will say, the waiter warned my party that it was quite spicy, however I have had spicier. People who can tolerate mild spice will be able to enjoy this dish - it does have a kick, but it is not too intense. Also, I would recommend having a reservation to avoid waiting in a long line to dine. Will be returning next time I am in the city!

The restaurant is beautifully laid out, ample space and great interiors! Lots of details paying homage to vintage India! (Check out the loos - lol)

I found that for the portion sizes you were getting, the prices were pretty inflated. To pay £18 for a biryani and get nothing on the side - not even a small bit of raitha (you normally get this whenever you have an authentic biryani) was disappointing. Paying the same amount (£18) for a single portion of chicken curry - this would normally cost max £15 or less! Similarly, paying over £5 for a small naan or roti was again, disappointing.

We were in a group, and felt rushed by the lady serving us. Whilst she was pleasant overall - I understand that the restaurant may be busy, but members of our group were feeling pressured by the way she was communicating and taking orders which is not how you want to feel when dining out! Especially when there is a big group of us there for a celebration.

Breakfast options look a little more interesting and accessible !

Dishoom is great if you’re after a surreal atmosphere that makes you feel like you have been transported to India, and want to splurge on something a bit special! But unfortunately due to the above, I won’t be coming back anytime soon!

venues.name: Tandoor Chop House
venues.description: Tandoori meats are given a British chop house treatment at this restaurant mixing cultures.

address.formatted: Charing Cross Underground Shopping Concourse, 8 Adelaide St, London

venues.vicinity: Charing Cross Underground Shopping Concourse, 8 Adelaide St, London

reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐ ⭐ ⭐
Dropped in to Tandoori Chop House with friends for an unplanned dinner—no reservation, but the staff were welcoming and got us a table right away. Tried the house Chicken Tandoor and pepper chicken—great flavour, though both could’ve been a bit more tender.
The standout was the Honey Chicken from the small plates—easily my favourite. Chips were perfectly crispy too. Solid spot overall, would definitely recommend.

Just a short walk from Charing Cross Station, this local Indian restaurant pleasantly surprised me. The cocktail menu was impressive—great selection and even better taste! Their Neigroni was really good!🍸

The tandoori chicken was bursting with flavor and just the right amount of spice. I was also impressed by the variety of naan options—fresh, warm, and delicious. For a spot in such a busy area, the food quality really stands out.

Service was friendly, though a little disorganized with the orders, so keep track of what you’ve asked for. Still, the overall experience was very enjoyable. Definitely worth a visit if you're nearby!

This is by far the best Indian restaurant I've ever been to. We had Sunday special menu which is a huge plate for two, and it has a little bit of everything. Now, we're big men, but it's impossible to eat all of it. And the food... Just superb. Butter chicken was out of this world without any exaggeration. I don't know the names of all the things we had on our platter, but everything was very tasty. Lentils in sauce - the most creamiest lentils I ever had... I can't recommend this restaurant enough.

The best chicken tandoori I ha e every tasted.  I loved it.. Will travel 9000 km again to have lunch .   The .a mango sorbet was the bomb.    Great service.  We were seated right without a wait,  but it was a Monday.   Loved the native carmelized milk in a stick.

5* Indian restaurant in Central London. I absolutely love it and recommend it. Very authentic tandoor grill served almost as in a traditional British grillhouse, yet better most Indian/Pakistani restaurants around, imo. I love the Punjabi-style dishes, especially the tandoori chicken, straight 10/10, and the paneer tikka. Every dish here is good, I will definitely revisit several times over.

venues.name: Circolo Popolare
venues.description: Glam, atmospheric eatery, opulently decorated with  20,000 bottles, serving trattoria fare & drinks.

reviews.text:
A detailed mixed review for a Monday night visit. The setting of the restaurant is quite impressive, it’s lovely inside. However it is very popular so is very busy. The tables are extremely close together so it feels like you’re sat on top of your neighbours. The service is very mediocre.

The waitress took the order for your the meal and the first round of drinks that’s about it. I was extremely disappointed to witness a member of staff using the toilet without washing their hands. Quite off putting knowing this when you’ve just eaten your meal.

Food was very tasty and this would be the reason we would visit again. Reasonably priced and good portion sizes.

The dessert however was very disappointing and we felt ripped off when it arrived. £14 for a slice of what tasted like dry shop bought cold chocolate cake. A tiny amount of chocolate sauce on the top didn’t help with the dryness would defo avoid!

Overall a decent experience for the food alone but it sadly lets itself down in many other aspects.

Recommendations are required

My husband and I went to Circolo Popolare for our anniversary dinner, and it was such a wonderful experience.

Ambience: ★★★★★
The restaurant is absolutely stunning—perfect for a romantic date night. The interiors are beautifully decorated, featuring elegant Italian ceramic plates and a warm, inviting atmosphere. The place is spotless and well-kept, making it a delight to dine in.

Service:
The service was excellent—friendly, attentive, and quick, which made the evening even more enjoyable.

Food:
The quality of ingredients truly matches what you’d expect in Italy. We started with the Trio d’Olive, which was fresh and flavourful, and the Mozzarella in Carrozza—crispy on the outside, perfectly cheesy inside, and served with a delicious tomato sauce.

For my main, I had the Mafaldine al Tartufo, which was incredibly delicious—rich, aromatic, and bursting with truffle flavour. I highly recommend trying this dish.

My husband ordered the Tagliolini Granchio e Limone. It was decent, but didn’t quite match the wow factor of the truffle pasta.

Note: The only downside was that the toilets were a little dirty and had an unpleasant smell. However, this did not take away from the fact that the restaurant itself is really nice, clean, and beautifully maintained.

Overall, we had a memorable anniversary dinner, and I would definitely return—especially for that Mafaldine al Tartufo!

What a beautiful experience!
My husband and I spent our “thanksgiving” here, and we’re not disappointed! We started with the burrata- absolute perfection floating on a delicious tomato reduction. For our main course we paired the ragu with a Sicily wine, it was fresh and delicious. To end our beautiful experience, we had the tiramisu! Both the food, service, and atmosphere were outstanding- we will be back!

From the outside this looks like a quiet unassuming restaurant. Once you get inside it turns into a huge barn-sized place. Interesting decor as all the photos in reviews show. Bottle display is impressive. Because it’s all open inside it can be quite loud with conversation, which combined with the semi-disco feel of the music makes for a high energy vibe. The food choice is varied enough to satisfy most tastes in my opinion. Quality is decent. I had pizza, smashed potatoes and stracciatella. The latter was novel for me and very nice as an appetizer. Service is reasonably efficient although they did forget the pizza order; they recovered quickly and all was well for us. Draft beer is from a local craft brewery. It appears to be an extremely busy place even for lunch, so reservations are a must; you can’t call and bookings are done online. That turned out to be easy and we got a reminder email well in advance. If you want a little bit of a quieter meal ask to be seated at the back behind the kitchen. It’s popular for birthdays and celebrations. Worth a visit if you plan on being in Oxford street.

Went here with my partner for our anniversary and had such a lovely evening. The restaurant is absolutely beautiful – warm lighting, bottles and postcards everywhere, and flowers hanging from the ceiling. Even the toilets are gorgeous with their unique Italian style!

The food was incredible – especially the carbonara, which they make right in front of you in a cheese wheel. The cocktails were great too, and I loved the quirky glasses they came in. The staff were so kind and attentive, and even gave us an anniversary card, which was such a sweet surprise. Paying was super easy through a QR code and Apple Pay.

The only downsides were that it was quite warm inside, and there’s an extra platform charge when paying, which feels a bit unfair.

Overall, it’s a stunning restaurant with amazing food, lovely staff, and a great atmosphere – perfect for a date night or special occasion!

venues.name: Carlotta
venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Amazing food. Amazing service. Amazing waiters and waitresses. Everyone was so welcoming and friendly. I been here twice so far and loved every time I visited. I highly recommend this place. I would suggest the shrimp cocktails, they’re the best thing I’ve ever had!

We came with my husband, parents and 11 month baby. The decoration is really pretty and interesting style. The food is also tasty with the cesar salad, arrabiatta pasta, cod and beef. We had also the tiramisu which was creamy and yummy. And finally the waiter Khan was very caring, kind and professional.

Just went to this fun Italian spot tucked into one of London’s cutest neighborhoods — right along a lively shopping street where you can wander before or after your meal. The place has such a fun vibe — it’s buzzing, loud in a good way, with people having fun and plates flying out of the kitchen and drinks from the bar.
The food? Properly delicious. Think generous carpaccio, spicy pasta, tender meat, that feel straight out of Italy, and starters you’ll want to share (but probably won’t). The drinks are spot-on too — from classic cocktails to fun ones (didn’t try the wines ) that somehow makes everything taste even better.
One thing: the line is no joke. Everyone seems to want in, and I get why. Definitely book ahead unless you enjoy standing on the street watching everyone else eat. But honestly, once you’re inside, it’s worth the wait. The crowd is such a mix — locals, tourists, couples, big groups of friends — and it just adds to the whole atmosphere.
If you’re looking for somewhere lively, tasty, and full of energy, this place nails it

From the bar all the way to the food…Everything was amazing. The whole restaurant had this vibe of a private privilege social club. Music playing in the background. The food had so much taste. Not to forget the espresso martini. Mamma Mia

Dined at Carlotta in Marylebone and had a really enjoyable experience. The food was excellent — authentic and full of flavor — paired with that classic Italian ambience that makes the whole evening feel special. Service was attentive and friendly throughout, adding to the welcoming atmosphere.

Even the details stood out, like their very stylish toilet, which matched the restaurant’s chic design. Overall, a great spot for Italian dining in London, and one I’d happily return to.

venues.name: Ave Mario
venues.description: Cool Italian restaurant whipping up meat dishes, pizza, pasta & desserts, plus weekend brunch.

reviews.text: My first time at Ava Mario and I wanted to be sat downstairs as upstairs had a very different decor so asked to change seats. I’d say go downstairs if you want more of an experience. I was initially told that I couldn’t order the carbonara just for one person but then another waiter said I could which was great as I wanted a different dish to my daughter. The pasta was delicious but I was a little disappointed with the salad as I would’ve  liked more Gorgonzola and walnuts. I’d definitely revisit as I’d like to try more of the mains.

This place is a must do, great food and fun atmosphere.  If you are lucky enough to go down 3 levels to eat you will be eating kitchen side with a lively party atmosphere.  This place has truly great food and is also a fun place to hangout!
The place is beautiful inside and the foods are great. Lemon pie is a litle too much but ok, tiramisu is better! Carbonara was good but funghi pasta was amazing 10/10. I recommend it

Great value Pre-Theatre Menu with generous portions served quickly – perfect before a show. Consistently good food, service, and décor from Big Mamma. The lemon pie is insane! Booths a little snug if you’re tall (or wide😂), but overall highly recommend!

The vibes is nice, but the food was very dissatisfying. When we received the 12£ calamari fritti, it was really disappointing , it was dry a bit burnt and the serving was small. The bruschetta is nice. The tagliarini is very salty, and carbonara is a bit bland. Mojito is 90% ice and 10% mojito. 👎👎👎 won’t be panning to visit again.

venues.name: Grasso
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: I never ever leave reviews but I had to after my experience at Grasso yesterday with my mum. We were running late due to traffic delays and they were super understanding about it. The food was incredible, with huge portion sizes and lovely atmosphere/music! The staff were really friendly too. I would honestly recommend this to everyone!

Really lovely Italian-American restaurant. The Mozzarella Bites were the best I've ever had, as a vegetarian they were able to accommodate doing it not on top of the Nduja sauce and keeping it on the side. It had a good amount of Mozzarella and the hot honey twist was incredible. The pizza tasted New York style with a crispy base and a good amount of sauce on the pizza. We celebrated a birthday and the staff were incredible in assisting with candles, plates for a cake that was bought in from outside. I highly recommend and will be going back.

Very nice restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating. We arrived at around 20:15 on a Friday night and only sat down at 21:00 so definitely book in advance. The vibe was chill so we didn’t mind waiting. The service was very quick and the food also arrived quite quickly. Everything was delicious - the sauce was a 10/10.

Grasso is stunning. The staff were all so friendly, attentive, made us feel welcome, the atmosphere was lively yet not overpowering with loud noise or lights, and the food was so good! We had the mozzarella sticks (recommend to share this as the portion is very generous) and I regret not filming a cheese pull because these things kept going! I had the lamb ragu and it was incredibly tender, very well portioned and tasty! We finished by sharing a cheesecake (also recommended as the portion was generous!), tasted so fresh with a very subtle hint of lemon and not too sweet.

We came to celebrate my graduation and the staff made the effort to congratulate me and put little candles in the cheesecake which was a lovely touch.

Absolutely will be coming here again!

We absolutely loved our experience at Grasso! The staff was incredibly friendly and welcoming, creating such a warm and inviting atmosphere. The ambiance was charming, and the food… simply outstanding.
We started with the mozzarella sticks—crispy on the outside, perfectly cheesy on the inside—absolutely delicious. The chicken parm was phenomenal, with tender, juicy chicken and rich, flavorful sauce. And the pizza, A true standout—fresh, flavorful, and baked to perfection. We can’t wait to come back

venues.name: Gloria
venues.description: Italian fare in an elevated dining room with a marble bar, mirrored ceiling, & rich, eclectic decor.

reviews.text: We came here for my husband’s birthday and had such a lovely evening! The atmosphere was calm and romantic with low lighting, even though it was busy. The pasta and pizza were delicious, and the food overall was really tasty. Our server was super friendly and made the night feel extra special. Highly recommend!

My partner and I have been a handful of times and thd food is always amazing. Today we had wonderful service! We were well looked after by the server Gervasio for my partners birthday meal. Food was amazing and they were super attentive and caring towards a friend who has a few severe allergies. Our food did take a short while to come out but we deduced this might be due to the kitchen doing a full clean down for our friend with allergies before cooking their meal. Thank you so much we will absolutely be back again!

The atmosphere was superb. A big wow!!!
Based on our experience on fancy-decor restaurants that we have been, the foods did not strikingly impress us. But the foods here are exceptional. Perfectly cooked pastas. Intense flavors. Tiramisu and Cheesecake are  a must-try.   Probably placing this as my no.1 in category of Italian restaurants in London so far.

Amazing dinner at Gloria! The food was delicious, the atmosphere warm and lively, and the service very personal. Our waiter was friendly and attentive, making the whole evening even better. Highly recommend for anyone who enjoys great Italian food and a welcoming vibe.

Visited Gloria for a friend's birthday dinner, and we had a lovely meal. Our server Rebecca really looked after us, making us feel very welcome and at home, and happy to make recommendations and explain different dishes and cocktails to us. The focaccia to mop up stracciatella was a delight as were the veal croquettes. Our main of truffle malfadine, served from a pecorino wheel, was tasty but very filling, meaning we could sadly not manage dessert, but we did have some great digestifs to compensate. The atmosphere was buzzing and leafy settings very pretty. My only gripe would be that the lighting was turned down low very early in the evening - I saw several diners switching on their phone lights to read the menu - but overall we had a great time and would be keen to dine in their other venues.

venues.name: Bocca di Lupo
venues.description: Authentic small or large plate Italian dining in compact restaurant with neighbouring gelateria.

reviews.text: This restaurant has been on my list for ages and I’m glad I finally came here! Service is so friendly and they make you feel very welcome. Every dish we ordered was beautifully served and tasted amazing! They even gave me a little birthday card and ice cream because it was my birthday! Love an Italian restaurant but this place is extra special! Will definitely be returning.

Popped in for lunch without a booking. Shown seats at the counter, which is by far the best! The menu is split between areas of Italy and you can go on a full culinary tour!
The service is excellent. you have the feeling of being treated like a beloved regular, even if it’s your first time.

I finally made it to Bocca di Lupo — and as an Italian, I can honestly say the food was delicious. It was a fantastic lads’ night!

We started with Manhattans on arrival, then enjoyed at the table:
•	Sage leaves with anchovy
•	Olives stuffed with minced pork & veal
•	Sea bream carpaccio with orange & rosemary
•	Ricotta & spinach ravioli with butter & sage
•	Pappardelle with venison stracotto
•	Roast teal with schiacciata con l’uva & guanciale

Highly recommended desserts:
•	Chocolate & marzipan ball with rum & raisins
•	Affogato al caffè
•	Uva fragola sorbet

All perfectly paired with a Teroldego Rotaliano Terrazze della Luna, 2023 — a smooth and elegant red.

A special thanks to James for the impeccable service — well done, buddy!

Amazing solo dinner at the counter. Loved the enthousiastic service and the food was delicious. Refined Italian kitchen with
delicious food, my favourite was the risotto.
If I’m in London again, I’ll revisit this place as their other food looked amazing as well.

I recently dined at Bocca di Lupo under somewhat unusual circumstances, as I had lost my voice just before the visit. Despite this, the staff were incredibly kind, patient, and accommodating, making the experience feel seamless and comfortable.

The food was delicious. We especially enjoyed the risotto and the asparagus. Both were full of flavour and really well done. Everything we tried was delicious. I can't wait to visit again.

venues.name: Faros Oxford Circus
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

address.formatted: Highlight House, 22-24 Great Portland St, London

venues.vicinity: Highlight House, 22-24 Great Portland St, London

reviews.text: The food was just as good as people say. The beef ragu was delicious and had great deep flavors. We also enjoyed the cheese bread and truffle fries. But the thing that can make or break an experience is the waiter. We had Jass and this young man did an outstanding job taking care of all the outdoor patio tables and was always on top of things. Lovely place and I’m glad we were able to walk you and get a table. We sat outdoors and it was cold outside but with the heaters they have installed I was warm! To finish things we split the tiramisu and it was delicious just like every thing else. Great place and atmosphere was on point.

The food was incredible and the service was impeccable.  Ozzy was our waitor and he was very attentive.

We had the burrata salad which was very tasty, the octopus cappacio was not as good but then I guess octopus doesn't have a strong flavour anyway, but the beef cappacio was very good.

Now, the main courses, wow! The truffle pasta was my favourite, the pasta itself had a great texture, and what I liked the most is that it wasn't soaked in cream, which often happens with a mushroom/truffle pasta dish.  Then the beef Ragu tagliatelle was also great, the beef Ragu was well cooked and seasoned, the tagliatelle again had a great texture.  We also had the risotto mare, there were lots of seafood in it (big prawns, baby squid, clams) and it was definitely cooked with a suace made from the prawns heads, it was super tasty.  We also had the pizza and it was great too.

For dessert, we ordered the tiramisu and chocolate bomb, both were very tasty as well, but they were quite heavy, so we were glad that we shared the desserts amongst the four of us.

Great restaurant, will definitely go again, high recommend it to anyone that's looking for a good quality Italian restaurant to visit in central London.

Absolutely perfect from service, atmosphere and the food. Ozzy looked after our table and made us feel welcomed from start to finish. Starters and mains were above expectations finished off with the best tiramisu I have ever had!
Will definitely visit again and recommend anyone who comes to London.
Best to book ahead to avoid disappointmen

Faros is absolutely fantastic! The food is top-notch — every dish is full of flavor and beautifully prepared. The service is excellent as well; everyone is attentive and welcoming. A special shoutout to Jass — he’s incredibly friendly and provided outstanding service that made our dining experience even better. Highly recommend this place!

We had an amazing evening at Faros in London! The food was absolutely delicious — the truffle pasta was rich, creamy, and packed with flavor, easily one of the best we’ve ever had. The ravioli were equally impressive, perfectly cooked and beautifully presented. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients and the care put into each dish.

The drinks were also a highlight of the evening — creative, well-balanced, and served with style. The atmosphere was warm and vibrant, and the staff were incredibly friendly and attentive without being overbearing.

Faros exceeded our expectations in every way. We’ll definitely be back and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable dining experience in London!

venues.name: Padella
venues.description: Modern bistro with a short list of housemade pasta dishes accompanied by wine & Italianate drinks.

address.formatted: Borough Market, Padella, 6 Southwark St, London

venues.vicinity: Borough Market, Padella, 6 Southwark St, London

reviews.text: Fantastic little restaurant with friendly staff and quick service. Our host (sadly didn’t catch his name) was very welcoming, recommended serval dishes and provided a complimentary glass of wine. Food was served fast and hot. The tiramisu for dessert was to die for. Couldn’t recommend enough and will definitely be back :)

Loved our experience at Padella! We visited for the first time for lunch and arrived right as it opened for the day, which helped as the restaurant filled up quickly. Staff were courteous and friendly, and the kitchen was a well-oiled machine. Seated at the bar, we got a front row view of the action, which was part of the charm (highly recommend)! The pasta was well made and if you’re visiting London, you gotta check Padella out!

I appreciated the warm welcome. I was seated promptly and even allowed to change seats. The waitress, Nura, helped me with my order,  her suggestions were exceptional.
