reviews.text: Went for lunch on a Saturday....the Express menu is good value for money. You can't substitute items on there and pay the difference. (I wanted to try their prawn toast). The tuna taco was a great shout. The salmon was also really good. Dessert outdid my expectations. Would recommend a visit!

We were excited to finally try Shack-Fuyu after hearing great things. We booked in advance, and it was packed when we arrived.

Between us, we shared:
Izakaya - tenderstem broccoli, edamame, wagyu beef tataki, crispy fried squid, Okonomiyaki prawn toast
Raw - seared salmon sashimi
Hot Stone - sukiyaki wagyu beef, pulled lamb
Robata - grilled salmon fillet
Dessert - kinako French toast

The salmon dishes were the standouts - perfectly cooked and full of flavour. I’m more of a savoury person, but even I loved the French toast. The broccoli and lamb were also really solid picks. Overall, the food was good.

Unfortunately, the experience let it down. We were seated next to a loud table who arrived after us but were served first, and they spent the evening shouting across the table. Our drinks took 25 minutes to arrive, and we had to ask multiple times - even though we could see them sitting at the bar. We were also served the wrong dishes more than once and had to chase missing items. At the end, we were even given the wrong bill.

I get that it was busy, but the service felt chaotic throughout, with no apology or effort to make up for it.

Glad we tried it, but I probably wouldn’t go back. For the price, we expected a better overall experience.

—

Edit: despite a comment on this review asking me to get directly in touch i’ve since emailed the provided address and received no response

Great selection of menu items, we were pleasantly surprised by the serving sizes and flavour profile. The French toast and matcha ice cream is a must have for dessert. The Shack’s spritz was a very nice Japanese take on a classic cocktail. Perfect for a nice warm Summer’s day. The quality of the service was superb, the staff were very friendly.

The food was excellent, that must be known.

Our waitress however took our order wrong, we had the Katsu Curry. It was lovely, but we had an event we had to get to so no time to really ask to change…which pushed our bill up.

Otherwise the restaurant itself is very loud, which may have explained the above ordering issue. The seating is cramped and not particularly comfortable.

I had high hopes, will try and return to try dessert and actually eat what I wanted. But as a first impression, not totally blown away despite very high hopes.

We finally got to visit this restaurant after hearing so many great things about it (mostly from Off Menu!). It lived up the hype! The food was excellent and the service was quick, but still friendly. We had a good selection of food and it was all executed perfectly. Great range of flavours and textures. It got quite busy around 5pm on the Saturday so it’s worth booking in advance.

venues.name: YiQi
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: The food was amazing. The flavour and the portion are good and value for money. The signature wing taste amazing with honey glaze and charcoal on the wings. The crab curry with steam rice was top notch. Would always recommend this place to have a good and flavour Asian cuisine. BOBY service was attentive and caring. Keep up guys. Top class

Chill yuzi Crab: SO good! The sauce is this amazing tangy, micro-spicy, refreshing masterpiece. AND it came with little buns to mop it up (genius!)The crab was massive – my friend and I were huffing and puffing for ages!
Sambal Seafood Fried Rice: Huge portion with whole prawns and squid rings.
Nyonya Lemongrass Grilled Chicken: Every piece was crackling crispy outside and then – BAM – super juicy inside. The green chili sauce made it even fresher.
King Oyster Mushroom Salad: Grilled mushrooms, a zesty sweet-and-sour dressing, and pomelo bits.
Thai Iced Tea: It wasn't sickly sweet! Friends, for a Thai tea born in the UK, not being sweet means it was born to be a good milk tea! The Tamarind Plum drink is for all my sour-loving friends.
Service: Impeccable. It felt just like the thoughtful service back home – bibs for the crab, frequent plate changes, hot towels. The manager says they roll out new dishes almost every month. I need to come back weekly to keep up!

I can’t find one bad thing to say about the quality or taste of the food. We randomly walked into this place, and we’re so glad we did—everything was excellent. The only miss for us was the drinks (we tried the tamarind mojitos and the flavor just wasn’t great). Other than that, a solid 10/10. Highly recommend if you’re in Chinatown, London.

Alright, seeing this many high reviews made me suspicious but DAMN this food is outstanding and worth the wait. You must must try the Guinness crispy chicken. I think it was the best chinese chicken dish I have consumed. The green tea latte is delicious, and the pad Thai was awesome. But that chicken is to die for. And the staff are so nice and helpful. Highly suggest!!!

Love food, in the heart of Chinatown!

Amazing dishes my favourite was the Guinness fried chicken!

A elegant pan asian restaurant with tasty dishes!

Loved the ambience and service was great!

venues.name: Tattu London
venues.description: Chic, spacious restaurant turning out sophisticated, contemporary takes on Cantonese classics.

address.formatted: The Now Building Rooftop, Outernet, Denmark St, London

venues.vicinity: The Now Building Rooftop, Outernet, Denmark St, London

reviews.text: We have been to Tattu Manchester and we couldn’t pass the opportunity to visit Tattu London. The food is simply extraordinary! Mouthwatering and exceptional. Every dish better than the previous. We especially liked the starters like wagyu beef dumplings, mushroom rolls or pork bao buns. Caramel soy beef was exquisite. So tender and juicy. Our server, Alex, was really friendly and he made our night even better. The restaurant is very good at adjusting for allergies which we appreciate. The decor is beautiful and stylish. We will definitely come back!

Celebrated my husband’s birthday at Tattu. They booked us an amazing table with window to ceiling views. The ambiance and aesthetics were beautiful and cozy and the food was absolutely delicious. Funny enough we were actually advised we ordered too much food but we polished our plates nonetheless lol. Our waiter Peter was so lovely and gracious (he snapped some amazing photos of us!). They also surprised my husband with a complimentary birthday treat.

Overall a fantastic experience and would definitely recommend!

To make our overseas friend’s Birthday celebration memorable, particularly as this was their second visit to London, we selected the Tattu restaurant, which exceeded our expectations from the moment we entered through the eliminated tunnel and ascended the lift. We were warmly greeted at the lift with exceptional hospitality while proceeding  to our table.

The restaurant’s ambiance is equally impressive, featuring exquisite decor. And The live DJ playing great music in the background.

The culinary offerings were equally impressive, with each delectable dish presented artistically and bursting with incredible flavours. The service was smooth, friendly, and never rushed, the attentive waiter further contributed to the exceptional ambience of the evening.
They even brought out a surprise birthday treat for our friend. it was a lovely touch that made the evening more special.

I highly recommend dining at Tattu, a renowned restaurant celebrated for its exceptional cuisine, impeccable service, and memorable dining experience.

This weekend was my second time visiting Tattu London and once again, it did not disappoint! The food, drinks and service were exceptional. Their lunch menu was also really great value for money with decent portion sizing and tasty options!

A huge thank you to both Mandy and Ahmed who were both amazing at their jobs and made the experience very enjoyable for us with their friendly nature and fantastic recommendations regarding the cocktails/veggie options!

We will return! :)

Tattu London offers a refined and elegant dining experience. The atmosphere is chic and intimate, perfect for a special evening out. The service was impeccable — attentive, warm, and professional from start to finish.

The food was beautifully presented and full of flavor. The duck dumplings were a standout — rich, tender, and perfectly balanced — definitely my favorite dish of the evening. Most of the dishes were excellent, though the salmon was slightly overcooked for my taste. Still, everything else was absolutely delicious.

I was a bit less impressed by the cocktails. Despite the restaurant’s strong reputation, I found them overpriced and not particularly well-balanced — the alcohol was barely noticeable, which made them feel a bit flat.

One drawback worth mentioning: there was no air conditioning, and it got uncomfortably warm inside, which detracted a little from the overall experience given the summer heat.

Overall, Tattu is a wonderful place for a stylish night out, with fantastic food, a lovely ambiance, and top-tier service — just a few details that could be improved.

venues.name: The Duck and Rice
venues.description: Stylish British pub with copper beer tanks and upstairs dining room serving elevated Chinese dishes.

reviews.text:
My girlfriend and I visited The Duck and Rice ahead of my birthday and it honestly couldn’t have been better. The food was absolutely delicious, we shared sweet and sour chicken, chicken chow mein, bao buns and venison pastries, and every single dish was so tasty.  You could really tell the quality of the ingredients and the care that went into the cooking.

A big shoutout has to go to our server, Hannah. She was so friendly, attentive without ever being overbearing, and genuinely made the whole evening feel special. It’s rare to come across service that feels that personal, and it honestly made all the difference.

I have a peanut allergy, so I have to be careful eating out particularly with Chinese food, but Hannah handled it brilliantly. She was knowledgeable, reassuring, and made me feel completely at ease, which meant I could just relax and enjoy the meal.

The place itself is lovely and inviting, and seems like a great place for a casual lunch or a more formal dinner.

The combination of amazing food, a lovely atmosphere, and such thoughtful service made this the perfect place to celebrate. We left already talking about what we’ll order next time.

Came here for dinner before a West End show. We were a bit early for our reservation, so grabbed a few drinks at the bar before our table was ready. For 3 people we ordered prawn chips , shumai, and XLB to start; then assam chilli king prawn (it is extremely spicy- fair warning!), crispy aromatic duck (quarter), pak choi with garlic, and Singapore fried noodle as mains.

Food arrived fairly quickly and everything was fantastic. They swapped our initial appetizer plates for clean plates when the mains came out. They present the crispy duck to you whole, then return with it shredded (with the bone on the plate) so you dive right into it more easily.

If I was local I'd probably make it a habit to do pre-show dinner here regularly. Everything was great!

I went on vacation with my family to London this summer, and this was a great place to dine at considering the numerous amount of restaurants nearby. The seating itself was a little tight, and I did see some customers struggle to get into them so as to not make contact with separate parties. Otherwise, the customer service was good, and the food arrived at a good time as well. My family and I enjoyed the duck the most, but everything else was delicious.

⸻

I visited this restaurant for my sister’s birthday and had such a lovely experience! The food was delicious, the ambiance was warm and welcoming, and the staff were genuinely kind and helpful. Everything—from the service to the setting—made the evening really special. We truly enjoyed ourselves and would definitely come back again!

I visited on Sunday 24th August as an early celebration for my Wife's birthday.
I went with my wife, my 8yo, my sister in law, her 3yo, and her husband.
From start to finish, service and food was on point. My son's reaction to the food was "this is definitely a 5 star review daddy"
The review isn't just because of this statement, but the food was absolutely spot on, delicious!
The waitress was attentive, but not over the top of in your face. We were never left waiting to make any orders and the atmosphere of the place was buzzing.
I highly recommend you visit if you are looking for a great meal in a beautiful surrounding.
Thank you for making my wife's birthday meal great.

venues.name: Din Tai Fung Covent Garden
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: As always, fabulous food! I’ll highlight the green beans and the incomparable xiao long bao are just sublime. This place had the signature spicy sauce as well that was a huge hit with our table. The service was delightful, and I’ll give particular gratitude to our excellent waiter Eddy who was so attentive and patient with us! The only thing to note was that it was a bit loud and bustling and overly lit which wasn’t super conducive to the atmosphere of the place. That said, I’d listen to heavy metal music under the heat of the blazing sun just to have more of those dumplings so Din Tai Fung will always be a go-to for that heavenly food!

WE CAME HERE THREE TIMES IN 3 DAYS. Amber was our waitress and was phenomenal. The food was amazing and the atmosphere was even better. Had multiple dishes from the classic pork xiao long bao, to the noodles in spicy sauce and the prawn pork dumplings.

The food was great! Everything came out very fast and tasted really good. The noodles and dumplings were excellent. The Mai tai is delish. Our server Jenny was amazing! My mother kept saying how amazing she was (and she can be hard to please)!! Jenny was the perfect waitress - if i come back,
I will be asking for her! If

Wow such great fresh tasting noodles and dumplings. Probably one of the best noodles and dumpling wrap I have had. Just popped in for a snack will have to come back.

Edit: came back 2 days later for dinner to try more of the menu and it did not disappoint. Best are the noodles and dumplings.

We had lunch at this branch few days ago. As a Taiwanese living in Europe, I didn’t have high expectations for the restaurant because most of us think the best Din Tai Fung is still the ones in Taipei, but DTF Covent Garden really blew my mind. All the food we ordered was executed perfectly, and of course the service was impeccable. Our Taiwanese waiter Jenny was friendly and efficient, showing the true hospitality training of this brand that we all feel proud of.

venues.name: Fatt Pundit
venues.description: Tapas-style Indo-Chinese specialties, fruit coolers & wine in a snug, industrial-chic space.

reviews.text: Had an excellent dinner here. Had to wait 20 min without reservation on a weekday night. Manisha provided top notch service once we were seated. Nice take on Indo Chinese cuisine, done with care. Food and service great, just one star removed on atmosphere as it is quite loud.

Arrived in London absolutely hangry, and Mervin was kind enough to squeeze us in. He truly saved the night! Their 4.9 rating is well deserved. The food was spectacular, the service just as impressive. My wife and I couldn’t get enough of the crispy spinach. And the lamb chops? Some of the best I’ve ever had, anywhere. Fatt Pundit absolutely lived up to the hype. Can’t wait to come back next time we’re in London!

Food was 10/10 and such great value for money.
If you need halal only then ask for the halal menu just so the experience is easier and clearly differentiated.

We tried the goat, beef and chicken momos they literally exploded in our mouths with flavour and juiciness. Our favourite was the beef. The sauces that went with them were delicious too.

The lamb chops were also amazing, they were thick and cooked and marinated to perfection.

We also got the ribeye dry red chilli, which was like a curry and stir fry and wow…probably some of the best saucy style beef I’ve tried. Cooked to perfection. Juicy, tender and melt in the mouth.

The Bombay chilli prawns were also amazing we ate that with the egg Szechuan fried rice. Everything was spiced to perfection, if you can’t hack chilli then maybe asked for a milder flavour. If you’re used to chillier food then it’s perfect. Probably a Nando’s level hot - extra hot as a comparison.

We also got a bing bread I think this was like a laccha paratha. This was so delicious you could taste the ghee and the crispy layers. I would happily eat this with some desi tea.

The most underwhelming item was the lollipop chicken and the sauce was just OK but it was still very fresh and delicious.

We also got the sizzling brownie and wow this was sooo delicious, with it being on a skillet the bottom of the brownie gets slightly chewy. It was just a perfect dessert simple but 10/10.

The service was also 10/10 alongside
the ambience and experience. The place had a calm and chill vibe. Even though it was extremely busy. The waiters and the managers carefully tended to all tables smoothly it was literally jammed from 5pm. You can tell the staff enjoy working there as they just vibe together.

I would definitely go again very soon to try the items I didn’t get to try.

Thank you!

BTW it’s like a 40 minute walk  from KGX.

Service was very polite and friendly. Decor was cute enough, although there are tiny tables and snug seating. Really enjoyed my delicious cocktail! Lots of what I ate was very tasty but we had a very long wait for our food and the waiter, unfortunately, told me a meat dish was vegan so I accidentally ate beef. Flavours could have been even punchier and the meal was expensive for what it was. All in all I had a fun time but wouldn’t rush to return.

Thinking of the food makes me want to return for more. Each of the four dishes did not disappoint. Crackling spinach...how do they get the spinach so wonderfully crackling, light, and airy!?!? Popcorn cauliflower 😋 could be an all day everyday snack. The noodles with chicken added in was an amalgamation of spices with a tinge of heat was so very tasty.

Good, attentive service. Without reservations, we were seated at the bar, comfortable enough and had a view of staff who cooked the moms dishes. She was friendly. Mood lighting. Very busy with customers, testament to the food. Highly recommend.

venues.name: Yauatcha Soho
venues.description: Top-of-the-range, contemporary Chinese dining with expertly-crafted dim-sum and handmade sweets.

reviews.text: I came here with a friend on a Friday evening and we had a great experience. The food was really tasty and well prepared. The staff let us know in advance that some dishes might take a bit longer since it was busy, which we really appreciated. In the end, the waiting time was actually very reasonable. The service was friendly, the atmosphere was welcoming, and everything came out very good. We’ll definitely be coming back!

Food quality is very high and tasty. I love their pickles and chill sauce very much. They offer cold press juice as well. Table staff was very friendly and attentive. I am sure I will visit again with friends. Highly recommend.

The food was absolutely delicious. Pricey for sure, but the portion sizes were generous enough and the quality of the food was outstanding. The staff were very professional and the venue itself was modern and clean, overall really great vibes as well!

Great brunch here today, the staff welcomed us in and we were served baby cucumbers which were a great palate cleanser. We all enjoyed different tea’s from their menu, the Milk Oolong was my favourite. Highly recommended and will definitely be going back there soon!

Incredible. Excellent service, food and atmosphere. Everything we ordered was delicious and the staff were very friendly. Highly recommend the cheung fun and the mushroom spring rolls. We will 100% be returning. Perfect for a celebration or groups as well

venues.name: Gold Mine
venues.description: No frills Chinese restaurant for signature roast duck and Cantonese specialities from classic menu.

reviews.text: Serves authentic chinese cuisines including Malaysian styled curry.  I heard about the Malaysian fried fish curry which is not on the menu.  I loved it.  The fried meat tofu is average. Great service for a very popular and busy restaurant. Very attentive staff.  Highly recommended for good quality food and excellent service.

Authentic Chinese restaurant ✨ — it really feels like a proper yum cha spot with the round tables 🪑 and traditional décor 🏮

🔸Service:
The waitress was very welcoming 😊 and even arranged the best seat for us. As usual in Chinese dining, we started with hot tea 🍵 (you can choose your own — we went with chamomile 🌼 this time).

🔸Food:

🍜 Fried Beef Noodles 🍜 – My favorite! The black bean sauce 🫘 mixed perfectly with the beef 🥩 and noodles, with onion 🧅 and sweet peppers 🫑 balancing it out.

🍤 Crystal Prawn Dumplings (Har Gow) 🍤– 4 pieces, fresh and delicious 🦐.

🥟 Scallop & Prawn Siu Mai 🥟 – 4 pieces, juicy and flavorful.

🥬 Steamed Veg & Meat Dumplings 🥬 – 3 pieces, loved the crystal wrapper with the veggie mix inside.

🍲 Beef Cheong Fun (Rice Roll) 🍲 – Soft rice roll drizzled with soy sauce, very tasty.

🍡 Dessert: Black Sesame Glutinous Rice Balls 🍡 – Soft, slightly chewy, with rich sesame filling 🖤. (Fun fact: black sesame is great for hair & skin ✨).

🔸Overall: A truly authentic Chinese dining experience 🥢, not the usual localized “British-Chinese.” Food, service, and atmosphere were all spot on 🌟. Definitely coming back, and highly recommend it to anyone who wants the real deal ✅.

I had passed by Gold Mine many times and noticed there always seemed to be a queue of people waiting outside during the day.  I checked online and found they are popular for their dim sum but also their roast meat.  I decided to pay them a visit as I love duck and pork dishes.

My first impression was good as they were happy for me to make a reservation for one person and were very responsive to my requests.

I had a three-course meal of Deep Fried Crispy Aromatic Duck, Roast Meat Rice (BBQ Pork and Crispy Pork) and Banana Fritters.  I had also planned to have the House Special Bean Curd but had no room after my main course.

All the dishes I had were delicious.  The duck was probably the best I have ever had.  It was crispy on the outside and the meat was not at all dry but succulent.  I had no problem finishing all the pancakes.  I asked for egg fried rice and it was well cooked, along with the two types of pork.  The pork meats were full of flavour but not overpowering.  The banana fritters were a great end to the meal.  Crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside.

The service was also very good.  The servers were attentive but not at all intrusive and I did not have to wait very long at all between courses.

One thing to note is that the restaurant was rather noisy and not the best place for a quiet or intimate meal.  I was glad that I had my noise cancelling headphones with me.  I would also recommend making a reservation, as it was very busy.

I definitely recommend Gold Mine if you fancy having Chinese cuisine, especially their roast meat dishes.  I hope to make another visit soon to try their dim sum, as it looks very good.

Time after time, we have gone back to visit Chris and his team at Bayswater. Food's great, fast and very efficient in the service. Always good to go before lunch and dinner crowd. Thank you for the many years of great food.

Delicious traditional Chinese fare in a casual atmosphere.  Service was efficient and friendly.

I ordered the pork dumplings, chef recommended chili chicken special (served cold, see photo), and a side of egg fried rice.  Prices are steep for a Chinese restaurant, but I think this is typical in the UK.

I also ordered a dry martini, which tasted too sweet and as soon as I let the server know, she immediately took the item off the bill.

This place reminded me so much of a typical Cantonese style dim sum restaurant in New York Chinatown so there was a touch of sweet nostalgia for me.

All in all, I would come to this restaurant again and again!

venues.name: Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine
venues.description: From Beijing's finest to London's tables - authentic Chinese cuisine with modern flair. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Dined at this restaurant twice. First time was lunch dim sum which was amazing. Would easily say it's the best dim sum in London and that inspired me to go back for dinner, which was very good but not amazing.  Definitely recommend going there for dim sum.  Excellent service, something you would expect in a Michelin star restaurant. The atmosphere feels like a very luxury fine dining restaurant, very relaxed and calm but very attentive.
I've also had dim sum in their Guangzhou restaurant (Tianhui) and I would say the dim sum is better at London restaurant.

This is the best fine dining Chinese restaurant I've ever experienced. We tried the Peking duck, which we'd reserved in advance, accompanied by Burgundy red wine. The dumplings that came with it were also very good. I can't wait to come back.

We had the Imperial Treasure tasting menu and the food was exceptional! All of the dishes were outstanding! Our top three were the peking duck, black truffle lobster and the steak with garlic chips!
Our waiter Stephen was soo attentive and gave us some good tips on how to enhance our soup! We had such a wonderful time and we will be coming back

One of the best Chinese dining experiences in London! The signature Snow Mountain BBQ Pork Buns were absolutely outstanding – perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside, with rich, flavorful char siu. The Seafood Tofu Soup was also excellent, full of fresh ingredients and very comforting.
Special thanks to our waiter Johnny, who was incredibly attentive and friendly. His professional recommendations made the meal even more enjoyable. Definitely a place I’d love to revisit and highly recommend to anyone looking for authentic, high-quality Chinese cuisine!

The dining experience at Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine was amazing! Authentic Cantonese dishes, fresh ingredients, and refined presentation. The staff were attentive and polite. A must-try restaurant in London for anyone who loves high-quality Chinese food!

venues.name: Hutong
venues.description: Upscale spot with lanterns, silk curtains and city views, serving dim sum and northern Chinese fare.

reviews.text:
It was a last minute booking as my other half couldn’t decide where he wanted to have dinner but since we’ve been at Hutong before, it was an excellent go to for any occasion.
Maybe I’m just getting too old but my boyfriend and I wasn’t impressed with the volume and choice of music.
Food and service were otherwise excellent as always. Also, always leave room for dessert!
Many thanks for making my boyfriend’s birthday a special one!

Celebrated our anniversary dinner here and it was worth it, 5 star on all categories. We were well assisted by Alan who’s not just a great staff but also a very good photographer, very attentive to our needs and details on all his service, the foods was great especially the duck, all I can say is wow, all the foods we got was amazing & freshly cooked, and the dessert was excellent, the best mango dessert I had so far in the UK, really tasted like sweet mango from Asia. And we were surprised with the free dessert to greet us for our special day, and they were also able to accommodate our request regarding the seating arrangement. Thank you to all the staffs! Really enjoyed our dinner from start to finish 😁

From getting to the shard to reaching the restaurant upstairs every single member of staff were so friendly. When we got to the restaurant our table was ready despite us being 10-15 minutes early, we were taken to our table and we had booked the skyline experience so was seated next to the window with a great view. The meal we had was amazing and the portion sizes were very fair, not too small and not too much. The duck was the best thing as they bring it out and cut it in front of your table for you to see. We was here celebrating a birthday and the staff even prepared a little happy birthday treat for my partner which was ever so kind. Well worth the money and I would come back here for sure

Wonderful treat for my daughter’s birthday. Our server was excellent. There are probably better, less expensive places if you want Chinese food here in London, but we wanted to treat ourselves to The Shard! The two highlights were our server who was lovely and the King Of Dragon cocktail which was amazing! Thanks to all the staff there!

Service was amazing and cocktails were 10/10. Dessert was lovely and the birthday treat was a nice touch. However, it would have been helpful to know there’s a cut-off 30 minutes before your booking ends, which did take away from the experience. I also found a staff comment about ordering more food a bit unnecessary — if I want more, that’s my choice and what I’m paying for. The food was just okay, nothing special, and the view felt quite far away (would have been better by a window). Overall, some highlights but not sure it’s worth the money.

venues.name: House of Ming
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Serving 2 difference halve and refried pecking duck, it was dry and no favouring even the duck skin isn’t crispy. The waiter said they make their own pecking duck pancake, we received factory made pancake .

I can taste the Honey roast pork char siu was frozen and reheat by microwave, It was dry and chewy.

£75 for a Lobster tails laid in giant lobster shell with the almost 70% butter I could not taste any lobster meat at all.

For Dim sum we have scallop and prawn har gao, it might be handmade but it usually comes with big pieces of scallop i guess I got a newborn. Har gao should be at least few pieces, we got some in finely chop.

It was a treat from my friend so I have to be polite and not to complaint . For the same price we paying in central london you can get much better quality and services.

Fried rice with xo sauce was nice not greasy but xo sauce should have dry scallop and spiciness.

Noodles with mushroom is slightly salty but it is the most decent food of that meal.

The waiters aren’t seem to know what are they serving and the ingredients. Foods aren’t serve as what we being told.

I was with a group of friends for a special event so I have to be polite and nice on that day.

My husband and I were staying at the Taj and as it was or 45th wedding anniversary thought we would have a nice meal. We chose House of Ming as we had heard good things about it, on arrival we were greeted warmly and showed to a lovely booth with curtains. Staff were attentive and the food was really nice, especially as we were vegetarian for that period, it was Navratri and we don't go vegetarian for the nine days. My husband (who isn't vegetarian normally) was also very impressed and as he's also a very good chef it's a huge relief when he finds the food excellent. We were given complimentary cocktails and a beautiful dessert in honour of our anniversary. Thank you to B. Prasad and everyone who works for House of Ming for making our evening extra special.

The service was lovely, the manager and all staff members were really kind. Celebrated a birthday and they bought out a mini cake and sang which was incredibly sweet. The staff went above and beyond to ensure we were taken care of and the food was delicious. Would recommend others try.

We had a wonderful evening at The House of Ming! The food was absolutely delicious, and the customer service was truly exceptional—definitely a 10/10 experience!

A special thank you to Shah, who made our dinner even more memorable. You looked after us throughout the entire evening, and your attentive, professional, and warm service really stood out. Your hospitality was truly commendable!

We’ll definitely be coming back soon!

House of Ming at the Taj St James Court London delivered an absolutely exceptional lunch experience!
From the moment we stepped in, the ambiance was perfectly serene and elegant, creating a truly special atmosphere.
We started with the Golden Fried Prawn, which was crispy and bursting with flavour, followed by the perfectly seasoned Chicken Salt and Pepper, and the delicate Prawn Har Gao Dimsum. Each appetizer was a testament to the kitchen's mastery of Chinese cuisine.
For our mains, the Hakka Noodles were cooked to perfection, the Chilli Oyster Fish was rich and satisfying, and the Veg Fried Rice was a delightful accompaniment. The delectable flavours of each dish were truly memorable.
A special mention must go to Dexter, whose warm welcome and attentive service made our lunch even more enjoyable. His care and professionalism ensured we had a truly wonderful time. We can't wait to return to House of Ming for another incredible meal!

venues.name: Peacock London
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

address.formatted: County Hall, Westminster Bridge Rd, The Queen's Walk, London

venues.vicinity: County Hall, Westminster Bridge Rd, The Queen's Walk, London

reviews.text: We booked this Chinese restaurant for lunch which was located at the very prime tourist location.  Initially we thought it was a place mainly for tourists.  Upon arrival, we were led to a window table that had a great view of the Bog Ben.  They were having a summer special that a whole Peking Duck was at a reduced price from £118 to £68.  With no second thought, we ordered the duck right the way.  Along with the duck, we also ordered a few dim sum which were very nicely presented.  It's a pity they didn't cut up the duck in front of us.  Price wise, it was higher than those in Chinatown by 20-30% but it was still reasonable for this location.  Their wait staff were very friendly and helpful.  The two hours of dining went by quickly.  I  would love to try their abalone on my next visit.

Tasty dishes in pleasant atmosphere. Some of the tables have great view to Big Ben. Friendly and polite staff.
But; we were a group of 25 guests. The staff should take time to present the set menus and how to eat the dishes because not all the guests were familiar with Cantonese food. With such big group, they should have a lead staff to coordinate the tables. Pity!

Excellent authentic Chinese food, beautifully presented.   The location on the river opposite Westminster is great, from our table we looked out the window across the tanes and Westminster Bridge  and Big Ben and Parliament House. Price wise very reasonable, I have paid more for Pub Meals no where the quality of the food we ate here.Our favourite dish was the lamb with cumin.

Delicious Chinese with a breathtaking view!
Popped in while visiting London for the first time and I loved it. I would recommend booking to secure a spot with the view, I hadn’t but luckily there was a spot and the lovely staff let us sit in one.
The food was delicious, particularly loved the beef with black bean sauce.
I will definitely be coming back and recommending this place to anyone popping over to London.

Amazing views of the London Eye, Parliament, and the Thames made this dinner special from the start. The food was next-level — flavourful, beautifully presented, and far above your typical Chinese restaurant. Staff were friendly and professional throughout. A fantastic experience all around. Highly recommended!

venues.name: Fatt Pundit
venues.description: Compact restaurant offering Indo-Chinese cuisine & drinks amid an informal atmosphere.

reviews.text:
I went to Fatt Pundit after seeing so many great reviews and was looking forward to it. The food was tasty and the wine went really well. Service was friendly and helpful too.

For me though, the whole experience felt more average than amazing. The atmosphere was fine but nothing special, and the toilets really need updating – they let the place down.

Overall, I’d say it was good but not quite what I was expecting. I’d probably go again, but with lower expectations next time.

As a fan of asian fusion cuisine I was surprised by how exquisitely good every dish looked and tasted while at a fairly adequate price. The ambience was relaxing and both Geet and Alex were very attentive towards our needs for refills, checking if we were pleased with the food and although it was a busy Friday, service was as fast as it was of top quality. Highly recommend for everyone that loves asian food and wishes to try Kolkata cuisine.

Fantastic service by the staff - Raj and Rutul, friendly and answered any questions we had. It was my birthday and I was surprised with a lovely candle and decoration on my desert. Food was 10/10
Will definitely be visiting again and recommending to others!!

Didn’t realize that you should have reservations for this place? Our first night of 7 in London , my 1st time and hubby Google ‘ good places to eat near me’, luckily we only walked about 5 minute from our hotel…we came early for dinner at 1630 . Was quickly seated at a high top…for two…Nihal was informative directed us to many tasty “tapas” items, the Crispy spinach was yummy and quite different, the lamb chops to die for (for me the mint puree has a kick!) Hakka noodle also good .

Atmosphere only 4.5 as for me too chilly in here with the AC.

Amazing food and service! They have a lovely halal menu and the staff are great! The chicken Szechuan noodles were perfect, momos were cooked to perfection and the Bombay chilly prawns were to die for! Lollypop chicken was 10/10, well seasoned and spicy. Staff were amazing! Shout out to Nihal and Alex- they were just great!!  they even let us bedazzle their phones with stickers- great service of food and super lovely!

venues.name: Noble Palace
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Best dim sum we have had. We went for lunch and were well taken care of by the servers and host. We enjoyed the pumpkin dumplings, sea bass, taro croquettes, and steamed pork buns. The standout was their crispy prawns wrapped in noodles served with a light soy sauce. We even went back to order another, but with iberico pork.

The restaurant and vibe itself was a standout. Very comfortable and elegant. We came with our 2 year old and everyone was very welcoming and even brought him special shrimp chips which kept him occupied. Special thanks to the Hungarian manager who I didn’t catch his name. Us hungry parents were very much appreciative we could enjoy a fine dining meal with the kiddo.

We will be back again and highly recommend you make a visit!

My husband booked Noble Palace for my birthday and what an experience. I was craving dim sum (baby wants dim sum) and wow what an amazing selection we had. The staff were really attentive and friendly and the ambiance of the restaurant was beautiful. Will definitely come back once baby it out!

Last month I been in Noble Palace
These  two dish are new and good taste

Pan-Fried Wagyu Beef Dumplings
Tempura Soft Shell Crab with Hot & Sour Sichuan Sauce

The whole experience was great.

I had a fantastic dining experience today. Yuri and Kara, our servers, were friendly and attentive, ensuring we had everything we needed. They even asked about allergies, which was thoughtful. The food was delicious, and the beautifully presented dessert was the perfect finishing touch. Highly recommend for great food and excellent service!

P.S. The dessert is a special order, so I recommend ordering it in advance. Don’t miss out on their special dessert—highly recommended!

Went here for a baby shower and everything from the customer service, food, and ambiance was great. Can’t say much about the price because we were a big group so I paid fairly for what I got. They adjust for dietary restrictions, were constantly refilling water/sparking water based on your preference, and kindly handed bags for leftovers. One of the nicest baby showers I’ve been to! Thank you!

venues.name: The Sichuan Restaurant
venues.description: Standard destination offering Chinese set lunches and a la carte dining.

reviews.text: Nice Sichuan Restaurant in the city. They have good selection of regional Chinese dishes and they served the orders quite promptly.  I just wished that if the menu indicated 3  hot or spicy levels, the dish should be really in hot and spicy level the way Sichuan dishes have in China. Staff are all attentive and accommodating.  They have clean washrooms as well.

Overall the food is really good, using straight away and said down a straight away. Food came in good pace and it genuinely felt like you're in China. We ordered a range of food for two with sparkling water. My favourite was the roasted duck and the noodles.  We also ordered the cucumber salad which was a bit of disappointment. Authentic, good price and service.  Would go again
Decent spot for Sichuan between Old Street and Moorgate stations. We had crispy duck and soft shell crab starters, followed by dan dan noodles (nice and spicy) and crispy shredded beef.

We had a great experience at this Chinese restaurant! The food was fresh, flavorful, and well-prepared. Highlights of the meal included the dry-fried green beans, which were crispy and savory, and the stir-fried onions with pork, which had a delicious balance of sweetness and spice. The eggplant dish was rich and tender, soaking up the sauce beautifully. The fried rice was light yet satisfying, with a nice mix of chicken, ham, and vegetables. Portions were generous and the service was friendly. A solid spot for authentic Chinese food—we’ll definitely be back!
The food was super nice. Everyone service was very nice and friendly ( Ellie Cindy Backy Ruby and Head ) very nice team. Will come back for sure

venues.name: Min Jiang
venues.description: Swish, 10th-floor Chinese restaurant in a high-end hotel, with lofty views of Kensington Gardens.

address.formatted: 2, Royal Garden Hotel, 24 Kensington High St, London

venues.vicinity: 2, Royal Garden Hotel, 24 Kensington High St, London

reviews.text:
Excellent fine Chinese dining.

Wide range of very tastey Chinese food. They're moderately priced and the service from entry to exit to tops.

There are some superb canopy type views of the city at night, which makes for a charming view of the city.

I've eaten there several times in recent years and the service is consistent and Excellent.

Try out their duck specialty, you'll enjoy it.

‼️book your Peking duck ‼️ Wonderful view and the food was really great.  We would have appreciated if the fact that we needed to make a reservation for Peking duck was advertised when we booked.  But the dishes we ordered in lieu were beautiful executed nonetheless.  The staff were lovely also - will come back again still!

More than average food for fair price, great location with amazing view.
The duck was better than average you can get in europe, the execution of the chef not so much. Doesnt say hello, doesnt explain anything, rushes to the table and starts cutting, leaves a lot of meat behind, which is then used to make 6 tiny bites. I wished he would just let ne debone the duck myself, thats how poor the execution was.

Min Jiang is one of my go-to favourites in London. I’ve been many times with different friends, and everyone has always been impressed. The food consistently meets expectations, the Beijing duck is especially outstanding, perfectly crispy and carved at the table, the price definitely matches the quality.

The view overlooking Hyde Park is stunning, a reliable spot for a memorable meal every time.

So we came here for my birthday. Expressly for the Peking Duck. With the backdrop of Kensington Gardens (which was stunning and must be wonderful on a sunny day) and elegant surroundings. It’s v relaxed though for some reason our food took longer than expected for which the server apologised. I would rate food 4 stars. It’s expensive but it was all delicious and well flavoured accompanied by tasty and plentiful sauces. It’s fabulous having the succulent juicy duck carved in front of us and it was all very enjoyable. Could the skin been a tad crisper and flavourful - perhaps! But it was still delicious. I would say that the second serving (we chose fried rice) didn’t contain much duck at all and we didn’t get the leg. So that was a bit disappointing.  But again the fried rice was perfectly cooked.  It got quite busy for the lunchtime and that added to the atmosphere. I liked the little gift bag for Chinese NY which was a nice touch at the end.

venues.name: Nanyang Blossom - Knightsbridge
venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Tucked away from the usual busy London spots, this restaurant is the kind of place you stumble on once and never forget. It doesn’t try too hard to impress from the outside, but the moment you step in, you realize you’re in for something special.

What struck me most wasn’t just the food—it was the way the whole evening unfolded. The team here treats you like more than a customer. Stella greeted us with genuine warmth, Jeanie guided us through the menu with ease, and even the chef came by to personally recommend dishes. That kind of care is rare, and it set the stage for what turned out to be an extraordinary meal.

The food? Absolutely outstanding. Every plate felt alive with flavor and balance, from the starters—like nutmeg prawns and chicken satay—to the mains, where the rendang and crispy ribs stole the show. The rendang especially was a revelation: deep, rich, and melt-in-your-mouth tender. Even the sides, simple noodles and vermicelli, carried the same attention to detail. It’s the kind of cooking that makes you stop mid-bite just to appreciate what’s happening on the plate.

By the time we finished, it didn’t feel like we had just eaten dinner—it felt like we had been hosted. Stella came back to chat with us at the end, and it felt less like a formal check-in and more like closing the night with a friend.

This place is more than a restaurant—it’s an experience. Refined yet unpretentious, welcoming yet polished. Easily one of the best meals I’ve had in London, and one I’ll be telling people about for a long time.

Sometimes the best experiences come from chance, and this restaurant was exactly that. We had been looking for an Asian spot outside of the usual, over-visited choices in London and were drawn here by its high ratings, even though only a few people had reviewed it. Initially hesitant, we decided to give it a try—and it turned into one of the most unforgettable dining experiences I’ve had.

From the moment we walked in, the hospitality stood out. We were warmly greeted by Stella, the host, who guided us to our table downstairs. Soon after, our server Jeanie introduced us to the menu and provided a tablet with photos of all the dishes, which made choosing much easier. As we browsed, the head chef personally came to our table, welcomed us, and even helped us select some of their standout dishes. His warmth and genuine interest in ensuring we had the best experience set the tone for the night, and our chat with him made the evening feel personal and memorable.

The food itself was exceptional—truly beyond words. Every dish, from starters to mains to sides, carried bold, balanced, and deeply satisfying flavors. For starters, we had the Yin Yang nutmeg prawns, chicken rolls, grilled chicken satay, and pan-fried chicken and vegetable dumplings. Each offered a unique blend of flavors and textures, and all were outstanding. For mains, we chose the smoky beef rib rendang and the crispy beef ribs—both phenomenal, but the rendang in particular was remarkable, with beef so tender it was unlike anything I’ve had before. We also ordered the black pepper Angus beef and the red honey chicken, both rich and flavorful. Sides included egg noodles and vermicelli, each complementing the dishes beautifully. Every single item we tried was executed perfectly and left a lasting impression.

To end the evening, Stella returned to check on us, genuinely interested in our experience and eager to hear our thoughts. The conversation felt warm and sincere, more like speaking with a friend than a typical host–guest exchange. It was the perfect conclusion to an already incredible night.

Everything about this restaurant—its food, service, and hospitality—was flawless. It is without question a 10/10 and, in my view, the best Asian restaurant in London. A true hidden gem that deserves far more recognition

Great service, amazing food, we didn’t make any reservations and they still gave us a table. It was mine and my girlfriends anniversary, they gave us a very delicious dessert for free as it was our anniversary. The staff were very kind and very 宾至如归. Thank you for having us we will be coming back for sure !!!

My mom and I walked in without a reservation on a Friday and luckily got a table. Service was outstanding. The food, wow. We got the garlic okra, fried rice, beef ribs, and lettuce wraps. Everything was 10/10. I wish we had room for desert.

I've been twice now and this is the best place for Malaysian food I have tried in the UK. Service is so friendly too, and a peaceful atmosphere to saviour the food. Looking forward to trying the rest of the menu, it might take some time!

Every dish I have tried so far has been great, with a lot of care invested into both the taste and the presentation. I've had char kway teow, Hainanese chicken rice, wagyu beef rice, chicken satay, chicken & vegetable dumplings, and kuih dessert. The chicken rice is especially great as it is difficult to get right outside Malaysia.

Carry on the good work and I will see you again soon!

venues.name: Ma La Sichuan
venues.description: Sleek restaurant serving Chinese Sichuan cuisine, along with dim sum.

reviews.text: What a lovely vibrant atmosphere, authentic Chinese food and really good portions of food! I did not expect to find a place like this at all behind the huzz and buzz of Big Ben and Westminster areas!  We were sight seeing with our friends from Canada and Belgium and we stumbled upon this restaurant, with 8 of us walk in and no reservations on a lunchtime and was quite busy but we’re still accomodated despite  the circumstances that we had. The location was only a few meters away from Westminster abbey which someone would thought this place did not exist . The food was served quick and fast and simply irresistible flavours . The service was simply handled by Judy , genuinely attentive, respectful and friendly. Food prices I thought was expensive which I thought it’s London price but I was proven wrong as the portions were actually for 2-3 people eating and I was gobsmocked to see the quality and quantity of it! It was indeed a very good value of our money !  Definitely will be back here if we are in London and it was truly an amazing experience! Highly recommended.

The restaurant is lively and always decently full which is a great sign. The service is efficient and friendly, and the waiters are all very attentive with regards to drinks. I will say that the food is rather good, the fried noodles, squid, and soft shell crab all recommended. Will be back soon!

Loved this asian restaurant, we ate all sorts of plates (all to share, group of 7) and they were all quite yummy. We walked in without a reservation and they treated us very politely, sat us down immediately. The food was great, our favorite was the fried rice and the sweet and sour chicken.

Definitely will be returning soon!

Excellent service!! as somebody who has worked in the hospitality industry almost my whole working career, I can tell they take pride in their customer service and attentiveness at this restaurant.

Food was delicious as well! My friend and I got the sim sung platter, prawn Singapore noodles, a bottle of wine, and duck spring rolls. We both agreed we’d definitely coming back soon, we loved everything.

And again, I don’t think I’ve ever had such attentive staff! They didn’t let us lift a finger… Even on such a busy evening, they were completely full!

Thank you for a lovely evening🫶🏽
Really nice food. We love that we can adjust spicy level according to ability. Really friendly staff. The fish tasted fresh and sooo soft and fluffy. The chicken was very nice too.

venues.name: Shan Shui Social
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
I found this restaurant when searching for restaurants that are good for big groups. We were celebrating my dad’s 70th. When we went we learnt that it was newly opened, a few months old. We got a table downstairs and were the only ones there. Perfect.

The server was friendly and helpful. She recommended dishes to us and the food came quickly. Portion sizes are small which would have been perfect for sharing in smaller groups. (I say that because we usually dine with 3-4 people and some dishes are so large that trying food is difficult because of the large amount.) This time there were 12 of us so we just doubled up. Everything was delicious! I didn’t manage to photo everything because the children were hungry. The roast duck was so good. This is definitely kid-friendly food.

I really hope this restaurant stays. It’s a great addition to the neighborhood.

Incredible experience. One of the best meals I had in London! I cannot recommend this restaurant more.

Wonderful lunch selections and very helpful staff with questions and suggestions.

The pepper salted squid reminded me of my favorite childhood spot in Portland, Oregon. Brought back many good memories.

Every dish was flavorful and bright. I missed a couple dishes in photos because I couldn’t wait!!

Can’t wait to be back and visit again!

The serving speed is impressively fast—if you eat slowly, you might almost feel disrespectful to the food. Overall, this is one of the best Cantonese meals I’ve had in London recently.

💡 Drinks

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lion Eye: A lychee & longan mocktail, refreshing and lightly sweet without being overwhelming.

⭐⭐⭐ Elderflower Zest: Tastes like elderflower soda, non-alcoholic but with a hint of “boozy” character.

🍴 Dishes

⭐⭐⭐⭐ ¼ Roast Duck: Distinct from Beijing or Nanjing styles—Hong Kong–style roast with rich, slightly sweet soy-based flavor. Would be perfect with a plum sauce.

⭐⭐⭐ Salt & Pepper Squid: Tasty, but too much batter; the crunch overpowered the squid itself.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Salted Egg Yolk Prawns: Bold, savory flavor with plump prawns. Not too heavy—perfect for those who love salted egg dishes.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Chongqing Chili Chicken: More numbing (málà) than spicy, dry-fried style, very suitable for Cantonese palates while still keeping Sichuan flavor.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Fried Wontons: Absolute favorite. Thin, crispy skin with big, juicy shrimp inside. Paired with a sweet-spicy sauce—unmissable.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Custard Lava Buns: Sadly, the filling wasn’t runny since we didn’t eat them immediately, but still tasty with a more savory salted egg yolk filling (not the sweet custard type).

⭐⭐⭐ “Mouthwatering Chicken”: Decent, but not the highlight compared to other dishes. Still solid, but overshadowed.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Braised Wheat Gluten: First time having this in the UK—closer to frozen tofu in texture, pleasantly flavorful.

Absolutely loved my meal here! This Shanghai restaurant offers authentic flavors with a modern twist. The braised pork belly was melt-in-your-mouth delicious, and the drunken chicken was perfectly seasoned. The service was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy yet stylish. A great place whether you're a fan of classic Shanghainese dishes or trying them for the first time. Highly recommend!

Shan Shui is really a solid place - good variety with Veggie options and well made in its approach to an authentic but also causal dining experience. We ordered quite a bit between three people but the prices weren’t anything you wouldn’t expect from a central London restaurant. Top favourites were the Kafou (pardon my spelling) a very unique but delicious dish, prawn wontons, braised mushroom and tofu with rice, char siu and roast duck. It was very delicious only minor notes the noodles in the char siu and prawn wontons dish weren’t the easiest to eat even for the most vetted chop stick user and the sauce was a bit salty I think that would’ve been a better choice in a soup form instead of dry. Also the chilli crab Bao was actually very tasty but …. Where was the crab a mere thought apparently cause there wasnt much in the Bao, luckily whatever filling they did have was still very tasty. I would defo visit again just maybe with more soup options !!

venues.name: A. Wong
venues.description: Upmarket Chinese eatery for dim sum & a 10-course "Taste of China" menu showcasing regional cuisine.

reviews.text: Absolutely fantastic tasting menu. The course menu takes up to three hours to finish, so make sure you come hungry. The staff were lovely and the service was superb. At the very end, they even give you a little postcard to write and send home.

A. Wong’s 36-course tasting menu is truly something special. It’s a journey through China via flavour and texture.
Some dishes felt comforting and familiar, others completely unexpected, but all of them told a story. The balance between fun and finesse is spot on.

Service was warm and knowledgeable, and the wine pairings brought even more depth to the experience.

Great vibes too, Chef Andrew is talented, humble and geniune.

A great dining experience ☺️
Would love to try their dim sum lunch menu next time !

Came here for my partner’s 30th and it is an absolute foodie dream come true! This place blew us away from start to finish.

First off, yes: it’s a two-Michelin-starred restaurant, and deservedly so — but the service isn’t stiff or distant. The team are warm, super friendly, and genuinely passionate about what they do. They’re detailed, attentive, and make you feel as though you’ve known them forever.

I am Chinese and my partner adores Chinese food. We’ve visited other Michelin-starred Chinese places before — but nothing compared to this. A. Wong delivers truly authentic regional Chinese cuisine, each dish capturing the soul of the province it represents, with that signature creative twist that only A wong can achieve. It’s like being transported to the heart of each region, but with modern flair.

We left the dinner talking about it non-stop. Every conversation with friends or family eventually circles back to that unforgettable culinary journey. The food was just exceptional!

We’ll absolutely be back very soon!!
Excellent tasting menu, uniquely Chinese. Beats some of the best fine dining meals I’ve had in Beijing and Shenzhen. Really enjoyed the wine pairing as well.

Occasional flashes of brilliance, but plenty of room for improvement.

With two Michelin stars and a menu built around dim sum and Cantonese-inspired dishes, it’s hard not to draw comparisons to other modern high-end dim sum restaurants. Chef Wong clearly wants to showcase creativity and reinterpret classics. When it works, it really works; when it doesn’t, execution falters and leaves diners familiar with Cantonese cuisine confused or disappointed.

HIGHLIGHTS

帶子腸粉 — seared scallops and honey-glazed Iberico pork cheung fan

粵式蜜汁叉燒臘腸配鵝肝 — Cantonese honey roast pork, wind-dried sausage with grated foie gras

酥皮鮑魚撻 — flaky abalone tart with aged balsamic vinegar

These dishes show imagination, balance, and refinement. The modern twists enhance rather than distract.

WEAKNESSES

Deep-fried items such as 周朝釀蟹鉗 (crab claw with tomato and wasabi) and 千煸茄子 (crispy chilli aubergine with star anise glaze) arrive either bitter or oily, likely from reused oil or poor temperature control.

Small, delicate bites often suffer from poor proportions: the wrapper overwhelms the filling, resulting in chew without flavour. This issue appears in 兔肉鹹水角 (rabbit and carrot glutinous puff), 千層帶子酥 (999 layered scallop puff with XO oil), and even the otherwise solid 上海小籠包 (Shanghai steamed dumpling, ginger infused vinegar). The xiao long bao also loses intensity by having vinegar pre-infused into the broth, reducing its flavour impact.

SERVICE
Service is proper and polite, but distant. Many other two-starred restaurants deliver a warmer, more personal experience that places the guest at the centre. To their credit, staff did ask what we particularly liked or disliked. However, when we voiced criticism, the only response was a polite “thanks for letting us know,” with no further engagement.

CONCLUSION
Not the perfect lunch we were hoping for. A. Wong could serve as a gateway for those new to Chinese cuisine, but execution issues need addressing before it can truly live up to its two-star billing.

venues.name: Golden Dragon (Chinatown)
venues.description: Spacious restaurant set over 2 floors serving Cantonese and Pekinese cuisine with dim sum lunches.

reviews.text:
Golden Dragon is everything you want from a Chinatown restaurant. Fast, attentive service, great food, and a buzzing atmosphere. From the moment we walked in, the table we had booked was ready for us straight away, and despite the restaurant being fast-paced and busy, we never once felt rushed. There were so many staff on hand that we never had to wait for anything—credit to the team for running such a slick operation.

We ordered the Oriental Set Menu, and the restaurant was more than happy to accommodate a swap from beef to chicken for one of our party, which meant everyone could enjoy the full menu together. A thoughtful touch that really stood out, and one they were within their right to not need to accommodate.

The meal began with a comforting chicken and corn soup, before the array of mains arrived. The standout for me was the Sweet and Sour Pork which was perfectly balanced, crispy, and packed with flavour. My friends raved about the Stir-Fried Diced Chicken with Cashew Nuts and the Spicy Szechuan Prawns, both cooked to perfection. The duck dish was also excellent, rich and tender, and rounded off the meal beautifully.

Overall, Golden Dragon delivered a brilliant Chinatown dining experience being efficient yet friendly service, excellent food across the board, and a lively atmosphere. Highly recommended, and I’ll definitely be returning.

A faultless dining experience today...came here on a Thursday as part of a trip. We regularly dine in Chinatown but so far hadn't experienced this restaurant. Filled with lots of Chinese (always a good sign..no offence meant) . We ordered a large array of dim sum and 2 a la carte dishes. Food arrived super quick and was really good one of my favourite char su pork I have ever eaten. Staff were friendly attentive and helpful. Definitely recommend this venue for both seasoned and novice dim sum eaters.

Golden Dragon in Chinatown is a lively spot known for its authentic Cantonese and dim sum offerings. The average main course is reasonably priced, usually around £12–£18, making it good value for both casual meals and special outings. Drinks are varied, with a mix of traditional teas, soft drinks, and a decent selection of wines and beers to pair with your meal. The atmosphere is bustling, especially at peak times, and the staff keep things running smoothly despite the crowds.

The food stands out for its freshness, with dishes arriving hot and well-prepared, especially the seafood and dumplings which are customer favourites. Golden Dragon also caters for accessibility, offering disabled facilities that make it easier for all guests to enjoy their dining experience.

I love my Chinese foods , and Golden Dragon didnt disappoint ..

Stopped in after the theater for something to eat. Large menu offering a great variety of food was good, not great. Was clear the staff wanted to go home even though there was still quite a crowd inside eating.

Authentic Cantonese cuisine in quite large portions. We had fish & tofu stew and shredded duck vermicelli soup, both were tasty and comforting
Edit: we came back for dim sum, and everything was wonderful. The egg pudding is a must try!

venues.name: Speedboat Bar
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Oh my word. My husband and I came here with high expectations for our anniversary. Firstly, a sincere shoutout to the friendly and highly attentive waitstaff. We reserved in advance (which I recommend doing as it gets busy!) and they had actually read my booking notes. In the notes I mentioned I was pregnant and so they double checked I was happy with the preparation and ingredients of certain dishes. The menu leans towards the spicy and salty side, but at the same time is very fragrant and aromatic. Quite addictive really! I’ve seen viral videos of that Tom Yam deluxe noodle dish so obviously we had to get it. It was delicious, but to my surprise, my favourite dish was their Naem fried rice. It’s been about a week since our visit and I’m still licking my lips thinking about it. To top everything off, we got a surprise scoop of taro ice cream. How adorable is that? Lots of love to Speedboat. We’ll be back, and definitely before our next anniversary!

hyped up place for sure and while the interior lives up to the hype and certainly some of the dishes do they are unfortunately inconsistent and I don’t think pay attention to detail… possibly because it gets so busy. Don’t get me wrong it was nice and tasty but just a little inconsistent and not insane value. The rice was overcooked and actually clumped together which I wouldn’t expect from a Thai restaurant- especially when paying £4 extra.. the purple aubergines were really nice, tender and flavourful. However for £12.50 I got one long purple aubergine- eight pieces. Would’ve said id happily pay £9, as it wasn’t mind blowing but very very nice. Would’ve been nicer with better rice. Good spice level, even though we received warning it was actually perfect. Channah got crispy egg noodles with gravy pork and squid and was pleasantly surprised with two different types of squid and she said good value for the amount of squid, as she’d expect more pork and less squid but it was the other way round. The spice also could’ve been higher and she wanted more greens in the mix and garnish. She really enjoyed though and felt it was good value for central London £17. Staff are possibly a bit overworked and overwhelmed but they are all so lovely. Happy to have come but wouldn’t rush to come back.

Food and drinks were great!! I am obsessed with Tom yum mama noodles and regularly have the instant version at home so this boujee version was fantastic!! The fried rice was very flavoursome and even better with the sauces! Pour the beef tongue curry sauce on it and it’s even better! The pineapple pie was a nice way to end the meal

I have lived in London for 6 years and tried all kinds of good or bad restaurants. However, this is the first time I have written a review for a restaurant. First of all, I would like to thank the patient waiters and their drinks are good. However, what puzzles me is that the pricing of your restaurant's dishes is like a joke with customers. Your specialty dish "yum pot" is priced at 29 pounds. In fact, it is pitifully small and the contents are only some fried pork and convenience-based bargains, and a bowl of small rice costs 4 pounds. In addition, as for your taste, as an Asian, I can responsibly tell other consumers that the taste level of your food has only reached the middle and lower reaches. Then, your dining environment focusses on the style of "market flavour” and " street food", so your dining environment is actually pitiful. Finally, in short, you don't have the dining environment and service experience of a high-class restaurant, and you don't make the food delicious. Overall, you have only achieved the level of 8 pounds per person. I don't understand why you have such a high Google rating.

I was a little bit underwhelmed with this place - huge potential with such a unique and cool vibe to the place. The only thing is it gets so crowded even the staff seem stressed with the hot plates darting around people. I wouldnt come back on a Thursday-Saturday night. Because it was so crowded I think the staff felt overwhelmed.

If it wasnt crowded I wouldve had a better experience for sure as the food was pretty good and the vibe was cool! Definitely recommend the noodles but sizzling seafood was average!

venues.name: Platapian Soho
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: 1st time to this Branch of Restaurant located in Greek Street. Came with friends for a get-together. Bowled over by the variety of dishes; perfect balance of seasoning delivering tantalising taste and all beautifully presented! Special mention for their unique Scallops starter! Loved their fantastic Cocktails, too! Do not hesitate to come try for yourselves! ThankYou too to Paul for his friendly and attentive service throughout the evening! Ps. Will be coming back but please fix the draughty front door!

What a wonderful place! Very zen and elegant place with lots of details! Food is incredible good! The scallop, papaya salad, and the clay pot rice are all amazing. Very fresh! You can really taste the food! Ploy is also helpful and super patient with us!! Definitely recommended!!!

Last night we had one of the most delicious meals we’ve ever had—not just in a Thai restaurant, but in any restaurant. The flavors were rich and authentic, the portions were generous, and the quality of the produce was outstanding.
Perfect for a romantic date night or a special celebration. We’ll definitely be back!

Platapian Soho in London is an exceptional spot. Most of the dishes are absolutely delicious, though a few can be a little on the salty side. The wine selection is excellent and really elevates the experience.

The service is decent, though understandably a bit stretched as the restaurant is always busy and buzzing with energy. Overall, the food stands out and I truly enjoyed my visit. Definitely worth recommending.
Highly recommended!! The BEST Thai food in London said by Thai people😆, good vibes, good services & good cocktails. The dessert was amazing.

venues.name: Kolae
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
I really enjoyed my visit over the weekend. I was very keen to try Kolae as it had been recommended by a friend and on the whole I was not disappointed.

We didn’t order a lot of the food on this occasion so I’d definitely like to go back and try some other dishes what we did have was incredibly flavourful and in some instances, very spicy,  the pepper chicken made me lose my voice. It was so spicy but so delicious. Luckily, our server recommended a cooling drink to soothe my throat.

I really liked the building and the place had a really nice vibe, although as is often the case, the toilets were a bit messy.

We were on the top floor and I don’t think there was a lift. I think we went up three flights of stairs to a smaller, lovely space, so do you bear that in mind when booking.

We felt rushed at the end but we did have a two hour booking limit. Another 15 mins would have been good.

Stand out was the kale, surprisingly, and the pork.

Recommended.

One of the best meals we've ever eaten. The lunchtime set menu is a brilliant deal, the prawns, butternut squash, fish curry and rice pudding dessert are all total world class.The guy from Alsace who looked after us was brilliant, friendly  helpful and kind. He did a brilliant job.One of the worlds best restaurants in my book, it was amazing, thanks for a lovely and memorable afternoon Kolae.

We had reservations for this very popular place near borough market. We ordered two curries and one salad for our meal. We ordered a wine and a beer. The prawn curry was super spicy which is fine as I like spicy but the curry was too thin and it was okay. We ordered a fish curry which was very good. The mango and cucumber salad was very good and so was the coconut sorbet. It was a good refreshing finish after the meal.

Utterly exceptional! Genuine Thai food, should come with a warning for how good it is! I had the set menu which had a fantastic mix of the general menu. Great drinks selection, especially curated to complement the food. Lovely atmosphere, super helpful staff. I would eat here ever day if I could. My new favourite place for sure!

Really great meal at Kolae today. Real punchy Thai flavours, all fresh and very well presented. Mussel skewer, crispy kale fritters and stone bass curry our favourites but everything was really good. service was also very good and helpful. Would definitely recommend

venues.name: Nua
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
A relatively new and nice modern Thai option in the area. The staff are really lovely from the moment you arrive and remain attentive throughout. The main menu is large and varied with photos to help aid any selection, but there’s also a reasonably priced lunch menu, offering either one or two courses from a concise range of options. From this menu, both the staters and main are served together on a single plate, presented well, and although not a massive portion is good for a lunch.

The pork skewers were delicious and a shame they only serve two, and the green curry was very tasty with a nice level of spice. The draught beer was a little slow to arrive but served ice cold which was great.

The decor and background music doesn’t give the most traditional or authentic atmosphere but fortunately everywhere is clean. I’ll certainly be returning and would recommend for a more unique independent offering.

Our group of four had a fantastic experience at Nua, enjoying a night of excellent Thai food. We started with the Nua Platter, which included Duck Spring Rolls, Chicken Satay, Steamed Thai Dim Sum, and Chargrilled Pork Skewers. A major positive is that they provide one of each item per person, avoiding the awkwardness of splitting dishes, something many other places don't get right. The accompanying sauces (satay, chilli and a hoisin-like sauce) were also spot on, adding extra depth to the starters.

For mains, we ordered a variety including the Pad Kra-Pao and Massaman Curry. Every dish was full of flavour: the pork was rich and juicy, the chicken was perfectly tender, and the boned-meat easily pulling away from the bone. The Sticky Rice and Jasmine Rice we had alongside complemented the mains beautifully.

Service throughout the meal was polite and courteous, though we did find it difficult to get attention when asking for the bill, waiting around 10 minutes.

Pricing is slightly on the higher end, but given the central London location and quality of the food, it felt reasonable enough.

Overall, Nua delivers delicious Thai food in a relaxed setting. A great choice for a treat or a special night out!

Overall the place was good. The food was tasty but not exceptional. The starters were tasty - the skewers, the tempura shrimp and the spring rolls were all good. The grilled chicken was fine but the portion size was small and the salad was not to my taste. Overall I’d love a rich sauce there instead of just a hot one. The service was extremely slow and it took them a lot of time to cook our order. What stands out is the wide selection on the menu.

We wanted to try this Thai restaurant and were not disappointed. We booked in advance as the space inside was limited. The food was great in flavour and portions. Service was slightly slow but the staff was super friendly and helpful. Toilets are on the lower ground floor with stairs.

Came for dinner to a quaint Thai spot in Fitzrovia.
It was a great evening, the restaurant was not too packed and they brought food efficiently. We ordered two Pad See Ews,
one with tofu and one with crispy chicken, and they were both delicious and quite flavoursome despite looking quite pale.
The highlight however were the duck spring roles, they were perfectly cooked, crispy and flavoursome, and not too oily.
Nice spot

venues.name: AngloThai
venues.description: Thai cuisine that's as vibrant as Bangkok itself - bold, beautiful, and delicious. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: They did something truly great with this restaurant. Incredibly gorgeous, delicious and balanced food. It’s definitively British food with Thai influence, not vice versa - very original and creative. Don’t think there was a bad dish here, I’d definitely recommend to NOT skip the supplement as that was one of the best bites. The curry as well as the oysters and sausage starter were additional standouts. I was literally cleaning off the plate with their homemade brioche. Even the cucumber broth amuse bouche was delectable. Only two dishes that didn’t wow me were the Thai tea dessert and the side of greens that was very very salty. Other than that this restaurant is exactly the type of cooking I’d love to see more of in London. Unfussy interior and service, very friendly and felt cozy but not rugged. Will definitely be returning!

This was one of the best tastings I have done in London. And at a very competitive price point. A couple highlights were the crab and caviar course and the bbq octopus. It may have been the best octopus I have ever had. The Thai spices were unique and fantastic across all the courses. They also had excellent ice cream in both of the dessert courses. The ambiance could be a bit more elevated, as it was quite tightly packed but the food makes it more than worth the visit!

Took my wife for her birthday dinner and we really enjoyed our meal. Every dish had a unique Asian spin that was flavorful and delicious.
