It was also lovely to find out we had extra courses but those should be a surprise (although the bread may have been the best bread course I’ve ever had). Would recommend without reservation.

Unique dining experience in a basement in Soho. The chefs and staff are friendly and the food is full of complicated favours and layers.  We did not order the drink package and order glasses / bottles from the menu direct is an alternative option.

It’s truly a miracle for 3 capable chefs to deliver so much in a small kitchen set up . It’s perhaps one of the best if not the best ways Michelin starred restaurants in London I dined in so far. The chefs told us that they change menu from time to time and I will visit again

Absolutely phenomenal! Wonderful staff, very professional kitchen. Very cosy atmosphere. They have set up the space well. Great to see the plating up with such precision and artistry. Every mouth full of food and sip of a drink was delicious leaving me wanting more!

venues.name: Kitchen Table
venues.description: 19-seat U-shaped table around a cooking station, with a multi-course menu of small European dishes.

reviews.text:
My 4th visit and for the first time I went for pescatarian menu, honestly I was disappointed. While my fellow diners were enjoying the normal menu, I felt like a vegetarian. I was expecting the kitchen to replace the beef and duck with seafoods instead of pure vegetables. I wouldn’t have gone for the menu if I knew that was the case, huge anticipation ended in disappointment. I was later advised and the veggie replacements were advertised but wasn’t obvious to me, maybe they shouldn’t call this a pescatarian menu.

More seriously, I don’t know how a professional kitchen really functions, but seeing chefs putting spoons in their mouth for tasting, then put it to a communal pot, nothing wrong with that.  But, then other utensils were taken from the same pot to stir the dishes before plating?! I was quite shocked/disgusted to see that, raised to the waiters but was told the chefs didn’t put the spoon in their mouth. By then I observed two incidents! A small discussion was going on in the kitchen then the communal pot was removed in front of me to the other end of the kitchen. It didn’t address the problem at all, did it? If it wasn’t for my friend’s celebration, I would simply walk out. I don’t know how 2 stars were granted if hygiene was one big factor.

Though some of the dishes had interesting flavours, but the hygiene experience totally ruined my evening.

Amazing experience! It's a great set up for fine dining, the social aspect and connection with the chefs, service and other dinners is great. The food was beautiful, different and delicious. This is the 4th tasting menu I've tried, Wales, Houston, Tasmania and now Kitchen Table and they all bring something new, interesting, varied, exciting and again delicious.

Sensational service thanks mainly to Daniel and Alex.

Expected a lot, food really missed the mark. For a two star level especially.
Oyster w granita nice opener, but playing it v safe.
Crab pleasant but not memorable and lacked texture.
Tomato - absolutely top notch 2 star dish. Has everything. That’s where the meal peaked for me.
Scallop caviar supplement dish, again leveraging amazing ingredients, was good but not memorable. AbiT one note the way cucumber notes interact with the scallop.

Trout - one slice of trout sashimi size was completely tasteless as was the hollandaise. Really really missed the mark. Whole dish lacked flavour and texture.

Bread course which was a brioche was totally average, sub par for 2* imo. Especially when a chain in London like Aux Merveilleux de Fred casually sells a way better one.

The curry like noodles dish that followed has tons of interesting flavour, but that’s all it was - it felt like scraping the bottom of a curry plate with some interesting candied notes. The noodles themselves were a mushy and lacked any taste.

The agnolotti with goats curd and onion consommé. Were pleasant, safe flavour combo seen it done many places - also imo the onion doesn’t really match the rest of the dish.

“Main” slice of pork with tiny sauce portions on side. Pork lacked any flavour, dish lacked texture.

The tiniest quantity of food for a main course I had anywhere in recent memory.

Both deserts were super solid. Fig - memorable and perfectly balanced.
The lemon cake - texture wise was spot on, flavour wise ok but unmemorable.

Petty fours super solid.

I’m a very experienced diner would say whole experience taking 4 hours is unduly taking up diners time. I’d wait 20min for plates if they were absolutely knocking it out of the park flavour wise however on this occasion most of them were ordinary and nothing more.

As an experienced diner at multi star places have to comment on quantity of food. It’s inexcusably too little, we had the 10 course menu. Left hungry.

Daniel gave us 11 star service on a 10 star scale and made our night memorable.

Maybe caught the resto on a night off but have to say whole menu feels like quickly put together lacking the depth of concept typically expected of the high standards and reputation set by Kitchen Table itself in the London dining scene. Happy to reconsider on another visit.

Where to begin! This is hands down our favourite restaurant in all of London, and we love Michelin-starred spots and would like to think of ourselves as proper foodies. The attention to detail from the moment you step inside is just incredible. You’re greeted by none other than Sandia Chang herself, and welcomed into the bar area with a lovely drink and some amuse-bouche to start the experience. It already feels special by then.

You get the chance to chat with some of the team, get a glimpse of the menu, and start soaking in the atmosphere. I love that they’ve recently tweaked their offering a bit. There’s now a shorter and a longer menu, which is great as it opens the door for more people to try it, even if they’re not going for the full tasting experience.

After around 20 to 30 minutes, you’re moved into the main dining area, the kitchen itself, surrounded by a counter table where the real magic happens. It’s like watching a symphony of chefs, all working together to serve you the most memorable dinner. You get to interact with them if you feel like it. They're incredibly warm, happy to chat and answer your questions, but also never pushy. It’s really up to you how involved you want to be, which I really appreciate.

Seeing James Knappett in action alongside his brilliant team is amazing. The level of passion for food and hospitality is so obvious, it’s infectious. Both times we’ve been, our favourite dish has been the lobster, but honestly, there are so many wonderful surprises along the way. The wine pairings are fantastic, perfectly chosen by Sandia, and we even ended with a beautifully paired cider, which was such a delightful surprise.

We’ve had dinner here twice now, in different seasons and years, and we still can’t stop thinking about it. Just an unforgettable place. Thank you so, so much to the whole team, we’re definitely coming back!

PS: I had to pick a few photos as I had too many and don't want to ruin the surprise.

Unbelievable food & service. The staff were incredible, kudos to Alex, the 3 Sam’s & Daniel especially! Food was exceptional, meticulously prepared and presented, and the passion was infectious from the staff and Chefs. We had 14 courses and each one was unique and memorable.
Highly recommend if you fancy the ultimate fine dining experience!

venues.name: Restaurant Story
venues.description: Chef Tom Sellers' novel approach to British classics. Choose from 6 or 10-course set menus.

reviews.text: Restaurant Story offers a beautifully curated fine dining experience with exceptional service from start to finish. The staff are warm, attentive and highly knowledgeable, making every guest feel welcome and well cared for. One of the standout touches is the bespoke printed menu tailored to your name and date, which adds a deeply personal element to the meal. The presentation is elegant, the storytelling thoughtful, and the atmosphere quietly luxurious without being stiff. A truly memorable evening. Pop to the terrace after lunch or dinner, a bustling vantage point. I’ll be back!

I had the privilege of working here nine years ago, and it’s remarkable to see how the dishes have evolved – even more refined, precise, and full of character. The storytelling woven into the meal and the way each course is guided and orchestrated make it an unforgettable experience. Flavours are masterfully balanced, the presentation is art, and the attention to detail is second to none. Next time we are in England, we will most certainly return – this place continues to set the standard for what a Michelin-starred restaurant should be.

We celebrated a birthday here. The cost for three people was £1650, but they didn’t even offer a slice of cake to say “happy birthday." The food was mediocre—nothing like the quality we experienced at other Michelin-starred restaurants in London, yet they charged more. Interestingly, they didn't enforce the dress code, as some guests arrived in T-shirts and casual dresses. We expected high-quality food and service given the price, but we were disappointed and wouldn't recommend it. If your budget is around £500 per person, it's better to explore other options in central London, where many good restaurants are available.

We tried to be harsh critiques , as we were paying a lot and it was Michelin. Some of the food was 10/10. They said the brioche bread was one of their classics , however we found it dry and lacking flavour in general.

The course is very filling we left the restaurant with our tummy stuffed. The whole experience will take 3 hours.

The reason I can’t give it more than 4 stars is because of the service charge . It was 13 percent! Making you pay more than 100 pounds in total. It was a bit exorbitant.

Absolutely superb wedding anniversary dinner. The service and personalisation were perfect. Food is at an exquisite level with a complexity and detail that surprises with every step on the tasting menu
Absolutely recommend as one of the best places we’ve been to.

venues.name: Row on 5
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Without doubt one of the best dining experiences I have had. If this doesn't get another Michelin star this year I will eat my hat.

We've followed chefs Jason and Spencer for many years, particularly enjoying Spencer Metzger's journey on Great British Menu a few years ago and when I heard of this collaboration with Jason Atherton this flew to the top of my list.

My wonderful wife was able to secure a reservation for my birthday this year and my word what a great experience this proved to be.

As soon as you enter you are made to feel as though you are the only people in the restaurant, the space is elegant and intimate, as we entered it was incredible to see Spencer and the rest of the chefs right there preparing the meals in front of you. The choreography and elegance of the service was second to none. I thought we were just lucky to see Spencer for a short time but throughout the meal he was a presence overseeing the service and coming over to explain the dishes along with his personable and equally talented staff.

Every single course was sensational, not a single curio or slight miss. While we were excited to experience each course as it came we were almost wistful that the previous course had finished... Now time to find an excuse to return as soon as possible!

Row on 5 is one of the most anticipated restaurant openings in London recently, and expectations were understandably high given chef Jason Atherton’s success with Row on 45 in Dubai. We visited for a special Valentine’s Day dinner and had an overall memorable but mixed experience.

The evening begins with a tour of the venue – including the wine cellar, kitchen, and champagne room – before you're seated downstairs for the opening courses. The introduction is impressive and clearly influenced by Frantzén, which unfortunately becomes a recurring theme throughout the evening. Some dishes felt a little too inspired, bordering on imitation.

Standout dishes included the langoustine claw, beautifully presented with engraved chopsticks (which we got to take home), and the main of sika deer, which was perfectly cooked and paired with thoughtful, sweet sauces. The seafood courses were strong and well-executed overall. That said, not all courses lived up to the same level — the use of tarts became repetitive, and a few bites (like the brioche and stilton tart) felt underwhelming being listed as an individual course, or oddly placed in the lineup.

Service was polished and professional, with personal touches that really elevated the evening — from engraved chopsticks to a personalised menu sealed with wax. It felt special. However, pacing was an issue. We waited too long between courses towards the end, with little communication from staff, and that disrupted the flow of the meal.

The wine list is massive — physically and in scale. While there’s a by-the-glass option available, the wine pairings felt overpriced, with “upgrades” on the cheaper pairings that came across as cheeky rather than premium. Charging £220 extra for a single dessert wine on a £145 pairing felt excessive.

Desserts were good but again lacked consistency. The petit fours were fun to try, but too many tarts and sweets made the end of the meal feel repetitive and overly sweet.

Row on 5 has all the elements of a top-tier fine dining experience — talented kitchen, high production value, polished service, and luxury touches — but it hasn’t fully found its identity yet. The team clearly has ambitions beyond their current 1 Michelin star, and with refinement, they could very well get there. For now, it’s a strong one-star experience with flashes of brilliance.

Would I return? Possibly, in a year or two. They're still finding their voice. I have to mention that the £250 price tag is one of the most expensive dinners in London, and is of questionable value in my experience.

What a lovely evening!  It’s rare that I’ve loved every course on a tasting menu, and especially so  with 17!    All delivered by craftsman who are clearly passionate, not only about the dishes they’ve created but also about the experience you’re having.  Elegant but not stuffy; intimate but not familiar; every last detail considered…from start to finish, they dazzled!  Anytime I’m in London, they are my first booking.

It took like 4 hours and a half to finish our dinner!🩷 but everything was worth it. Our first time here and we really enjoyed it. Food, absolutely amazing and perfect. Drinks, I had the nonalcoholic pairing one, went very well with the food, Amazing sommelier!! Good vibes, good atmosphere and good service.😆. We really had a good time. ☺️

Simply overrated. The tasting menu was advertised for 15 courses, 5 of which were the sweets/dessert. It felt more like 1 snack (4 bites portion size served separately), 5 seafood/meat dishes, one-bite cheese, pre-dessert, dessert and petit four (multiple little gadgets). They raised my expectations too high, but the actual experience was what it really meant.

Meat portion was tiny. Lamb dish was so small like scraps (tasted ok, just too tiny tiny to enjoy properly).  There was more sauce than the actual substance to eat. It is also noted that no textually identifiable vegetables were used in the tasting menu.

I also felt culinary skills were rather limited for £250 tasting menu price point (price excluded drinks and service charges). But the presentation could easily hide the limitations.

For one course, it was presented by a server with a serious bad breath, likely caused by smoking or something else. It spoiled the dish from anticipation and the rest of the dinner. Sine then, I was hoping someone else came to present the remaining dishes.

The open kitchen was good for a show, but the restaurant flow had to be flawless, expecting every detail to be visible to the diners. Chefs were all very busy even the open kitchen was only serving 1/3 of the available dining area seating.

For instance, citrus zest was prepared using a grater and a scraper in a rush. The chef was brushing so hard and quick in a haste, and the zest didn't land on the food at all. Brushing off the zest with force would be more likely to miss your target food, making the ingredients on each serving inconsistent

I chose the counter seating. Perhaps the "corridor" behind my seat was a bit tight. The server passed by to another table and scratched the back of the stool and my hair. I was fuming that he didn't even apologise as if he didn't feel the bump. Otherwise, the counter seating was a good option for solo or couple diners.

Non-alcholic beverage selected was limited. Yuzu Collins didn't taste like the description provided, except a lot of soda water. Sigh

I'd say 3 stars for Google review in general, but have to deduct one star taking into account they were charging £250 (tasting menu price excluding drinks and service charge) that was equivalent to other Michelin 2-star restaurant tasting menu price in London.

venues.name: Akoko
venues.description: Elevated West African dishes are paired with international wines at this warm, upmarket restaurant.

reviews.text:
Akoko was hands down the best fine dining experience I’ve had this year. We had the tasting menu with the non-alcoholic pairing, and somehow each dish was better than the last. How is that even possible? Every course carried a subtle heat, something you rarely see in fine dining, and honestly, more restaurants should take note.

The drinks were just as impressive, each beautifully crafted with West African influences from Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, and Côte d’Ivoire. Sitting at the counter seats gave us the best view of the action, watching the chefs work with such care and precision. The staff were also incredibly friendly, explaining each dish in detail and sharing the stories behind them. The warmth and love from the whole team was truly felt throughout the experience.

My favourite dishes were the Jollof, squid abunuabunu, and monkfish egusi, all absolute standouts. It was such a joy to experience the flavours of West Africa, especially since it’s a cuisine we rarely get to enjoy back home in Sydney. Truly exceptional from start to finish. 👏🔥

I visited Akoko with my partner for our anniversary, and it was an incredible experience from start to finish. We enjoyed a 10-course tasting menu inspired by West African cuisine, and as a Nigerian, it was truly heartwarming to see so many familiar dishes beautifully reimagined.

The standout dish for me was the MoiMoi with mackerel and black eye bean sauce – perfectly balanced and packed with flavour. We were seated near the counter, which gave us a great view of the chefs in action and added an intimate touch to the evening.

A special highlight was chatting with the head chef after the service, who gave us more insight into the menu and the inspiration behind the dishes.

I’d also like to give a big thank you to Raheem, our waiter, whose professionalism, knowledge, and thoughtful commentary on each course made the experience even more memorable.

Highly recommend Akoko for a special occasion – it’s a true celebration of West African flavours done with elegance and creativity.

Hard to even describe the experience at this West African fine dining establishment. Superlatives feel cliche. From the hand washing ceremony to the final dessert you will be transported to another culture and eat food you've likely never tasted before. You are presented with a menu when you sit down that describes the multiple courses you will receive. Mine offered an additional caviar dish for a supplement that I accepted since... Why not? The servers present each dish with an explanation of the ingredients and how best to eat it. Each server was incredible. I sat solo at the counter watching the chefs prepare the dishes. Each dish was unique and hard to even pick a favorite but there wasn't anything I wouldn't love to eat again. It's pricey for sure but you get your money's worth.

I've dined at many fine restaurants in London, but Akoko is the one I always find myself wanting to return to. It's been a while since my last visit, yet the flavours remain unforgettable — rich, bold, and truly 10/10. Consistently impressive, Akoko delivers a unique and memorable culinary experience every time.

5* Food, 4* Service

The food was excellent. Unique flavours in the excellent tasting menu, which left us feeling very satisfied. Good mix of fish and meats and the smaller portion sizes is made up for the large number or portions.

The desserts were some of the best dishes I’ve had anywhere - we loved the Chin Chin and Black Sesame Fudge.

Would recommend for those who want to experience some more refined flavours of Nigerian / West African cuisine.

Pairing menu with cocktails would be a nice touch for those that aren’t into the wines as much.

venues.name: Club Gascon - French Michelin Starred Restaurant
venues.description: Southwest French menu with all sorts of foie gras dishes in formal, marble-and-wood setting.

address.formatted: St Bartholomew House, 57 W Smithfield, London

venues.vicinity: St Bartholomew House, 57 W Smithfield, London

reviews.text:
My partner secretly booked this restaurant for my birthday, and it was an unforgettable experience from start to finish. The staff were so welcoming and knowledgeable, which made us feel truly taken care of.

We chose the full set menu with wine pairing, and every dish was incredible. As a French person, I can be a bit critical when it comes to food (we French take it very seriously 😉), but here everything was simply perfect. One highlight for me was an artichoke dish by Chef Pascal, with just one bite, it brought me straight back to a childhood memory. It’s truly amazing when a chef can create food that evokes such deep emotions!

We were also very grateful to the Chef and his team for taking the time to show us around the kitchen and share a moment with us. It made the evening feel even more special and memorable.

I had the most wonderful birthday celebration here, and it’s an experience I’ll always remember. Thank you so much to the whole team!

We had a wonderful evening at the Club Gascon on 7th August. The food is of an amazing standard complemented by original and unique presentations which really add to the whole culinary experience.
Everyone of the dishes was delicious.  The service was attentive, friendly and professional. The atmosphere was relaxed and sophisticated in a decor of impeccable standard.
We really enjoyed everything about the evening, will definitely return and would recommend.
We certainly feel that the price was very reasonable for the quality of this experience.
A big thank you to the team for a very lovely evening making our special occasion perfect.

Club Gascon offers a refined, inventive cuisine in a beautiful warm and cozy setting. The food is of superb quality, and although not every dish in their 6 or 8 courses menu will please everyone, the quality of the food and the creativity of the pairings makes it an enriching dining experience.

The service is very kind and attentive. I would recommend the wine pairing as it paired beautifully with the food, and was very tasty.

The restaurant more than deserves its Michelin star, and in my opinion is a must-visit for anyone looking for a calm fine dining experience in London. The setting of the restaurant is also fantastic around Smithfield Market, on the northern boundary of the City of London, a stone’s throw away from Farringdon Elizabeth Line station entrance.

I was very lucky to be taken on a first date here. The restaurant was empty but the food was amazing.

Had a phenomenal tasting menu and by the end, my date and I were on the floor, we could not eat anymore, we were extremely well fed. They really catered to my date’s gluten free diet as well so he was not missing out on anything.

The only annoying thing for me was the person serving us wouldn’t leave us alone to talk on our date, she proceeded to tell my date her entire life story which I found rather odd. They need to leave people alone to have their conversations and not tell them their entire life story, highly inappropriate especially as I was on a first date.

However the food was incredible and they really catered to my date’s gluten free requirements so we were both very happy.

Food was not bad despite portions were very small for the tasting menu. The restaurant didn't have a non-alcoholic beverage menu. When I told the sommelier that I was not drinking and asked for any non-alcoholic options, she replied "coke". I was shocked and speechless at the moment. It never occurred to me that I'd be drinking coke for a French meal. I didn't give up asking, so she said she could ask the bar to make a virgin Mojito but didn't know how much they would charge me... ummmm... she then "guessed" between £10-£15. I was really thinking if I should leave the restaurant as the conversation was getting weirder. Anyway, I stayed for the tasting menu. Virgin Mojito was a disaster, too sour and lots of crushed ice, herbs not fragrant at all. There was not enough front-of-house staff so food was always waiting on the tray to get served. For example, foam on dessert almost disappeared and turned to liquid when delivered. There were 9 tables on a Monday evening, so wasn't too busy to be excused.

venues.name: Hélène Darroze at The Connaught
venues.description: Famous chef's haute cuisine in an elegant hotel dining room with wood panels and colourful fabrics.

reviews.text: I had a wonderful experience at Hélène Darroze. The service was impeccable—attentive, warm, and professional. Every dish was beautifully presented and full of flavor, showcasing incredible attention to detail and creativity. The ambiance added to the overall experience, making it a truly memorable meal. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a fine dining experience that delivers on both taste and hospitality.

We had an amazing experience on Saturday night with the 7-course tasting menu. Every detail is thought of, the staff is extremely friendly and the food was absolutely delicious. They even designed a vegetarian tasting menu on request for my wife. Although they didn't do anything specific for the wedding anniversary we were celebrating there (slightly surprising), you receive small "extras" throughout the meal, amuse-bouche, palate cleanser, little pastry individually wrapped to take away. All in all, a great evening.

Together with Epicure most certainly the best french restaurant I have ever visited. Perfect from start to finish from every perspective. My favourites were the squid with potatoes, tomato with sardines and the lobster. Plus the bread ice cream was crazy good. I must also underline how amazing and knowledgable yet down to earth the service was. Highly recommended!

From the moment you arrive, the Connaught and all its history welcome you. The doormen and staff are the most welcoming, ready to help you and with the biggest smile. The facilities overall are excellent. The decoration of the restaurant deserves special mention.
Now onto the main event, the food and the proposals of Darroze are always excellent. In these pictures you can see the spring menu. Albeit not taking dramatic risks, every plate hits a perfect note that will stay with you for days. Worth mentioning the pricing is very fair for the excellent quality provided, which is greatly appreciated. I recommend it to anyone and I will continue to visit.

Attended for a special family occasion. Highly recommended with outstanding service. We enjoyed the 7-course "Taste of Summer" menu complete with champagne pairings. Not entirely necessary to share photos, as there are many gracious photos already provided by other reviewers. However, the champagne pairings were spot on and we've provided a few of those tasted for reference.

venues.name: Core by Clare Smyth
venues.description: Seasonal British fine dining from ex Gordon Ramsay chef in laid-back, light and airy surroundings.

address.formatted: Notting Hill Brasserie, 92 Kensington Park Rd, London

venues.vicinity: Notting Hill Brasserie, 92 Kensington Park Rd, London

reviews.text:
Core by Clare is truly deserving of its prestigious three Michelin stars. From the moment I stepped through the door, I was enveloped in an atmosphere of elegance and warmth.

The culinary experience was nothing short of extraordinary; each dish was a masterpiece, beautifully presented and bursting with flavor.

As a fully vegetarian diner, I was thrilled to discover the creativity and thoughtfulness that went into my meal. The vegetarian options were not only diverse but also innovative, showcasing the chef's ability to elevate plant-based ingredients to new heights. Each dish was a delightful symphony of flavors, with vibrant colors and textures that made every bite a joy. I especially loved the potato dish!

The staff at Core were exceptionally friendly and personable, making me feel welcomed and valued throughout my visit.

In summary, Core by Clare is a remarkable dining destination that combines exquisite food, attentive service, and a welcoming atmosphere. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a memorable culinary adventure.

What a fantastic evening we had at Core. We were placed at the chef's table, which gave us the opportunity to see the kitchen. The kitchen was busy but orderly and very quiet. Clare was there overseeing each dish that left the kitchen.  The service was exceptional, fast, professional but unobtrusive.  The food presentation was imaginative and beautiful. We had the Classic taster menu, from which my froends substituted a couple of dishes. That was a great and flexible service.
The food was an explosion of various tastes and colour. The menu was new reflecting the seasonal changes with produce from local farms.
Although the portions looked small, I was full long before the desert came.
I would like to take family there again to enjoy this lovely place.

Core is a 3 Michelin star restaurant for a reason. Everything was amazingly delicious and beautiful. The staff were very friendly and personable. I had called ahead to inquire if they could accommodate my fish and shellfish allergy and they kindly made me a special menu.
I also want to clarify for anyone who might be skeptical about the size of the dishes in fine dining restaurants like Core; I promise you will leave VERY full and VERY satisfied!

We were blown away by our first 3 star Michelin dining experience. The chefs are truly making art with their dishes, and each one is delicious. The classic menu was a great choice for us, and we loved everything save the cod (which we still liked, but wasn't as impressive in flavor). The staff were attentive and flexible. CORE is fabulous, from the food to the staff to the ambiance.

Be sure to book your reservation as soon as slots open up! The dining room is intimate.

The experience is highly recommended. The service was solid 5/5 it was outstanding, the food was really good but i had very high expectations where it barely met. The atmosphere and the place is very nice and well put together.
The maltesers cake/dessert was one of the best desserts i have ever tried if not the best. We tried both menus the classic and the seasonal, both were really good and creative.

venues.name: Behind Restaurant
venues.description: Seasonal seafood tasting menus offered in a compact, acclaimed destination that has a wine bar.

reviews.text:
What a quietly dazzling place this is. There’s something wonderfully conspiratorial about stepping through that modest entrance, as though you’re being let in on a secret.

The evening began with a generosity that’s actually become rare in fine dining - an extra splash of sauce here, a little more wine there - no questions, no charge, and not in excess, but with the sort of intuitive hospitality that says, “We’re glad you’re here.” It wasn’t about selling a product, or ticking boxes of ‘luxury’ and ‘innovation’; it was about making an experience breathe.

The fish-focused menu was, quite simply, divine. Each plate felt considered but never contrived. The chef’s attention to detail was everywhere, not only in the precise cooking but in the courtesy and conversation that accompanied it. He seemed genuinely invested in the pleasure of his guests, which lent the whole evening a warmth too often missing from Michelin-minded establishments.

In short, Behind is a restaurant that remembers why restaurants exist at all: to nourish, to delight, and, if only for a few hours, to make the world feel exquisitely well-arranged.

We had a great time at Behind, exceptional on all counts. Being able to interact with the chefs was a cool experience and the space is set up to facilitate. Food was first rate and demonstrated a mastery of seafood. Wine pairings were thoughtful and well presented.

Fantastic lunch!
Such a beautiful restaurant!
Intimate, friendly, special.
The chefs produced the most exquisite flavours, which we devoured!
Audrey was very knowledgeable about all the wines and was lovely too.
Highly recommend this restaurant, it’s cool, it’s delicious and it’s small and intimate. Everything is done in front of you, absolutely loved it!
Will be back, I wish Andy continued success.

Great experience. Fantastic for those who love seafood, as it's the focus of their menu. They're not necessarily pushing boundaries with their cooking, but their quality and skill is undoubted. Very well deserved of their michelin star, probably one of our favorite 1-star restaurants in London now.

It was a fantastic experience, showing just how unique flavours can come from simple ingredients. Perfect for seafood lovers, though they’re more than happy to accommodate non-meat eaters as well. While we expected mostly seafood, the chef surprised us with refreshing herb sorbets and fruity shots between courses, which was a delightful touch. The atmosphere is definitely more relaxed than most fine dining spots, with soft lighting and mellow music adding to the charm. The chefs were incredibly friendly and welcoming, making it feel almost like dining at home with friends. And don’t miss out on checking the unique restrooms while you’re there.

venues.name: Restaurant 1890 by Gordon Ramsay
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
I highly appreciate the restaurant for the way they handled a small incident.
My family reserved a table for 2 adults and 1 child. We only remembered to mention that we would be bringing a child under 10 years old and asked whether the restaurant would accept that. Both the restaurant and I forgot to confirm that we would only need 2 tasting menus for the adults. My child would not be dining, just sitting with us. As a result, the restaurant prepared 3 tasting menus.

Right after finishing the amuse-bouche, we clarified the situation. Normally, I would have been required to pay for all 3 tasting menus without being able to cancel at that point. Fortunately, the restaurant agreed to serve and charge us for only 2 tasting menus.

The food and quality were absolutely worth the price for such a culinary experience.

We truly value this restaurant!

The restaurant is located at The Savoy Hotel. Need to reserve in advance, they will confirm your attendance and any dietary restrictions. We had dinner here. Do plan for a 3+ hours time to enjoy the tasting menu thoroughly. There were no ala carte menu.

The tasting menu comes with amuse bouche, bread with butter, 2 appetizers, 2 mains, 2 desserts, and petit four. There is also an option for additional caviar and / or additional cheese platters for extra $. The cheese platters were absolutely delicious. You get to choose 5 different type of cheese from the cheese cart. There were also pairing menu with wine, but we did not go for that. We had a few cocktails, "XV" was my favorite.

Although each of the portion looks small, at the end of the tasting menu you will feel really full.

Service was great, all the servers were very attentive, knowledgeable about the food and drinks. We got the tasting menu list with us at the end.

Great atmosphere to eat with your family or friends.

The tasting menu went downhill since the main course. The duck with skin on was rubbery and chewy. Then the cheese course was just average. Pre-dessert and dessert were just mediocre. However, all the canapés and the first few courses were great. Having said that, the design of the overall tasting menu was quite poor, in my opinion, in terms of portion sizes amidst the technical misses. Fish and meat portion was tiny, but there are a lot of baked elements, what I see as dull "dry" food, including crumpet, brioche, biscuits, and madeleines. I don't have a food allergy, but eating too much bread in general felt stuffed, rather than stomach satisfied; not to mention the expectations of higher standards and culinary surprises. My favourites were crispy frog leg and crab. Black truffle bomb was also executed perfectly.

The restaurant interior was rather too dark to enjoy the dishes visually. By today's preferences, it feels a bit dated, rather than from a particular architectural style. Toilet facilities were located outside the restaurant in another part of the hotel via a flight of stairs. Not very convenient.

Service was OK. But I'm not sure how they took my comments that I didn't like the food much from the main course onwards. I heard faintly they were talking in the kitchen. Wall acoustic was not very well designed. At the end of the meal, they had IT issue printing the bill and said they would send me the receipt by email, but they didn't send it. Leaving me the impression that the hardware and the software of the restaurant were rather poor.

Considering the one-michellin-star restaurant competition in London, their price were set at the higher range, but they couldn't deliver the equivalent, so I'd conclude the tasting menu had a very low value for money.

We spent night two in London attending the tasting at Gordon Ramsay’s 1890.  We made reservations several months ago and were very much looking forward to this visit.  Overall it was a splendid experience.  The ambiance and feel was unparalleled.  The staff, especially the maître ď  on the floor was exceptional.  Every dish was amazing.  We ordered the black truffle add-on.  Oh yes!!   We also chose the wine pairing for me and the non-alcoholic pairing for my wife.  I recommend both of these pairings!  One of the wines was served in a dark glass with the staff wanting my guess on color and type.  Relax everyone, you’ll never be more wrong than me lol. We had only one complaint, the gentleman with the heavy accent serving several of the dishes had atrocious breath.  Very off putting.  Next time in London, we will definitely attend restaurant Gordon Ramsay!  4.9 stars!  Cheers!
An absolutely amazing experience.  The food is plated like art on a canvas plate.  The staff maneuver each and every plating like performers at a ballet.  The food is unlike any other.  Exceptional!

venues.name: Cycene
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: A tremendous evening of hospitality.  Keen focus on British ingredients leveraging local producers, a rooftop garden, and foraging.  All British wine pairings available, as well as a soft beverage pairing that my son absolutely loved.  Could not recommend more strongly when in Shoreditch!

We came for dinner and really enjoyed the experience from the bar to kitchen to dining area. The service was refined yet friendly. There were some interesting flavours in the 15 courses but everything worked for me. My favourites were the A5 wagyu snack, crab, wagyu and scallop (supplement) and the pigeon. This is definitely a special occasion place but I highly recommend it!

Cycene, named after the Old English word for “kitchen”. Cycene is contemporary British restaurant. The current Head Chef is Taz Sarhane Known for his innovative approach to modern British cuisine. He has developed a passion for ingredient preservation techniques like fermenting and dry-aging.
The menu format is tasting menu only of ten courses, with just 15 customers at capacity in total. They source British ingredients.
The design space is intimate with details include wooden panelling.

We had high expectations for Cycene when we chose it to celebrate our anniversary, but unfortunately, our visit was marred by poor hospitality, lack of communication, and an unreasonably rigid approach to service. While some members of the team were professional and attentive, others, especially the chef Taz Sarhane, seemed inexperienced and bad-tempered, which further contributed to a frustrating evening.

We arrived 20 minutes late due to heavy rain and traffic, but as a courtesy, we tried calling the restaurant three times, 30 minutes before our reservation, with no response. Upon arrival, instead of any form of acknowledgment or explanation, we were immediately escorted upstairs to our table. While the service on the ground-floor bar was just about to start with two empty seats, clearly ours. Only after sitting down did we realize that we had completely missed the initial experience at the ground-floor bar, which was supposed to include bread, broth and a course with A5 Wagyu and Caviar. No one mentioned this to us, and we had to ask three different staff members before finally getting a response. It was only after repeatedly bringing it up that the chef himself came to speak with us—but instead of addressing our concerns professionally, he was dismissive, defensive, and outright rude.

Rather than showing even the slightest empathy, the chef repeatedly emphasized his strict timing policy, stating that he did not want to keep later guests waiting because of our delay. However, there were clearly two empty seats at the bar, and we were the last guests of the night, making his argument feel completely unjustified. When we expressed our disappointment at how the situation had been handled, he became visibly irritated and told us we could leave if we were unhappy—a shocking level of hostility from a Michelin-starred establishment. Throughout the conversation, he kept bringing up the restaurant’s Michelin status, as if to look down on us rather than addressing the issue professionally.

The food itself was underwhelming. While we could see that the kitchen was attempting to incorporate Nordic-style fermentation techniques, the execution felt forced and unbalanced, lacking the refinement and harmony that this approach requires. Some flavors were overly intense and clashed rather than complementing each other, resulting in a mediocre and forgettable dining experience. Compared to the many Michelin-starred restaurants we have visited around the world, the food here simply did not stand out. To make matters worse, when the chef finally offered a “compensation” for the missed experience, all we received was bread—something that should have been served to us without needing to ask.

Despite the chef’s unprofessional behavior, we must acknowledge that some members of the staff were polite and attentive. Fine dining is not just about food; it is about hospitality, attention to detail, and the ability to create a seamless experience for guests. This restaurant failed in all these aspects, and given the dismissive attitude from leadership, we cannot recommend it.

London is one of the most diverse cities in the world and home to an incredibly rich dining scene. It is also where we live and work, and we find it unacceptable that the chef’s unreasonable attitude is allowed to tarnish the experience of those who come to Cycene with high expectations, eager to explore the avant-garde dining concept at Blue Mountain School. During our conversation, the chef insisted that he prepares over 100 dishes a day for different guests and therefore cannot make compromises for anyone. But isn’t ensuring a great experience for every guest exactly what every hospitality professional should strive for?

There are far better Michelin-starred restaurants that value their guests and execute their vision with skill and grace—this is not one of them.
Had to come back after the first time where I had the best langoustine ever with the previous chef. Nice flavours, light and creative. Loved the snacks especially the duck liver parfait!

venues.name: The Ninth
venues.description: Casual restaurant with romantic first-floor space, serving French-influenced Mediterranean cuisine.

reviews.text:
Had the set lunch which was excellent value for money.

Ingredients were fresh and the food was perfectly presented. I enjoyed the crab pasta starter. But there was nothing about the food that stood out. Even the recommended potato side dish was pleasant but not something I'd dream about. It was overall a very pleasant and above average experience but forgettable.

Visited last week for the early dinner set menu. Excellent value for money: a three course michelin starred dinner for £38 per person. There were two of us eating so we tried all the meat options (vegetarian options available, but we didn't try those)

The whole meal was lovely, but there was a few dishes in particular which were amazing. The cured trout starter tasted very fresh, with a simple yet delicious flavour, topped with roe. The pork tenderloin was cooked excellently, texture was almost like a filet mignon, but with the rich flavours of pork. Pain perdu with tonka bean dessert was a lovely end to the meal, not too sweet, just how I like it. The other dishes were also excellent.

Overall a great restaurant, well deserving of its michelin star. I'll definitely have to come again to try the à la carte menu.

Lovely dinner, food was delicious.
Scallops were fresh and delicate. Both the beef cheek & tongue, and the Iberico pork pluma were exceptionally tender and flavourful.
We ordered two of their pastas - the squid ink malloreddus and truffle conchiglie. Both were lovely, even my husband who doesn’t eat much pasta loved them a lot.

Both desserts we had were nice but their signature Pain Perdu is a must, perfectly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.

Waitress was very friendly and informative, we were not in a rush but noticed the service was a tad slow though. Can’t comment on the wine pairings as we didn’t order this.

Had an amazing set menu dinner there last night with some girlfriends. Beautiful place, superb food. The only "wrinkle" on an otherwise incredible experience was the fact that when we booked the dinner, the price of the three-course option was £38. However, when we arrived a month later, the price went up to £44. What??? Nearly 16% increase in ONE month?! Also the 25% (!!!) service charge was added to our bill, which is obviously ludicrous. It is discretionary though. Apart from that, it was a beautiful dinner and the waitresses were very friendly.

We went here for my birthday last week and we loved it. The food was fantastic and from the moment you walk through the door you are made welcome. I think they may have been short staffed this day but this did not impact our experience.

From start to finish the food was incredible, the crab spaghetti though was an absolute stand out winner in my eyes!! It had the most incredible flavour and the samphire was a welcome addition, but there were little crunchy bits that simulated the feeling of eating crab, they weren’t to crunchy but had enough crunch to really give you the feeling.

The pork was amazing, and lots of the lovely fish dishes. I can definitely recommend coming here, after drinks it pushed the price up, but for £35 for the set menu what’s not to like.

We came here because we were told to, now I’m telling you to. 🤤

venues.name: The Ritz Restaurant
venues.description: High-end British–French dining in baroque-style  gilded salon with ceiling frescoes and chandeliers.

reviews.text: Having enjoyed Afternoon Tea and the Rivoli Bar at the Ritz in the past, I now wanted to try out the restaurant. I visited for the breakfast service. The atmosphere is really fantastic. The coffee, orange juice, English breakfast and Eggs Benedict were very good. The only thing I noticed was that the hash brown was a bit hard on the edges and therefore a little difficult to cut. I would have liked a little more attention to detail with the service. I had to actively ask for a new juice. Otherwise the staff were all very kind. Overall, it was a great experience that I would like to repeat in the future.

Wahhhhh, Sunday lunch at The Ritz.
Art des table for 4 people.
Started with a warm welcome and clear instructions from the doorman. Rivoli Bar for a cocktail, very helpful member of staff to explain the extensive menu. Cocktails were very good. Then walking through the main halls to the restaurant was beautiful and greeted and brought to our table effortlessly.
Introduced to waiters and sommelier and so we began. Stunning amuse bouche, fish cookery and sauces stunning, beef Wellington good, sauces and potatoes amazing. Pre desert stunning and the crepe suzette amazing...
Sommelier was possibly the highlight. Warm, welcoming and loved talking, explaing and recommending a few wines. His manner and professionalism was exemplary.
What a fantastic experience.

Absolutely sublime experience at the Ritz! Every bit as fancy and impressive as it was expensive! Definitely worth it however for taste of food presentation quality and ambiance. We went for my mom’s birthday on 9/16/25 and dined on the 7 course meal. Of note for the course meals everyone in the table has to do the same experience. This delectable delight had the perfect amount of savory and sweet and was definitely good enough portion size to be filling as well. Each course was a culinary delight with robust well paired flavors that lended to the next dish. The service was also outstanding everyone was attentive courteous and well versed on presentation of the dishes. The ambiance was also amazing quite striking elegance in a more intimate setting. They additionally made mention of my mom’s birthday and ensured that this was recognized. I appreciated their hard work and dedication to making my moms birthday meal memorable

An extraordinary experience. John Williams gained his second Michelin star in February 2025 but we've known this restaurant to be one of the best, if not the best restaurant in London for many years. The dining room is opulent, the service friendly and simply the best anywhere and the kitchen just keeps cooking and presenting some of the best UK food we've ever enjoyed. There's a perfectly reasonable dress code. You will not be disappointed.

We had the pleasure of visiting the RITZ resutatnt a Two Michelin starred restaurant in London, and the experience was truly exceptional. The food was exquisite, and the service was absolutely outstanding we were treated like royalty. It felt like being princes for the evening.

This was my third visit, and each time has been uniquely beautiful, with something new to admire. What truly makes the place special is the people the warmth, care, and attention they bring.

A heartfelt thank you to the managers special Mr Enzo…  and every team member working behind the scenes. You’ve created something truly memorable. we will never forget

venues.name: Ormer Mayfair
venues.description: Carefully sourced British ingredients take centre stage in this wood-panelled hotel dining room.

address.formatted: Flemings Mayfair, 7-12 Half Moon St, 7-12 Half Moon St, Mayfair, London

venues.vicinity: Flemings Mayfair, 7-12 Half Moon St, 7-12 Half Moon St, Mayfair, London

reviews.text: I really love this place! The food is super delicious. You can see the love in every dish, right down to the details. The service is amazing. If you enjoy wine pairing, the sommelier here is adorable—friendly, knowledgeable, and fun to chat with. All the staff are so cheerful and welcoming. It’s perfect from the start to the end. I’ll definitely be coming back with my family and close friends!

We dined at the  Ormer Mayfair while staying at the Flemming Mayfair, September 11-12, 2025..  The five-course tasting menu was exceptional in creativity, presentation and taste. The service throughout the meal was impeccable and our sommelier brought us some exceptional wines.  Of special note during the meal were the broth, roast Yorkshire duck and a dessert made with a blown candy shell and mascarpone filling.  A wonderful evening at an outstanding restaurant.

The service at Omer Mayfair is outstanding, innovative, cool, and contemporary. The staff are knowledgeable and clearly well-trained. They do talk a bit too much for my taste, but their energy and friendliness make the experience lively.
The space, however, is less impressive. It is located in a basement with a slightly musty, old-fashioned feel that does not match the fresh, modern service style. I loved the service pieces, with creative tableware that added personality, and wish the rest of the space had that same sense of originality.
The food was technically excellent, with precise seasoning, proper cuisson, and beautifully composed plates. But I felt like I had eaten a similar version of every dish before. There was almost no sense of surprise or creativity. If you are going to serve such small portions, each dish has to be mind-blowing, and here they simply were not. The Moroccan influence was barely noticeable, showing up only in a few small details.
The dessert was the highlight of the evening. It finally had the fusion surprise elements I wish every other dish had. I also appreciated the chocolate offered when leaving.

This is definitely one of the best restaurants I’ve tried in London. The quality of the service is absolutely amazing. The course menu is very well selected and explained by your server. The place itself is also very nice and cozy, also the quiet environment allows you to talk comfortably with your guests. My family and I had a great time here, we would definitely dine here again.

We came here to celebrate our 2 year wedding anniversary and it was spectacular. The service was fantastic. The atmosphere was calm and classic British. The food was delicious, it was exactly as desired on the menu and really brought out the flavours of the dishes and the chefs inspirational countries. The menu had been curated with lots of flair and very well made. Definitely some beautiful food to enjoy.

venues.name: HIDE
venues.description: A three floor space in a contemporary setting with elevated morning to late-night dining options.

reviews.text: We had great dinner at HIDE. The restaurant has beautiful atmosphere. All dishes were delicious and very well balanced. The highlight of our dinner was monk fish and scallops. The selection of wine is amazing. The service is top notch.

What a fantastic experience from start to finish! This place is truly a gem, the bar is elegant, classy, and the drinks are next level. I tried one with watermelon, and wow, what a taste! The ambiance is wonderful, with a lovely aroma throughout. We enjoyed a couple of drinks, and everything was absolutely delicious. Even the bathrooms are impressive!

The food was excellent — fresh flavors, beautifully balanced, and presented with a clean, refined aesthetic. Each dish reflected great attention to detail in execution.

Unfortunately, the service fell short of the same standard. While the plates spoke for themselves, the experience was let down when our waiter began walking away midway through explaining a dish. It disrupted the flow and diminished what should have been a polished, engaging moment.

Overall, the cooking deserves recognition, but service consistency needs to match the quality coming out of the kitchen for the experience to truly shine.

Difficult to assess. We were told initially we were going to be upstairs, but we were sat downstairs. Very busy venue with lots of groups some quieter than others. We went for breakfast and I am a huge fan of cooked breakfasts. The “fry up” was a very small mushroom, one unexciting sausage of no great flavour and two small rashers of streaky bacon and half a large tomato with a thick central core. The food was reasonably free of too much grease, but not overly flavoursome, sadly a nice but underwhelming breakfast, not least for the price. At £30 one expects great textured flavour rich sausages. Eggs were just ages nicely cooked but not much more to say. Staff were lovely breakfast was ok. My sourdough toast was good and my daughter was thrilled with her huge croissant with a number of choices of spreads and jams. Is it interesting? Yes, was it the sort of meal I would expect to see at a one Michelin starred venue not really
Great atmosphere. Centre piece stairs / architectural aesthetically pleasing. Amazing food. Quality of food great! Presented well. Great service. Lovely staff.  Highly recommended.

venues.name: HUMO
venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Had an enjoyable experience for dinner. Complementary small bites were very welcome. The highlights were the grilled menu items and in particular the lamb. Their lamb was slightly gamier than expected but I liked it anyways. Great sauces and garnish. The shrimp dish was also very tasty.

I only have one issue which was the lack of carbs on the menu.

Restaurant is very pretty to look at and is meticulously designed from floor to ceiling.

Service was friendly and excellent.

Awesome experience...had booked the upstairs tasting menu but on arrival was told there was a cancellation at the chef's table and asked if I'd like to eat downstairs. Food was outstanding...high-quality ingredients, and most dishes were grounded in tradition but featured fun and creative twists. Delicious. One of the stand-outs: the salad (salad???). Hearing the stories directly from the chef was fun, and despite his obvious talents he seems like a very grounded and humble guy, easy to talk with and ready to ask questions. Also one of the stronger curated wine pairings I've had at a fine dining restaurant recently.

We had such an incredible experience here.
Firstly the food is amazing, each dish was perfect and couldn’t fault them. Such a depth of flavour and very well balanced.
The atmosphere is great, love the open kitchen so you can see the flames they are cooking on. It can get hot if you are sat next to the kitchen but I saw they give people little fans to help with the heat.
The staff have great attention to detail. We loved the careful explanations for each part of the dish, and suggestions on which order to eat them.

Honestly, perfect
Myself and my partner went for the tasting menu at the counter for her 28th birthday and I cannot fault a single bit of it.
All the staff were very attentive and knowledgeable about each and every element of the courses.
The food speaks for itself, flavours I wouldn't have thought to put together but evening just works.
Yes it was expensive at over 500 but it was worth every penny.
Beautiful experience and I will definitely be retuning.

Absolutely delicious meal. Wonderful interiors and stunning open fire grill in the centre of the restaurant. Everyone was so polite and efficient.
We didn't know what to expect but he food was incredible. They suggested we order a dish from each section and the dishes did not disappoint.
Complex, deep flavours perfectly balanced.

Would highly recommend to anyone

venues.name: Frog by Adam Handling Restaurant Covent Garden
venues.description: Flagship restaurant of chef Adam Handling, using local ingredients on a contemporary seasonal menu.

attributions: Frog by Adam Handling Restaurant Covent Garden
Frog by Adam Handling Restaurant Covent Garden
Frog by Adam Handling Restaurant Covent Garden
Frog by Adam Handling Restaurant Covent Garden

reviews.text: I had an amazing night. I felt welcome and taken care of the moment I walked in. I sat at the counter. Because I love watching the chefs and they did an amazing job. So calm. So concentrated. The food they sent out was perfect. The tasting menu gave me so many different foods. And I loved that the Michelin Star food felt so personal and homely. When the staff tells so you to spoon the gravy with the bread you are in the right place 😊 A Michelin star restaurant where you can your fingers dirty, And the wine pairing. Perfect. The sommelier knows what he is doing. Just listening to him makes your evening. Thanks to the whole team for a perfect night.

We revisited Frog by Adam Handling after eight years, this time celebrating a friend’s 21st birthday. We’d previously enjoyed the private dining room downstairs, but for this occasion we chose the main dining space upstairs.

We opted for the lunch menu, which began with three amuse-bouches, followed by Parker House bread and butter, a fish course, a duck course, dessert, and petits fours. One of the highlights is that you can bring your own wine at lunch with no corkage fee (though there is one at dinner).

The interior is vibrant, with an open-plan kitchen, bench-style seating, and bold artwork—including modern takes on portraits of the late Queen and the current King. We sat at a circular table near the window with its striking white rubber surface.

Amuse-bouches
•	Tuna & herbs: a delicate pastry cup filled with tuna and topped with bright herbs.
•	Crab, green chilli, buckwheat: a crisp cylindrical shell filled with white and brown crab meat, subtly spiced.
•	Chicken & egg: crispy chicken skin served inside an egg—imaginative and delicious.

Bread & butter
The Parker House bread was warm and beautifully presented in a tear-apart loaf. The standout, though, was the butter: chicken skin butter with a rich chicken parfait centre, elegantly shaped like a rose.

Palate cleanser
A cucumber tea served between courses was refreshing but fairly simple compared to the other dishes.

Fish course
Cod with courgette and smoked fish elements. The presentation was stunning, with courgette prepared in several ways. However, the portion of cod itself was surprisingly small.

Meat course
Merrifield duck with apricot and cobnuts. The sauce was superb, though the duck portion was again on the small side.

Dessert
Verbena, Earl Grey, and peach—a beautifully balanced dessert that was tart, sweet, slightly sour, and visually elegant.

Petits fours
A seeded madeleine served with cream and raspberry jam. Pleasant, though not as memorable as the other courses.

Service & atmosphere
The service was warm, attentive, and interactive throughout. Adam Handling wasn’t in the kitchen during our visit but did make an appearance in the dining room, as his family was also dining there.

Afterwards, we noted that the cocktail bar Eve, located downstairs, opens at 4pm—a stylish spot to continue the afternoon with drinks.

We went here on a Thursday lunchtime for the lunch tasting menu as a birthday treat for my husband. We were shown to our table and given the wine list whilst the server showed us some options for champagne, myself had some fizz whilst the husband had a glass of red wine. The food was sensational. Each course was brought to us with a description of what the dish was and the inspiration behind the dish.
We had 5 courses and each got better and better! The lamb main courses and strawberry desert were a highlight for me. My husband went for the extra cheese course, which he said was outstanding. The truffle honey was deliecious . 100% recommend this restaurant, friendly service, and an amazing experience. I can't wait to return!

Frog by Adam Handling is one of those rare restaurant experiences that truly leaves you speechless.  A rare perfect experience.
The service was friendly but attentive and professional - everything it should be. The dining room itself had good energy and niche decor which I found very suitable. More importantly, the food from start to finish was just breathtaking. It was personal, innovative, clever, and most importantly, bloody delicious. This is three star cooking not one star cooking.

Terrific food, things I’ve never had before or thought of eating together. The staff were friendly, professional and on the most part, attentive. We had a couple of issues with missed requests, but it didn’t detract from the experience.
Overall, great food, staff and ambience. Defo worth visiting for a special occasion or if you like fine dining. Good value as well

venues.name: Scully
venues.description: Hip, wood-hued eatery serving artfully plated seasonal flavors from Australia to India & Ireland.

address.formatted: Rex House, 4 St James's Market, London

venues.vicinity: Rex House, 4 St James's Market, London

reviews.text: Attended the London Restaurant Festival event on 17/09/2025. The food was superb! I can’t recommend this restaurant enough. The food was exceptional, the service was amazing and the overall vibe was phenomenal. I will definitely be back!

Scully in St. James’s delivers one of the most exciting dining experiences in London. Every dish bursts with bold, unexpected flavours—think rich spices, clever pickling, and perfect balance. The open kitchen and shelves of colourful ferments set the tone, while the service is warm and knowledgeable.

From bold welcome snacks like spiced chickpeas and tendon crackers with oyster cream to vegetable-driven stars like forbidden rice or a delicate tomato-strawberry-coconut salad, every dish feels thoughtful yet off-beat

A true gem for adventurous food lovers.

Scully, Chef Ramael Scully, born in Malaysia to a mother of Chinese and Indian heritage and an Irish-Balinese father. He grew up in Sydney. Chef Scully brings an array of international influences to his self-titled restaurant; from Malaysia to Sydney via India and China.
The dishes bursted with flavours but with the right balance. I also noticed extensive use of exotic vegetables within the dish itself.
The ambience is casual and relaxed. Service was friendly, attentive and professional.

Had a truly fabulous meal here last night. It is truly impressive how such unusual ingredients are blended to create such exceptional flavours. I also love the relaxed atmosphere. Our favourite main was the hogget. Just wow.  My friend’s 13 year old son hoovered EVERYTHING up. I think that says it all! Well done team!!

Really depends on what you order. The dishes I ordered are extremely delicious, but the ones my partner ordered are genuinely mediocre. The chicken leg is great! Pity that no tasting menu option for lunch.

venues.name: EL&N London
venues.description: Playful pink venue serving all-day brunch, desserts & cakes, plus fancy coffees & mocktails.

reviews.text: Soooo pretty here. Very aesthetic and chill. Great photos and yummy dessert. Stayed there for hours with my friend and daughter. Only down side were the girls toilets were a bit boring compared to the cafe.

The cakes looked great and the menu was extensive. The place was very cute an Instagrammy. The ordering interface with the tablets on the table was fun. All in all, we found the cakes too sweet and sickly. The lattes were good though.

The drinks were good. The French toast only has syrup and fruit, so it tastes like bread with syrup. The bathroom was very dirty and there were food and napkins on the floor. The place was nice and overrated, and it gives the impression that it's dirty. This was 9:00 pm.

Venue: EL&N (Wardour Street)
Date of Visit: 31/10/2025

Great Food, Great Vibes, Great Experience!

I came for an afternoon tea/snack with an acquaintance.

The decor and atmosphere is rather pleasant and customer service was to a high standard. WiFi was available.

Our Order:
- Cafe Latte (Soy Milk)
- Cappuccino (Soy Milk)
- Club Sandwich (Chicken)
- Pistachio Cake Slice
- Fruit Cake Slice (take away)
- Pistachio Croissant

The food arrived within 10 minutes or so

I particularly enjoyed looking at the display of cakes etc by the window but I think they should have some sort of cover rather than being completely in the open, for hygiene reasons

With regards to the food the sandwich was pleasant with a variety of flavours, served at an ideal temperature

The cakes/croissant were the real treat and were truly scrumptious and tasted fresh and full of flavour

I thoroughly enjoyed my visit and would like to visit again.

Please do consider the prices, it's not cheap compared to your standard coffee shops. If you're on a budget you might faint at paying £8.50 for a slice of cake!

Total Paid: £52-53

Overall a great experience 5/5

Another delightful experience. Great quality control, and a place that specialises in desserts. A personal favourite that one has reviewed multiple times across different branches and I appreciate the consistency. I have dined, delivered and taken away and El&N has maintained high standards. I highly recommend it.

venues.name: L'ETO Soho
venues.description: Contemporary cafe-style restaurant serving large breakfast menu, lunch, snacks and dinner.

reviews.text:
L'ETO is offering a large variety of delicious cake such as Honey cake, rasberuy pastery etc. The cakes and pasteries are tasty food but also well decorated and presented. It definitely makes you willing to eat.

There's also a nice choice of warm and cold breakage such as Spanish late... which composted by coffe in ice cubs on which you have to add hot milk and condensed mike. I have to say is pretty nice experience.

The place is nicely decorated and it's cosy. I like this cosy atmosphere with the feeling of movement as it is still pretty popular place.

You will be well served... the staff are nice and friendly.  They are explaining also very well the menu.

I would NOT recommend the Tiramisu... its not the right place for that.

That said this is very nice place and I recommend it.

We had a wonderful experience! The cakes were absolutely delicious and the service was outstanding. Sarah took such great care of us – she was attentive, kind, and made us feel very welcome. Everyone we met was super friendly, which made our visit even more enjoyable. Highly recommended!

Really cool and beautifully decorated dessert shop! The vibe is modern and cozy — perfect for catching up with friends or just enjoying something sweet. We were seated right away as the space is spacious, and there’s an amazing variety of cakes to choose from. The ones we tried were nice! Overall a great spot for cake lovers

Delicious food and excellent service, very whimsical and cosy atmosphere with no pressure to rush and very attentive service, all the staff are so cheerful and friendly and extremely helpful and knowledgeable about the menu, keen to get feedback on customers thoughts and what their favourites are. Sarah was so engaging and enhanced my already enjoyable experience here. I am only sad that you no longer have the saffron latte on the menu! However the saffron dulce de leche delivers every time

I had an absolutely wonderful experience both the food and the service were top-notch. What especially made the evening exceptional was Sarah, one of the staff members. Her warmth and attentiveness shone throughout the meal. She greeted us with a bright smile, was attentive without being overbearing, and really seemed to care that everything was perfect. We will visit again 😇

venues.name: EL&N London
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Promu and Karima were excellent hosts at EL &N. The food was incredible. Very tasty, reasonably priced and quick service. Promu and Karima went out of their way to answer our questions and made us feel very welcome. I recommend EL&N !

The service was very slow. I had to ask the waitress to take my order, and she only came twice: once to accept the order and once to bring the tea. I asked for a cheesecake from their dessert stand, but it never arrived until I reminded her again. My plates were left on the table until I asked for dessert as well. The food itself is good, but the service really needs improvement.

What a lovely space, we had such an amazing waiter Sheik -

The food is absolutely amazing aswell. I don’t regret going there

EL&N London is a trendy and vibrant café. I tried the Spanish Latte, Flat White, Honey Cake, and Lotus Cheesecake — all were delicious and well-prepared. The place was quite busy, both inside and outside, with about a 5-minute wait to get in and another 10 minutes for the order to arrive. Despite the crowd, the overall experience was enjoyable and worth the visit.

Visited 09/09/2025. Kitchen was out of service but customers were not being informed at the door but only when sitting down.

A lovely array of pastries, cakes and sandwiches available on the day I visited. Place was pretty empty inside with a few outside.

The staff I had interacted with were lovely but service was a bit slow, I had to get up and ask someone to take my order and also had to get up to go pay when finished as I needed to leave. Doesn't appear to be very well managed (albeit on a less busy day with the kitchen out of order!)

Had the Turkey and Cheese ciabatta, it was nice and cost £11.

Will have to go back to try their main menu/cooked items.

Everything is halal.

venues.name: Scarlett Green
venues.description: Buzzy, bi-level cafe & restaurant drawing on elevated Antipodean-inspired cuisine & drinks.

reviews.text:
This place is amazing with tasty food!
Everything we order was so delicious!! The perfect place for brunch and more.
Coffee is excellent!
Stephane made our experience the best! Such a great person, we felt welcomed.

Nice decor.. didn't have a reservation but they allowed walkins. It wasn't busy yet too. Stopped in for a quick drink and bite. We had bites from the menu and it was out of this world filled of flavour with really high quality ingredients used. I had their own old fashioned drink and there were small coconut bits in the ice. The shrimp was absolutely tasty as well as the chicken and the choux bun filled with cheese and Vegemite.

My Daughter & I came here for breakfast last year twice & this year twice. We wouldn’t go anywhere else. The food is just amazing! Our favourite are Pancakes, banana bread & sweetcorn fritters. We wish there was one in Cheshire & Manchester!

Bumped into this place merely because the high rating it already had and voila! No wonder Scarlett Green received such rating because it’s really that great. Great food, ambience, service. 7 stars if I could 😍

Delicious and creative food, beautifully presented in a stylish and well-designed space. The location is really cool, and the staff is absolutely wonderful – friendly, attentive, and welcoming. Also worth mentioning: the tea is excellent. A place I’d definitely recommend!

venues.name: LUMI Camden
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the vibrant atmosphere of Camden, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Impeccable service - they went above and beyond to ensure we had the booth so we were comfortable with a toddler. Staff were hospitable and happy which is a rarity these days.
Had the Chicken and waffles (majority of the menu is all halal too), pancakes and french toast - all came hot, quickly and tasted great. Chicken and waffles were crispy, not overly sweet or sickly.
Pancakes were very soft and fluffy.

Makel was friendly and ensured we had a great visit.

Would definitely be visiting again!

Excellent little restaurant! The food was beautiful and delicious (we had the granola and the eggs Benedict) and the vibe was great. Everyone was friendly and we were seated quickly even though there was a queue. I’ll come back next time I’m in town.

Absolutely loved this brunch spot. The pancakes were soft and fluffy with strawberries, bananas and rich pistachio sauce. The chicken and waffles were crispy on the outside and tender inside, perfectly paired with egg and sauce. The juices were beautiful and refreshing. The place has a cozy vibe with greenery and rustic brick walls, perfect for a relaxing and photo-friendly morning.

Not only are the dishes delicious, they are served with care and attention to plating. Eggs were perfectly cooked, runny and jammy. We enjoyed this place so much that we came back twice. Portions are perfect for the price.

Service was friendly and food was served hot and reasonably quickly. The coffee and hot beverages are also really good. Plenty of seating on the main floor and even more seating downstairs. Clean restrooms.

This place is an absolute gem for brunch. The restaurant’s atmosphere, beautifully presented dishes and drinks, together with their service make for an unforgettable experience. If you are visiting Camden Market, it is worth the short walk to enjoy the food and experience.

venues.name: Victoria House Coffee & Food
venues.description: Quaint cafe featuring global brunch plates & Indian-inspired dinner dishes, plus outdoor tables.

reviews.text: We came here for a late afternoon brunch and had an outstanding experience. We ordered an iced dirty chai and a sparkling elderflower mocktail as drinks, and we got the country omelette and the rooty frooty fresh and fruity waffle as mains. Everything tasted great, and the waffle was notably one of the most aesthetically pleasing and delicious waffles I’ve ever had. The presentation was simply breathtakingly beautiful. The staff was very friendly and attentive, and we would definitely come back again when we’re in London!

Loved the food here, very flavorful and tasty. The place is popular for all the right reasons. The service was super warm. Even though there was a long queue for the restaurant, the staff was very polite in dealing with people waiting outside. The service was fast and swift. Knowing they could fit more people because of the rush, they still didnt push people to eat quickly or even order quickly. That was very nice and speak volumes about the values of the restaurant. Highly recommend going here, especially try shakshuka it was super good.

We arrived just as they were opening and without a reservation but they seated us right away and took our order, two traditional full English breakfasts. We were served within minutes and everything was absolutely delicious! The atmosphere is energetic but not chaotic. We will certainly visit again on any subsequent trips to London!
Nice service and very polite staff. The food was good, delicious explosion pancakes. The burrata toast anneggs benedict tasted so good. Good atmosphere and clean place. We’ll be back!
