From the window, everything looked and smelled delicious, and it was! It was very difficult to choose what to eat because everything looked delicious. The chocolate bar and cappuccino were delicious! A special mention for the friendly and warm service I received.

I came across this cozy little café back in February. It looked so inviting and warm that I stepped inside, and the staff were incredibly kind, even recommending their favourites and a little backstory of the cafe. I’m not usually a coffee drinker, so I went for a hot chocolate, and it was absolutely stunning. Looking forward to my next visit when I’m back in London!

After being recommended this location by a friend, I'd made a point to visit it for a weekly treat when possible around my lectures in the autumn/winter. The staff was always nice, and though the goods could maybe be considered expensive, you absolutely get your money's worth! Everything I have had here has not only been well made and decadent, but filling too. Lovely place!

venues.name: Fortitude Bakehouse
venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Stopped here somewhat recently on a whim. Super busy! They have a really great selection available - We both had one of the beignets, which were very tasty but I think they could've been a bit more generous with the toppings for the price, service was quick and friendly, will definitely be back again if we're in the area.

The street it’s located on, along with the overall vibe and style of the place, was really charming. The coffee was excellent. The baked goods we tried were tasty, though the savory ones we chose were a bit too oily for our liking. As for the sweet option, it was nice, but we would have preferred it without the chocolate sauce. Overall, it’s a lovely spot with a cozy atmosphere, definitely worth a visit.

It’s definitely an “Instagram” spot - everything was oversized and well made. The proportions of the pastries were a bit off, aka not enough pastry to sausage roll or croissant to chocolate ratio.
Plenty of options means there is something for everyone, but I do believe this is one of those over hyped places

I WANT TO GIVE FORTITUDE 10000 STARS!!! My fav bakery in town. Always come for the feta & spinach. Other recommendation is the almond croissant!

Better to come before 11.

The coffee is also amazing. Vanilla latte with oat milk.
High prices for high quality goods! Did not disappoint in the slightest. Lovely flavours and light pastry for both sweet and savoury items. Benches to sit out the front, no toilets available.

venues.name: Beigel Bake
venues.description: 24-hour bakery known for traditional Jewish-style filled bagels such as salt beef and smoked salmon.

reviews.text: Honestly the best place for beigels!!! The salt beef-gherkin-mustard combo is always my favourite, but even a plain cream cheese beigel here is amazing. The texture of the beigel is just simply the best. Never fail to pop in here whenever I’m back in London!

I happened to pass by and saw that there was a long line of people, and because it was a Sunday I chose to come two days later when there were fewer people and at a more convenient time. On the one hand, the saleswoman didn't understand that I asked for the 'house dish', on the other hand, the bib sandwich was full of tender meat and was delicious. I enjoyed it very much and will go back there again.

Decent bagel at this bakery that is an institution in London. I had a salt beef beigel with extra of pickles. There is a good amount of meat in the beigel per serving . Meat is not dry and it’s flavoursome. Service was fast (I was not stuck in a queue). I would say if you are in the area looking for something to eat /after a night out this is your best bet. Good value for money.

It’s been quite a while since I’ve last been here and tried the Salt beef bagel. It was lunch time and as usual there’s the typical queue (full of tourists), the turnover was quick so I was served in a few minutes.

Sadly, it seems they have changed some components of the salt beef bagel. The mustard that was usually my favourite part was subtle and flat, missing its usual strong kick. The pickles weren’t as punchy neither with the salt beef being lukewarm. Overall it was underwhelming. It was tasty, but it did not live up to what I had remembered a few years back.

We went back twice for the salt beef bagel and sandwich after trying it the first time—it was absolutely incredible! The meat was melt-in-your-mouth tender, and the bagel was perfectly fresh. We stood in line but didn’t have to wait long, even when it's busy, the service is impressively efficient. The salmon cream cheese option was tasty too, but if you're visiting, don’t miss the salt beef bagel or sandwich—it's a must try!

venues.name: Chestnut Bakery, Covent Garden
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Wonderful assortment of pastries but the ones we ordered were just alright, nothing mindblowing. A little too sweet for our liking. Soft serve with honey toast was an interesting offer that we don’t see many in other cafes/bakeries so it was lovely. Wanted the vanilla flavour soft serve but it was sold out so I had the chocolate one which was decent. The honey toast that came with it was a little too sweet and dry though. It’s a lovely place with great vibes for a coffee with a friend, to rest your legs after some shopping in central London but not specifically be there for the baked goods. Menu offers breakfast/brunch type of food I have yet to try but I’ll probably skip that. Staff were extremely helpful and kind though. Made us feel really welcomed despite being so busy.

We sat upstairs right by the window with the scenic view of the street. The pastries were each made to be a perfect image of itself. The labneh cherry tomato toasty was the best savory breakfast sandwich you can ask for to be balanced with the sweetness of the blueberry tart - which is easy to miss, but not in Chestnut - every bite you get fresh blueberries and never a jammy sticking to your teeth goo, but a wonderful creamy filling encased by the more exquisite laminated dough.
Not one miss!

Came in just before 6. There wasn’t any seating downstairs expect a small table near the entrance which we had to sit there was four of us. Even though the cafe was open we was told upstairs seating was closed. Wanted the Karak tea which wasn’t available, either was the brookie. Ordered two scoops of ice cream which I asked for choc. Then I see one of the guys giving vanilla asked the lady that was serving me that I asked for choc which she said there wasn’t any available even though she took my order. She wasn’t paying attention as she kept repeating my order. As we sat with our hot choc and the basic vanilla ice cream. We can see the bins getting taken out, everything getting cleared up. There was still people coming in. Considering we were in convent garden and you pay more than average I don’t expect to see huge bins going past me multiple times, aswell everything getting cleared up. The cafe is open and should accommodate accordingly during the opening hours. Won’t be coming in a hurry anytime soon.

Chestnut Bakery in Covent Garden has quickly become one of my favorite spots in London for pastries and coffee. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, with a modern yet cozy design that makes it perfect for a relaxed break during a busy day in the city.
The staff are friendly, which adds to the overall experience and makes you feel at home even in the middle of a busy area like Covent Garden.
The highlight for me is definitely their tiramisu Danish. It’s unlike anything I’ve tried before. It feels indulgent without being overly sweet, and it’s the kind of pastry you’ll think about long after you’ve left. I honestly would come back just for that one item.
They also offer a wide selection of baked goods, The coffee is consistently good too, which makes it a perfect pairing with any pastry. I also appreciate that everything feels fresh, and the presentation of the pastries makes it hard to choose just one. The place is great whether you want to sit inside and enjoy the calm atmosphere or grab something to take away while exploring Covent Garden.
What’s exciting is that Chestnut Bakery also has another branch in Riyadh, so it’s great to see them bringing their unique style and quality to different parts of the world.
If you’re in Covent Garden and looking for a bakery that goes beyond the usual, I highly recommend Chestnut Bakery.

Top notch bakery, cute, great baked goods, and just super tasty. All the pastries were buttery, especially the croissant. The zataar knot was fantastic, especially with a bit of labneh. The pistachio croissant was sweet, but not sugary. Overall just great, the service was a bit too slow though.

venues.name: The Dusty Knuckle Bakery
venues.description: Light cafe fare such as creative sandwiches & salads with coffee drinks & fresh breads to-go.

reviews.text:
so yum! ive had this bakery on my radar for a while now, and it was so worth the wait to come along.
whilst £11 is obviously a lot for a sandwich, you 100% get what you pay for. The homemade bread was absolutely lovely and the sandwich was packed full of flavourful filling.
the atmosphere was lovely, and sitting outside was great. service was brilliant and hardly a wait for my food either. i came at about 12 o’clock and didn’t have to queue, however when i left at 12:40 there was a large queue, so definitely get there a bit earlier if you want a sandwich! they deserve the popularity though, i absolutely loved this bakery.

After being recommended this bakery I was eager to visit and it didn't disappoint.

Maybe one of the largest bakeries you'll ever visit, hidden down the end of a back lane with extensive outdoor seating it's a great spot for brunch or lunch on the weekend just be prepared to que.

I visited on a Saturday and waited no more than a couple of minutes and tried two of my favourite UK stallwards the Morning Roll (chai spiced sugar dusted cruffin) and the go-to Honey and Feta swirl which was laden with sesame and poppy seeds and was absolutely banging!

All their pastries and bread looked top tier. Flaky lamination and a deep caramel crust on all their sourdough (just the way I like it!)

The breakfast sando looked unreal, and is clearly a top seller for good reason.

I look forward to my next visit to try the rest!

Keep up the good work team! 🤘

Unbeatable breads, amazing sandwiches, and really creative options! The queue this past July 6th weekend was wild, but worth it! We waited in the queue about 20 minutes until we ordered, but there were plenty of tables and we were able to sit 4 of us at a table inside. Despite the crowds, service was so fast! Our sandwiches + drinks arrived within 8-10 minutes of ordering and were of course, the best in London.

It’s the first time I’ve seen it this busy, but even with the queue, these baked goods are always worth it.

Best sandwich I’ve ever had! If you want the focaccia sandwiches then you need to come at 11:30! The till doesn’t take payments for the order unless it is exactly 11:30 and after. Takeaway orders are collected outside of the shop.

Although I’m not a big fan of coronation chicken, but they’ve done very well at combining different ingredients, crunchy nuts, herbs, green apple slices, not to mention the airy and flavourful sour dough potato bread, I can see why people queue up here for food.

The only downside to me is that the place gets so busy and it can be crowded. Also as a first time visitor, there’s not much guidance on what to do, you just sort of figure it out. The location for me was a little hard to find, you walk down the alleyway and it is the shop to your right, the name of the shop wasn’t visible unless you step opposite the shop.

I had the pleasure of visiting The Dusty Knuckle in Dalston for breakfast today, and it was an experience worth sharing. Nestled in the Abbot Street Car Park, this café offers a unique blend of industrial charm and warm hospitality.​

I opted for the Egg, Chilli Cheese on focaccia with a side of bacon. The sandwich was a delightful fusion of spicy pickled green chillies, spring onions, and fresh coriander, all between slices of soft focaccia.

Their sourdough bread is renowned, and the pastries—ranging from morning buns to cinnamon rolls—are simply irresistible. The open-plan kitchen allows patrons to witness the baking process firsthand, adding to the authenticity of the experience. ​They also have bakery classes going on simultaneously!

Beyond the food, The Dusty Knuckle stands out for its mission to empower at-risk youth through mentorship and employment opportunities. This dedication to community enrichment adds a meaningful layer to the overall experience. ​

The seating area, both indoors and outdoors, offers ample space, making it suitable for individuals, families, and groups. Be prepared for popularity, especially during peak hours, but the quality of food and service makes any wait worthwhile.​ ❤️

1. Egg chilli cheese focaccia with bacon - £9.8

2. Hot chocolate - £4.5
3. Bacon Sarnie - £8.5

venues.name: COMMON BREADS
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
The cheese manakish, musakhan, and spinach pies were absolutely incredible. The owner manages the restaurant himself, and the location is just perfect. I truly congratulate him and wish him even more success and new branches in the future.

You can actually ask them to make the pastries in a small size for takeaway — they were absolutely delicious, arrived hot and fresh, and perfectly clean. Truly amazing!

We recently hosted a work event and chose Common Breads for the catering. From start to finish, the experience was exceptional. They tailored our order perfectly, offering a wide variety of options to suit everyone’s preferences. The food was outstanding — fresh, delicious, and of the highest quality — and the service was just as impressive.

Our team and guests were genuinely impressed, and it made the event feel extra special. I would wholeheartedly recommend Common Breads to anyone looking for catering that combines quality, variety, and excellent service.

The chicken musakhan manouche was the best dish - highly recommended. The other dishes were alright. Worth a try but nothing to rave about.

Service is great and staff are friendly.

Got some quick bites on a weekday evening. Loved the ambience, decor and the layout. It was quiet when I went and the perfect spot to read.

The food and service is lovely, would love to come back to try more items on the menu.

Every visit is perfect! the food is always fresh, flavorful, and truly the best Lebanese in the city. Their oat chai is unmatched, and the owner ( Kamal) is so warm and welcoming. Clean, professional, 10/10.I’d love to see them open more locations.

venues.name: Bageriet
venues.description: Compact Nordic bakery & cafe with traditional Swedish cakes and pastries to eat in or take away.

reviews.text: As a Swedish Londoner this place will always have a warm place in my heart!! I also had the most wonderful few shifts working here just before Covid started, and got to learn about how everything’s made on the premisses! Can’t recommend enough if you want some authentic Swedish cinnamon buns 💕

They are comparable to any bakery in Stockholm👌 they even make the princess cake. It is pretty small, but the atmosphere is cosy. The pastries were delicious, but the pistachio one was a little too sweet for me. The coffee can be improved.

Wow!! What a selection, what a bakers, what customer service!! I ordered a special cake and 48hrs it was ready to collect and the engraving I asked for, perfectly done, just as I asked for! Would recommend any day, even just for a visit to see (or sample) the cakes!

We visited this cute and cosy bakery for breakfast. They have different kinds of Swedish pastries, cookies and cakes. Everything looks so delicious that it is quite hard to make a decision. Great and varied tea selection. The staff is very polite and helpful and overall good ambients with perfect lighting and music.

Service was warm and friendly, recommending which pastries to try.

Notgrotta (Extra buttery shortbread with hazelnut chocolate) indeed had a buttery crumbly melt in your mouth tart base with molten chocolate within.

Josefin (Almond tart with orange) had a nice balance of almond (not artificial taste) and refreshing orange.

The cinnamon bun, which I thought would be the highlight, was quite disappointing. Not as fluffy as I thought it would be. And a bit too much cinnamon.

venues.name: Miel Bakery
venues.description: Cosy, classic French bakery offering housemade breads, pastries & seasonal tarts, plus hot drinks.

reviews.text: I wanted to love this bakery but I felt my almond croissant was a little too sweet. It was well filled and the pastry was extra buttery. The cinnamon buns looked amazing here so I would come back to try. Only two outdoor seats for seating. Pastries range from £3.5-£6 so some are definitely on the premium priced side. My almond croissant was £4.50.

As we were eating our croissants outside an older lady walked past and blared out “I can’t just walk past, I have to get one”. And it makes sense once you try one. Delicious heavenly croissants. This is an exceptional bakery offering a range of both sweet and savory croissants.
A truly lovely local bakery with amazing pastries. Out of the oven fresh, all absolutely delicious made with fresh and quality ingredients. Their coffee is also phenomenal.

The worker made our experience greater than expected! Friendly and helpful worker. We loved the Flat White and Iced Hojicha. Nice and quiet place (we were there around 3-4pm). Overall experience is 5/5 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟! Will definitely come back.

Amazing bakery. My favourite in London! All the classic French pastries are delicious! Don’t miss their pain au chocolat, kouign amann, banana bread and the daily special square croissants. The coffee is also great :)

venues.name: Maison Bertaux
venues.description: 19th-century, French patisserie and tea rooms with marble-topped tables, plus art gallery spaces.

reviews.text: Yummy pastries and busy workers!! Recommend rosehip tea 🌹and the mixed fruit 🍓cheesecake and the raspberry tart. Both were light and creamy. ✨🤍SO good!! We got 6 pastries and two pots of tea. 🫖That FILLED the four of us up and filled the table as well!! 100% recommend if you want a cheaper afternoon tea with more bang for your buck. 💷💥

4.5/5.
I cannot get over the scones and the collated cream and the fresh berry tart. Especially the latter. The creme inside was divine. The outer whipped cream is so light and airy. The dessert itself is perfectly sweet. Not cloying, not un-satisfying. Just perfect. With the freshest assortment of berries. Their hot chocolate is comforting, especially on a cold day. The service is good, there is seating. Would definitely visit this place many, many times to try everything they have on their menu. Outstanding stuff!

Scones were very good. Very big piece and very generous with the jam and clotted cream. At first we were hesitant as the scone was not heated up but it was still very very good, especially with the tea! We also had the berry tart which was very refreshing. Price was reasonable, 40 pounds for 3 scones, 1 tart, and 2 teas. Would come back again!

Such a cute little shop!
A kind grandpa warmly introduced all the items to us.
We came especially to try their scones—served with traditional clotted cream and jam, they were super crispy and delicious.
Highly recommend the fruit-flavored ones—they’re so good!
The staff even thoughtfully reminded us to keep an eye on our belongings and phones.
Sitting inside with a gentle breeze and enjoying these classic British treats—totally worth it!
Absolutely delightful! The pastries are fresh, beautifully crafted, and full of authentic French flavor. A must-visit for anyone with a sweet tooth. 🥐✨

venues.name: Chestnut Bakery, Belgravia
venues.description: International breads, pastries & sandwiches featured in a high-end bakery & cafe setup.

reviews.text:
Wonderful place to kick start the day. My favorite Chestnut Bakery branch in a very beautiful and aesthetic area of the city (posh 😅). Big selection of sweet and savory pastries plus the breakfast dishes, you can’t go wrong here. Service was very good and staff were welcoming and helpful. Don’t miss their crispy cinnamon roll.
Highly recommended 👍🏼

Stopped by Chestnut Bakery and was pleasantly surprised! I had an Americano and their Chicken Club Sandwich – and both were spot on. The sandwich was especially impressive – packed with flavour, and the melted cheese took it to another level. Fresh ingredients, warm and satisfying – honestly one of the best chicken clubs I’ve had in a while.

The coffee was smooth and well-balanced, perfect with the meal. Cozy atmosphere and friendly staff made the experience even better. Definitely recommend if you’re in the area – a great spot for a quick bite or relaxed coffee break.

The flatbreads are to die for. Haven’t tried the pastry yet but I imagine they’re good as they sell out quickly! Service is so kind. I will say, probably not the place to go if you’re in a rush as the workers will give you plenty of space.

Lovely place, clean, bright and specious, the waiters where lovely and quick to respond, the almond pastry ordered were beautifully presented and I loved the coffee
I couldn't eat there as they had nothing gluten free but my daughter said it was tasty. I did appreciate the loveliness of the place .

We paid on like with a QR code and the invoice was sent to my email, the total for coffee and pastry came to £10.97 a tad on the expensive side (Lovely or not..)❤️

This bakery was surprisingly nice: amazing atmosphere, delicious menu and great service.
Our server, Nejd, has been very helpful and welcoming with us and our requests. Outstanding menu, great vegetarian options and vast choices of sweet and savory food.
Scandi atmosphere with wood interior design, lots of white and cream color, lighting completes everything.
We’ll definitely be back!

venues.name: Arôme Bakery - Duke Street
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
I got two strawberry tarts with vanilla cream as I was told it was their last day and a chocolate and pear tarte.

Strawberry tarte is very delicate and crumbly, the strawberries were nice and ripe, cream was more like a vanilla flavoured whipped cream than custard and the tarte base was very buttery. Very delicious for first two bites but then it gets boring and dull. I’d split it with 2/3 people as it get sickly after some time.

I had high hopes for chocolate and pear tarte as autumn is a season of the pear and the apple. It was disappointing. Pear layer is thinner or the same as chocolate but the chocolate ganache is so thick that it’s overpowering every flavour. If you want to taste any pear you need to separate cause it’s too delicate too fight the strong and thick layer of ganache. Flavours don’t balance each other out. The chocolate layer is a thick overkill that becomes a blip of chocolate in the mouth.

Matcha was nice but quite small.

The team working didn’t care about being there and if asked any questions about the pastries they couldn’t be more uninterested. It seems the popularity of the place makes them confident in not caring about people coming there. Which is a shame considering the prices and that in this climate it would be a treat for most to go to a place like this.

I bought two strawberry tarts and one chocolate and pear one + matcha.

In total I spent £26.20. I would not come back tbh.

On an extremely hot day, the Iced Citrus Black was absolutely perfect super refreshing! I also tried two desserts: the first was the café’s signature Honey Toast, and the other was a Coffee Cheesecake. I didn’t expect much from the cheesecake, but it turned out to be really delicious highly recommended! As for the Honey Toast, it was okay, but not amazing for me. The sweetness level was fine, but the toast itself was a bit on the dry side.

Possibly better than their other bakery in Covent Garden. Different options available here and all taste incredible. The chocolate and banana croissant is one of the best things I’ve ever put in my mouth - will keep
coming back just for this. Their coffee isn’t bad either.

Arome Bakery has a lovely vibe, stylish, warm, and inviting. The coffee was great, and the butter toast was absolutely delicious: perfectly crisp and rich. The sausage croissant was a bit ordinary, but still enjoyable. Overall, a great place to unwind and treat yourself to something tasty

The croissant with banana, chocolate and almond paste was pretty good. Overall this bakery has a lot of nice looking desserts, I can recommend it. The place is pretty small inside and is usually crowded given its touristic location

venues.name: TOAD Bakery
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
The line is long but it moves relatively
quickly! The pastries are delicious and fresh - get the kalamansi and coconut iced bun, this was cheap but delicious, cornbread croissant was savoury but could’ve done with more jalepeno, plum danish was ok, and the everything bagel croissant was delicious! Tastes just like a bagel, but in croissant form so it’s super buttery and flakey.

The least favourite was the Jaffa cake, texture was a bit too dense.

Would queue again!

This was a very nice pastry, and to be honest they seemed to have tonnes of great options. It was delicious! My only gripe with this place is that the queue was mental - I was in it for 45 minutes. I have no issue with a place being popular but the queue was barely moving which was slightly frustrating.

The line was sooooo long and you look at it, and think is it worth it for a bakery??

And let me tell you… it is SO worth it. I truly believe this is the best bakery in London and is worth every single person in line waiting for pastries. We ordered so much and enjoyed every last bite. They had a collab at the time and we had a beef curry pastry which was fab. The pastry just tasted incredible, the different savoury and sweet options were an added bonus.
Great place. Sometimes you need to wait for quite a while but its worth the wait. Lovely pastries, lots to choose from: both sweet and savoury. Go there!!

Legitimately my favourite bakery in London because of their friendly, neighbourhood welcome, their interesting experimenting with bakery products and of course everything is excellent. I can highly recommend their sandwiches as well as the cakes on offer!

venues.name: Maya’s Bakehouse
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Amazing little bakery, we tried the cinnamon+cardamon bun, the chimichurri bun and the basque cheesecake! All were immense and will definitely be returning!! Lovely staff as well who even cut our pastries in half so we could try them all in the store 🫶🏻
I’m so glad that finally right time walking by and get the coffee and bun from Maya’s ! Bun is very delicious, favorite so far in Lambeth area !

This is hands down the best bakery in London. Baked goods are out of this world. Flavour combinations are chic, original and absolutely delicious. I wish they didn’t run out of things so quickly. I guess that is just a testament to their craft and quality over quantity approach.
Amazing seeded sourdough, cardamom bun and mince pie! Great coffee too and they also have a grocery corner with amazing produce. Will definitely come back!

Freshly baked pastries,bread, and cookies.
We also tried the basque cheese cake , and it tasted amazing.
Only opens from
Wednesday to Saturday.
Highly recommended ❤️

venues.name: GAIL's Bakery Soho
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Amazing food. We had baked eggs with streaky bacon with toast soldiers. It was so good. No lactose free milk though. Oat or soy only.

What an excellent little cafe. The drinks and pastries are fantastic and the service is very warm and friendly. The cafe in itself is small but cosy and I will certainly be purchasing from other branches too.

I went out of my way to visit as id seen some good reviews.
They were a bit limited and what they did have wasn't exciting me in terms of cake.
I did get what looked like a cinnamon bun in a mushroom shape and with chocolate in.
It was dry . Barely any chocolate.
It was a disappointment.
Some of the savoury food looked lovely.
No steps to get in.
Some seating available.
Near Oxford street.
I don't think I'd try again
Quaint spot. Amazing baked good! And delicious porridge. Comfort food on an autumn morning. 💖

The service is amazing. We liked the hospitality.
The manager (Anass) is very friendly with customers and professional.

venues.name: Dunn's Bakery
venues.description: Long-running local bakery offering bread, sandwiches, traditional pastries and celebration cakes.

reviews.text: We frequent Dunn’s so it was only fitting to order a Dunn’s cake for our wedding. We were not disappointed! Turned out exactly as we imagined and tasted delicious. We barely got to eat any, as guests loved it so much they had finished it off entirely by the end of the reception (photos by our lovely photographer @elvira_azimova)

Australian’s love their sausage rolls served hot, often with ketchup, so it was very exciting to not only see these beauties in the hot oven BUT ALSO for the ketchup to be put INSIDE THE SAUSAGE ROLL when we asked for sauce. What is this SORCERY (saucery🤭)? I don’t know but I didn’t mess about to find out. Acquired and devoured in minutes. Pure magic! 😋🤤👏 Vegan sausage rolls also available.

Dunn's Bakery is a reliable spot for a quick bite or fresh loaf of bread when you're in the neighborhood. While they might not be the most extraordinary bakery in town, they consistently deliver decent quality. We've never had a bad experience, so they're always a safe bet for a satisfying treat.

The apple fritter made me feel like a kid again. The review is based on many products I ve tried over the years and the price tag that comes with it. Everything is always fresh and service is quick. Sandwiches are delicious and very well bellow the average market price. For the size of this bakery the variety and quality is impressive.

I had a lovely time at Dunn's Bakery, enjoying coffee and cake outdoors with a friend. The atmosphere was relaxed, and cakes tasted great. A small mishap happened when my paper cup broke and some coffee spilled. To my surprise, one of the shop assistants noticed from inside and immediately came out to offer me a new cup—without me even needing to ask. Although I had already poured the coffee into my own bottle and didn't need the replacement, I truly appreciated his attentiveness and quick response.

It’s also worth noting that during these challenging times of inflation, Dunn’s continues to provide excellent service, employing at least four shop assistants at the front desk to ensure customers are well taken care of. That shows strong commitment from the owner to both staff and customers. Overall, a warm and thoughtful experience—thank you, Dunn’s!

venues.name: Don't Tell Dad
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
We had a fantastic evening at Don’t Tell Dad! Some real standouts were the truffle beignets, and the mozzarella with chard and pine nuts, which had a lovely garlicky finish. The venison was rich, and the liver parfait paired with it was even richer - the plum jam really cut through beautifully. The chilli butter greens and pomme Anna were also delicious.

The cocktails were interesting (especially the Cynar Sour), and the wine was a real highlight. We tried a grape we’d never had before, Nosiola, and loved it.

Service was quick, personable, friendly, and chatty.

Tell everyone… except your dad!

We visited on a Sunday, and there was a very long queue for the pastries. The wait was worth it though. We tried a few pastries, and they were absolutely delicious with amazing flavours and just the right amount of sweetness. The texture was perfect too — soft and fresh. There’s also a dining area with a nice ambiance, though the prices are on the higher side.

I went there last night to celebrate my birthday and I was not disappointed. I couldn’t have wished for better. Every single detail, from the welcoming atmosphere to the thoughtful service and the beautifully prepared food, made the evening unforgettable. It wasn’t just a meal, it felt like a true celebration. I couldn’t have imagined a better place to mark such a special occasion, and I’m deeply grateful for the genuine care and warmth that made the night so memorable. Thank you!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Loved Don’t Tell Dad! The street it’s on has such a great vibe and the interior design is spot on. Extra points for having Chicago the Musical playing in the toilets – absolutely epic.

Food was brilliant. Bit gutted they’d run out of bread because I really wanted to try it, but my lamb was honestly to die for. Everything felt really well thought out and properly crafted.

What sets this place apart is that while loads of London restaurants are basically good home cooking at restaurant prices, this is proper restaurant food. Can’t wait to go back and try the bakery next time!

Loveliest peach danish I’ve ever had, and the coffee was perfectly balanced 10/10. The queue for pastries on the weekend is insane but weekdays are a better bet! Def recommended for a cafe/bite in Queen’s Park.

venues.name: Patisserie Sainte Anne
venues.description: Cosy, colourful French bakery with classic breads and pastries, cakes, macarons and chocolates.

reviews.text: Absolutely divine baked goods and drinks here! I’ve had the pain au chocolat- the chocolate is rich and the pastry is so buttery you can literally taste every flake and fold. It’s addictive. I’ve come back every day since my first one. Their mille-feuille? Unreal. The filling is creamy, custardy perfection- honestly, if I had a bucket and spoon, I’d live off it. Everything here just feels so decadent. The coffee is smooth and silky too — none of that bitter aftertaste you get at the big chains. And the staff are genuinely lovely — one of them even took the time to tell me how they make the croissants, which made me appreciate it even more. The place itself is adorable, cozy, and aesthetic — and being right across from work is dangerously convenient.

Everything I have had from here has been excellent and the kouign-amann aux pommes is always superb, I have had many 😋

I'd go so far as to say their kouign-amann aux pommes is the best pastry in London! Right up there with Habanos cigars and Scotch whiskey for pure pleasure of consumption 😃

Really disappointed with the apricot tart I bought recently — the base was undercooked and not up to the standard we’ve come to expect. This used to be our favourite spot, and we truly hope the new owners can live up to the high standards set before…

We lived in Hammersmith several years ago and then the place was our favourite- not a day without their fab baguette, not a weekend without their amazing desserts (you would enjoy each and every from the menu!) A magnificent taste of real France on the bank of River Thames it was then! Then we moved and only rarely I had a chance to pop in and buy as much as I could to enjoy these treats as long as possible!.. But my two recent visits really shocked me: not a baguette, not a single piece of dessert or tart was the same as before!?! That’s how I discovered what I actually started to suspect: the new owner. Thus - a totally new place, taste and aftertaste…
Now I know why I don’t have to take this long trip to this once a gem of Hammersmith: a very average quality of every dessert, a very poor quality of pastries (croissant shouldn’t be called that name here anymore…) and bread (brioche is anything but a brioche here now…)
I agree with other reviews, that new owners were too bold to keep the same price level for their products, but the worse thing is, that they also are trying to cut down their expenses by using lower quality (or quantity) of the ingredients.
But more importantly, I agree with the statement , that you can’t use the history of this place as your own, you have to clearly tell customers, that you are new there and just TRYING to keep this place as good as it once was…
Adieu, Patisserie Saint Anna

UPDATE. Received a response from the owner today: “Fake review”,. Sorry, guys, but this one is not fake. As a proof, adding a photo of my yesterday dessert (couldn’t finish it, sorry…). Use to love it so much, but now it has lots of lumps in it, so no pleasure of eating that at all…

One bite is all it all took to realise the pastries have changed and for worse!

Been a regular for last 2 years, sadly my hunt for my favourite neighbourhood patisserie begins again 🥲

Update 13.07 - tried again and still the same. Meanwhile, AI has also been put to great use by the new owners as they simply don’t have time to read and respond to criticism. Next time don’t forget to delete the AI prompts before replying to customers :)

venues.name: Fabrique Bakery Hoxton
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Love this bakery… sweetest people and the best cinnamon and cardamom buns. The cardamom bun is like a soft hug, reminds me of Iraqi kleicha 🥹♥️

The place is known for there cinnamon bun - and they deserve the reputation.

I tried there famous cinnamon bun. It is slightly chewy, feels glazed with some crispy sugar crystals on the top. Perfect way to start a Sunday.  Only downside: could’ve have been slightly more moist, but likely personal preference here.

Likely one of the best cinnamon buns in the city.
I loved the ambiance of eating right in the working area/kitchen, so lovely and lively. The 2 nut pastries we had were fantastic, plus the flaky croissant was delicious. I can’t wait to go back.

A taste of Stockholm in London! A really lovely, cosy bakery in Hoxton. We arrived at noon and all of the cinnamon buns had gone and there were only a few things left but what we did have was lovely. Soft, chewy buns and great cardamom flavour. Tasty coffee too. On the expensive side but friendly and nice seating in the sunshine too!

Good morning from a lovely little corner, suitable for grabbing a coffee and breakfast on the way and if you have time to sit down for a drink and a bite to eat in peace.  The smiling and friendly young people of the staff will put you in a good mood, and the food and drinks will give you the strength to overcome the stress of everyday life.
I've been living 5 minutes from the cafe for a month now, but I'm always in a rush for the overground and it never occurred to me to look to the right where Fabrique is. Take a look because the quality of the items on offer is definitely worth it ❤️.
Buying a surprise bag from the To Good to Go app brought me here.  Exactly for 3.39 you get your breakfast and bread...delicious, like homemade and tempting (despite my diet :))
Enjoy ❤️ I recommend!

venues.name: The Buttery
venues.description: Lime Tree Hotel’s charming cafe with elevated breakfast & lunch, plus cocktails & garden seating.

address.formatted: Lime Tree Hotel, 135-137 Ebury St, London

venues.vicinity: Lime Tree Hotel, 135-137 Ebury St, London

reviews.text:
Such a nice back yard to have a brunch. The staff was lovely.
The food was really tasty, however the service was not so quick, we waited a really long time for our food to be served. Moreover both of us ordered something with poached eggs and one egg on each plate was hard boiled.

Absolutely loved my experience at the buttery ! The atmosphere is relaxing and beautifully designed, but what really stood out was the exceptional service. The manager Artan was incredibly welcoming, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect from start to finish. You can tell they truly care about customer satisfaction. Highly recommended!
Beautiful and cozy. If you want to be seated in the garden, you should reserve a table ahead of time! Coffee is excellent, the food itself is just normal, not too amazing.

Very tasty food and coffee.
We sat in the restaurant itself which was fine, the garden is probably way prettier.  Amazing eggs royal, probably best I had in London.
Restaurant is on the pricier side though.
Loved it!! One of the cutest brunch spots. If you’re looking for a relaxed place in a calm, charming area, this is the perfect match.

venues.name: Paradise Green
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Really great food, options for more healthy or vegan options if required, but they have proper hearty mains too. The chicken parmigiana was delicious. We were seated around the front which to start with was a bit cold and breezy every time the front door was opened but it eventually was ok.

The first waiter that we saw was very abrupt when talking to my sister, and taking the order from her. He was fine with me but seemed to have a different attitude with my sister.
I think equality and diversity needs to be taught to this particular waiter.
Other than that the food was great, and the second waiter was very friendly.

Gorgeous space, service was lovely. Enjoyed  my last meal of my trip to London here and it was beautiful, however it felt a bit pricey for what we got. Overall - lovely experience in gorgeous setting.

We had an incredible experience at Paradise Green (part of the Daisy Green restaurant chain). We felt warmly welcomed. The food was absolutely amazing just like other Daisy Green chain restaurants, well-balanced, and beautifully presented. Their coffee was equally impressive for a restaurant.

But what truly sets Paradise Green apart is not just the quality of the food and drinks. Our waitress, Elizabeth, went above and beyond in making our visit special. Friendly, attentive, and genuinely caring, she reminded me how rare it is to find such warmth and professionalism in hospitality these days. Daisy Green chain should be super proud to have you.

It's also great to know that the restaurant chain is a women-led business, founded by an Australian woman. Also, it's very hard to find these days...

Thanks so much to Elizabeth and the entire team. We can’t wait to come back!

I had a lovely time at Paradise Green, the staff were warm and accommodating, and the space itself was absolutely beautiful. My only critique would be the limited protein options on the brunch menu, as most were pork based. A bit more variety to cater to different dietary preferences would have really elevated the experience but great time regardless and would definitely recommend

venues.name: Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Notting Hill
venues.description: Creative takes on burgers in a greenery-trimmed space serving brunch & dinner.

reviews.text:
Finally tried this much-talked-about spot! Lots of hype around it, and it does deliver a cozy modern brunch vibe.

The scrambled eggs were perfectly creamy and tasty.
The granola was fresh and balanced, definitely a good choice if you want something lighter.
🥞 The famous pancakes… honestly a bit overrated in my opinion. They’re decent, but maybe not as life changing as the reviews suggest.

Overall, it’s a good brunch stop if you’re around Notting Hill — stylish, buzzy, and worth checking out at least once.

Had the most delightful Saturday brunch with my sister. The selection is a good mix between different breakfasts cuisines and the staples all have their own twist that really works. Gosh the pancake is divine, wish they also had a smaller portion for solo diners.

Just beyond my expectations!
We ordered their pancakes and it was really good topped with hazelnut syrup I guess, but I would recommend to share it! 9/10.
The egg sandwich is 10/10 fluffy egg and delicious sauce in a spongy brioche bun.
Steak & egg was also good! 10/10

Thanks to the chef and the staff👍🏻

Okay this place deserves all the hype. The food was absolutely amazing. We had the cilbir eggs and the crispy chicken sandwich, pork sausages and matcha latte. Service was so fast on a busy morning and everything was great. Loved the vibes. We went without a reservation and waited only for 5 minutes. I think it's easier for 2 people to get a seat.

Lovely atmosphere and very welcoming staff. Coffee was great and the cheddar scrambled eggs and shakshuka were delicious. I tried the famous hazelnut pancake, but honestly it was far too heavy and not the classic pancake style — impossible to finish. Overall, still a nice spot in quiet Notting Hill.

venues.name: Brother Marcus Borough
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Came a few weeks back for an anniversary dinner. Absolutely outstanding food and service, thoroughly looked after. We sat outside and it's perfect for a cool evening in the late summer. Drinks menu was extensive and we'll definitely be back. Also thought it was incredible value for money we were totally stuffed for £50pp and had 2 drinks each.

After walking one round in Borough with not many places to sit for a meal, we headed towards Brother Marcus that is also pet friendly.

Alfresco dining was beautiful and the food is delicately made. They use very fresh ingredients and you get a taste of Mediterranean.

The pita and hummus dip was a delight to begin the meal with the pan fried bream and prawn pasta.  The pasta was well
Made. Maybe even hand made.

We had two lovely desserts

Amazing food and service. This is my second visit to Brother Marcus. The chicken was cooked to perfection, moist, flavourful and not dry. The fluffy pita bread is incredible. It was a summer evening so everyone sat outside and it was a vibe. The service was great and they know the food menu well. Phil who served our table was a super star, polite, caring and attentive. I will come back.

Shah's an amazing server! Very attentive and explained the menu in great detail. My friend had  a few food allergies and the staff went above and beyond to accommodate.

The food was delicious and I can't wait to come back! The best dinner I've had in a long while 😊

If you’re wandering through Borough Market and need a place to park yourself with good food and good vibes, this spot has you covered. The atmosphere is effortlessly chill — the kind of place where time slows down and you forget you only “popped in for a quick bite.” Pro tip: book ahead unless you enjoy the thrill of disappointment.
Here’s the twist: the vegetables here totally upstage the meat. The broccoli and aubergine skewers? Stars of the show. Order them or regret it later. The halloumi with honey is a dreamy little number for those who like their savoury with a side of sweet. As for the calamari… it’s fine, but no standing ovations. We also ordered chicken but I didn’t find it special.

Flavour-wise, they deliver. Price-wise… well, your wallet might raise an eyebrow. Still, if you want a market-side feast where veggies take the crown, this is your spot.

venues.name: Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

attributions: Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone

reviews.text:
I finally got to try the famous Sunday in Brooklyn pancakes, and they were absolutely lovely. Perfectly fluffy, rich in flavour, and not overly sweet, just the right balance that makes them so easy to enjoy. I can completely see why they’re so popular.

On top of the food, the service was excellent. Our server, Marcus, was incredibly attentive and made sure everything was just right throughout the meal. His thoughtful service really added to the experience.

All in all, it was a fantastic visit, and I’ll definitely be coming back again soon!

Well… I came 3 times to this brunch spot to try different dishes.
Breakfast egg sandwich 10/10. Fluffy and well cooked eggs and a spongy bun!
Steak&eggs 9/10 both egg and steak were good and perfectly cooked but the potatoes on the side were a bit dry and tasted like left over potatoes.
Their famous pancakes 10000/10000 really yummy!

Great spot for breakfast! The vibe is really nice and the place is pretty big with lots of seating. Overall, the food was tasty, but I tried their signature pancakes ‘Sunday Pancakes - single' (which is quite big for me and my friend) and felt they were a bit too sweet for me 😅 not really my thing

We enjoyed our meal here today, especially the Shakshuka and Cauliflower Melt burger. The portions are large, with great presentation and rich American flavours.

Staff were friendly and welcoming. We enjoyed the ambience but it was a bit loud in some parts of the restaurant. It was packed with people, and is extremely popular so we’d recommend booking a table in advance, especially on weekends. If you can, ask for a table where it’s quieter.

Overall, great value for money and highly recommended for an authentic American meal.

One of my favorite breakfast spots in London — I always make sure to visit! First time trying this branch though, and the vibe wasn’t as nice as Notting Hill. Food was amazing as always (the pancakes are a must!), but service was a bit unorganized and we had to remind them about our order. Still, I’ll definitely come back! 💛

venues.name: Eggbreak
venues.description: Hip cafe focused on egg dishes, from omelets to eggy pastas, in casual digs with juices and liquor.

reviews.text: We had to download an app in order to book a table. The menu had a great selection of egg dishes, all very tasty and different. It also had sweet dishes and salads. The food was tasty and flavours were great but it is quite pricey for eggs. Service was great. The atmosphere was nothing special.

I stopped by Eggbreak around 9:30 AM without a reservation and was pleasantly surprised to be seated after just a short 10-minute wait, not bad at all for such a popular spot.

The place itself is lovely. The interior has a warm, inviting charm that instantly makes you feel relaxed, and the atmosphere strikes a perfect balance between buzzing and cozy. What stood out just as much was the team, genuinely friendly, always smiling, and attentive without being overbearing. That kind of service goes a long way.

Food and drinks came out quickly, which was impressive given how busy it was. I was tempted to order the whole menu (seriously, everything looked amazing), but I went with the Turkish eggs, and they were absolutely excellent. Rich, flavorful, and satisfying enough to carry me through the day.

All in all, Eggbreak delivered on every level, great vibe, kind service, and food that truly hits the spot. I’ll definitely be back, and maybe next time, I will try everything on the menu

One of my favorite meals and best breakfast while visiting London! Portions were filling, juices were so good and the staff was busy but kind- would definitely come back here for breakfast! Inside is very cute and cozy as well

Small cafe (watch your head of you're tall!) with great food options for breakfast and brunch. The coffee is also really nice (free refills on the house brew). They also offer gluten free bread that was toasted to perfection.
There will likely be a cue when you arrive but it's worth the wait.

Eggbreak had been on my list since I moved to London a year ago. It’s a very popular spot, especially with tourists in the Notting Hill area, so I went in with high expectations. Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing.

Food:
I tried the Egg, Bacon & Cheese Toastie, it looked great but tasted very average, nothing special.

I also ordered Ari’s Pancakes, but couldn’t finish them as the bananas were not fresh, which was off-putting.

I ordered a pot of tea as well, but the tea strainer provided was clearly not clean (as shown in my photos), which was another let-down.

Service & Atmosphere:
The place was very busy, and while that reflects its popularity, the staff seemed rushed and a bit erratic. Service felt inattentive overall.

Overall:
Given all the hype, I expected much better food and service. There are far better breakfast places in London, and I don’t think I’ll be returning to Eggbreak. It would also be hard for me to recommend it to others.

venues.name: Brother Marcus South Kensington
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

address.formatted: SOUTH KENSINGTON STATION ARCADE, 1-3 Pelham St, London

venues.vicinity: SOUTH KENSINGTON STATION ARCADE, 1-3 Pelham St, London

reviews.text: Great dinner experience. Everything we ordered was delicious, and special thanks to our server, Raina! She was super helpful and kindly answered all my questions about the dishes and ingredients and made our dinner extra special:)

Brother Marcus is an absolute gem in London! The atmosphere is warm and stylish, with a relaxed vibe that’s perfect for brunch or a casual dinner. The food was outstanding — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The menu had a great variety of Mediterranean-inspired dishes, and everything we tried was delicious.

The service was friendly and attentive without being overbearing, and the staff made us feel right at home.
Can't wait to come back!

Had an amazing brunch at Brother Marcus on south Kensington ! The food was outstanding.

the fried chicken rösti with eggs was perfectly seasoned and beautifully cooked, the granola with apricot was fresh and light, and the scrambled eggs on toast were spot on. Drinks were refreshing too, especially the watermelon & pomegranate juice.

Service was friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was bright, modern, and welcoming. Everything was well-prepared, delicious, and nicely presented. A great spot for a relaxed brunch.

I’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend!
We had a great time here. The breakfast was delicious and the banana bread is a must-have. Our waitresses Jessica and Raina were super friendly. We would definitely come back again.

Brother Marcus is a lovely, quaint restaurant around the corner from South Kensington Station. As a family we were celebrating a milestone, and greatly appreciated the team's efforts to make us feel special with a bottle of bubbly and dessert. Special shout out to all the staff, the manager and Belle for creating a warm atmosphere coupled with wholesome, good quality plates of food. Would definitely recommend others to try this place!

venues.name: Duck & Waffle
venues.description: British & European cuisine 24/7 in a modern 40th-floor space that has floor-to-ceiling windows.

reviews.text:
Great food and service!  Maitre’d was very kind and accommodated our schedule change with grace and service.

Wonderful food, service, ambiance was scenic.

English breakfast was amazing, duck and waffles signature dish is like butter melting in your mouth.

An absolute amazing experience! Took myself on a solo date there and had a great time. The food was delicious, the service was impeccable. The waffle was light and fluffy and the sweet sauce complemented the duck just perfectly.  Strongly recommend!

I had a lovely experience at Waffle and Duck. The food was really tasty and beautifully presented, and the staff were very friendly and attentive, making us feel well looked after. Our order arrived quickly, which was a nice surprise. They also have a great selection of wines to complement the meal. On top of all that, the view is absolutely amazing – it really adds to the whole dining experience. Highly recommended!

We dined at Duck & Waffle as a group of 9, and everything from start to finish was absolutely exceptional. The food was delicious, the ambiance was vibrant yet classy, and the drinks were perfectly crafted. The service was also fantastic — attentive, friendly, and efficient, even with our large group.

Of course, the duck dish is a must-try — it absolutely lives up to the hype!

Highly recommend visiting Duck & Waffle when in London. It’s a memorable experience in every way — food, views, and vibes all on point!

We had a great time at our visit to Duck & Waffle. You can't beat the ambiance or views of the city (from the 40th floor!), the service was on point, and everything we ordered—from cocktails to food—was fabulous.

Recommended:
- Waffle on the Rocks
- Crushed Piña
- Spicy Verde
- CHEESY POLENTA CROQUETAS (insanely good)
- DUCK BARBACOA TACOS (also insanely good)
- CRISPY BBQ BEEF PUFFS
- CAESAR SALAD
- SIRLOIN AU POIVRE
- MAC ‘N’ CHEESE (lovely)
- TRUFFLE MASH (so good)

I will absolutely be back on my next trip to London!

venues.name: Milk Beach Soho
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
We had an incredible experience at Milk Beach Soho for my friend’s birthday lunch. I called ahead due to train delays, and Kimberly kindly reassured me they would hold our table, a huge relief on such a special day.
From start to finish, everything was perfect. The ambience is relaxed yet vibrant, even the restrooms are beautifully designed, with calming ocean sounds. The food was delicious, thoughtfully presented, and portions were just right. We didn’t even finish everything, which surprised us!
A heartfelt thank you to Swiz, who truly made our experience exceptional. She was warm, attentive, and explained the menu with care, suggesting drinks tailored to our preferences and they were exactly what we loved. Her service struck the perfect balance of professionalism and friendliness without ever rushing us.
The birthday surprise was the cherry on top: a small dessert brought out with a lit candle, a handwritten “Happy Birthday” card, and a tiny gift box tied with a bow containing a bite-sized sweet. My friend described it as “a little piece of heaven.” That thoughtful gesture made her day.
It was our first time at Milk Beach Soho and certainly won’t be the last. Absolutely memorable in every way.

We visited Milk Beach in SoHo and had such a wonderful experience. The atmosphere was welcoming and stylish, and from the moment we arrived the service was friendly, attentive, and professional. The food was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every dish we tried felt thoughtfully prepared and exceeded our expectations.

Overall, Milk Beach is a fantastic spot that combines great service with outstanding food. We’ll definitely be back and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting SoHo.

An absolutely amazing experience. From the moment we arrived, the service stood out - the host who checked our reservation was warm and welcoming, and our waitress was lovely throughout.

We sat out on the patio, which truly gave off beach day vibes - the atmosphere felt like a little summer escape in the middle of Soho. We were a group of six, and everything was handled smoothly and efficiently.

We tried a good number of cocktails (all fantastic), and honestly worked our way through most of the menu ; which, while not huge, is well-curated. The portions were generous, the food was excellent, and the setting just elevated the whole afternoon.
Highly recommend for a relaxed, sun-soaked outing with great food, drinks, and service.

I recently went to the barre and yoga socials at Milk Beach and it was such a fun experience! The classes were super well run – Brittney did an amazing job organising everything and bringing in great instructors who made the sessions both challenging and enjoyable. After the workouts, everyone hung out over share plates and cocktails, which was the perfect way to relax and connect with others. On top of that, there were lots of goodies given out just for attending, which was such a nice surprise. Overall, such a well put together event – can’t wait for the next one!

An absolute gem! The food was delicious, the prices are incredibly reasonable and the venue is great. But what really sets this place apart is the staff - they went above and beyond to accommodate all our needs (thanks Kimberly!), we’re wonderfully attentive, and genuinely lovely. I wish I could give them 10 stars! Definitely becoming a regular here.

venues.name: Broken Eggs
venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: omg i love this place. If you want nice tortillas, pan con tomato, peppers, croquettes you must go. Its located in Fitzrovia,

This has quickly become one of my favourite restaurants in London! The food is incredible - authentic, full of flavour, and perfectly seasoned every time. The tortilla and pan con tomate are my favourite dishes! The service is just as impressive, with Daniel being a particularly outstanding server - attentive, friendly, and genuinely welcoming. I highly recommend this place!
The food was absolutely delicious. Honest, down to earth Spanish cooking. The croquetas and tortilla were divine. I left here full and very happy and I'll definitely be going back.

Great tortilla options with the best chorizo I’ve had. There’s some sunny tables outside that get great sun in the middle of the day. The interior is so cute too and would be great for a wine date night
The best Spanish food so far! Everything was so perfect, food, the staff, atmosphere! We would love to go back as soon as possible.

venues.name: Drunch Oxford Circus
venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: A lovely little brunch cafe near Oxford Circus with indoor and outdoor seating options. It's a bit of a walk from the main road so a good distance away from all the noise. The service was friendly and the food was tasty, plus a bonus that they have gluten free a bread option.

Exceptional service from start to finish the moment we arrived at Drunch. Every member of the team delivered with genuine care, warmth, and a true passion for hospitality. Special thanks to Khadija and Pujan—your attention to detail and commitment to excellence did not go unnoticed.

The omelette was absolutely delicious and made just to my expectations! My sister’s burger and my mum’s grilled chicken salad were just as impressive. Hats off to the chef—every dish was spot on!

You both went above and beyond to ensure we felt welcomed and well taken care of. We’ll definitely be back!

The veggie full english and the mexican benedict eggs, which were very nice and good portions too. We also got the fashion coffees, good and nice to take pics of. the buttermilk fried chicken was small (only 5 pieces) and very bland, wouldn’t recommend.

I visited this place in London and was very pleased🩷👍👍. The interior is stylish and cozy - it's nice to be inside. I ordered Grilled Salmon on skewers with guacamole - the salmon was perfectly fried, juicy and tender, and the guacamole added freshness and piquancy. Superfood Salad pleasantly surprised with a combination of couscous, avocado, walnuts, pineapple and corn - hearty, tasty and healthy.

For dessert, I took R.I.P. Diet Cheesecake - incredibly tender and tasty, with an ideal balance of sweetness. The Pink Dreams cocktail pleased with a light berry taste and beautiful presentation.

The service was attentive and friendly. Everything was served quickly and with a smile. I will definitely come back again - a great place with delicious food and a pleasant atmosphere!

We were by Oxford Circus looking for somewhere to eat before travelling back to Birmingham when we stumbled across this place and my goodness, what a find.
The place is gorgeous, the food was incredible and the staff were so nice. They let us store our suitcases in a back area and quickly gave us a table even though we were a party of 6 without a reservation.
The food was delicious and the drinks were equally good. I had a pistachio chai latte and I honestly could have drank six of them. I also had an orange, carrot and ginger juice which I could tell had been freshly squeezed as I ordered it.
Very good value for money and as someone who doesn’t eat pork, I was delighted to find that I could still have a full English as they offer beef sausage and turkey bacon.

venues.name: The Breakfast Club Soho
venues.description: English and American breakfasts, plus comfort foods and burgers in cheerful, quirky surrounds.

reviews.text: Cozy breakfast spot located right in the heart of Soho serving delicious savory dishes. An absolute refreshing change from the usual sweet heavy brunch menus. We visited as a group of six and were seated impressively quickly, which is rare for central London. The staff were warm, attentive and made us feel welcome right away. I was especially impressed by their Strawberry Matcha. High quality, vibrant and just sweet enough. The Iced Latte with an extra shot of caramel was also excellent. As for food, I recommend the Smashed Avocado Toast topped with crispy bacon, and hash browns. Generous portions and packed with flavor. If you’re after a savory brunch spot with great service, central location and fair pricing, this place is well worth a visit.🥑🍳

Overall a good experience, the staff were really friendly but the service was a little slow. We pre booked but were only allowed the table for 1 hour, so it felt a little rushed because we were celebrating a birthday. The food itself was really good but I would really recommend pre-booking as there was a long queue if you hadn't. For vegans there is a lot of choice.

This place is great. We waited around 15 minutes for a table but understandably so. It’s so good. Well worth the wait. I went with my mum and she got scrambled eggs on an absolute door stop piece of sourdough. Both were cooked to perfection. I got the Big Stack and my god it was good. It had the best of both worlds: pancakes and bacon/egg etc etc. so full I didn’t finish it. Also had a delish vanilla matcha.
They have a few locations in the city so if the one you want to go to has a queue then there will be another not too far away!

Perfect place for a good breakfast in Central London! The All American is pretty good, the poached eggs in particular were cooked properly. I did not like the pancakes, they were too thick in my opinion. In any case, I would recommend this place.
Consider a relatively quick queue for entering.

Restaurant specializing in breakfast. The menu goes from a full English to fluffy pancakes and every breakfast item in between. There's a short cocktail menu if you need that morning mimosa. The service is friendly, swift and helpful. The restaurant is card payment only.
Ordered the Eggs Benedict, my go to dining out breakfast item. The eggs were overcooked. The muffins were tough, spent a lot of time sawing through them.
Overall it was tasty but not a pleasure to eat. I told the staff this after they asked and was offered a free coffee.
Was disappointed with the quality of what I ordered, but would go back and order something different.

venues.name: The Table Café
venues.description: Breakfast-to-dinner British fare served in a bright, modern space.

reviews.text:
We were really impressed by The Table! It’s a small, charming restaurant with a very cozy atmosphere and lots of plants that give it a lovely, rustic touch. The menus are colorful and nicely designed, and the staff were all super friendly and attentive.

We had The Table Full English — a classic English breakfast and everything was absolutely delicious and served hot. The quality of the food was excellent, and you could really taste that it was freshly prepared.

They also offer vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options, which is fantastic. Debora was especially knowledgeable and gave me great advice on the gluten-free alternatives available.

A big thank you to Debora, who took such great care of us and gave wonderful service and recommendations. :)

We can definitely recommend this place — great food, warm atmosphere, and lovely people!

We visited The Table again today, and once more we were absolutely delighted. The dishes were freshly prepared in the open kitchen, which we really love — it’s such a great and inviting concept.

This time, we had the brunch classics: Smoked Ham Hock + Chorizo Hash with Halloumi and an Avocado + Feta Toast with bacon. Everything was delicious and beautifully presented.

Our server today was Daniel, who double-checked my gluten-free option and made sure everything was just right. He provided excellent service.

Very much enjoyed my meal out on Saturday, sheltering from the rain.
Waffles (with cinnamon pear and shortbread crumb) were gorgeous and they were happy to accept my substitutions. So many options, I was overwhelmed! Will just have to come back 😁😁
Our server was so nice and really made the experience extra special.

The food at The Table Café is amazing! We ordered a burrata salad and a classic English breakfast, and everything was absolutely perfect.

We had to sit outside because there weren't any seats inside, which wasn't our favorite thing, but honestly, the food was just so good that it made up for it!

Beautiful cafe with a lovely secluded outdoor seating area. Outdoor seating is under large canopies with heaters. Indoor seating is lovely and open with an open kitchen at the back. Service was fantastic, we waited only a couple of minutes for a table. Food was really good. We had the eggs royale and brunch waffles. Both were brilliant, really tasty and decent size portions. The ice chai latte was also so good, like a milkshake! Seems to be popular so would recommend booking if you really want to come.

venues.name: Nessa Soho
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: The dining area had a nice and cozy ambiance with dim lighting. It took about ten minutes to get the bread (7£ for four small slices is pretty steep). The mains took an approximate additional thirty minutes to arrive afterwards. The chicken breast was overcooked and dry and for 28£ it should have had more substance. The squash ravioli had the strangest flavor of sweetness and were absolutely not enjoyable to eat. Service charge included in the bill. Will definitely not be back or recommend this place for an enjoyable food experience.

The food was 10/10!! The service was a tad slow that night but staff were all very kind regardless. The pear, kale & squash salad was delicious, the whipped butter that came with the rolled out soda bread was so soft and airy, and of course the sea bream was absolutely divine, we literally ate in silence and didn't even spare time to snag a photo because it was THAT good. The mocktails and the jaffa dessert were also amazing! This’ll be on my top recommended!

Absolutely loved my visit to Nessa! The pancakes were epic—light, fluffy, and full of flavor. The chicken burger was also delicious: perfectly cooked, juicy, and packed with taste. The team was super friendly and welcoming, creating such a warm and relaxed atmosphere. Service was spot on without ever feeling rushed. A fab spot for brunch or a casual bite—can’t wait to go back!

Went on Sunday 31/08 for a birthday brunch with 10 of my friends. I must say, STEFANIA, the lovely, professional yet welcoming was superb. She catered and assisted EVERY person on the table and we was quiet a handful but she managed it very well from the specific orders to cake preference which the pricing was absurd but she made me feel at ease paying it all with delight that’s how great she is. She is an asset to the team, will actually be telling all my peers to Visit this restaurant just because of STEFANIA, thank you for making our Sunday a great a service! She deserves a raise

We were a group of 6 girls. The staff were nice. However, we ordered orange juice but it was full of pulp and it was very better. You could tell they just get it without any effort and the quality of oranges were not very good and quantity was very very small. It was smaller than a glass of water. The other thing that was disappointing was that one of the cappuccinos we ordered was already split it from the kitchen and then the waiter served it for us and he spilled a bit on the the girl and he didn’t even apologise and the girl was a bit shy to tell him but it looked like it was badly made and under the mug you could see that the coffee was spilled from the kitchen and there was not even an apology.

At the end of our stay a waitress came to us and said are you guys ordering any drinks or should I get the bill which I found a bit rude because we were enjoying our time and we  actually got a lot of plates and coffees, so I didn’t find the service very good however the other staff were really nice. They did replace the orange juice with a cappuccino.

Overall, I wouldn’t come again to that place because the food was overpriced and some of the plates weren’t the best. One of the plates had bacon and the bacon was very overcooked and stiff and the toasts are the muffins were a bit too toasted.

But I would say it’s a nice place for a coffee meet up but only for coffee

venues.name: Bill's Covent Garden Restaurant
venues.description: Contemporary European chain dishing up separate breakfast, afternoon tea, lunch and dinner menus.

address.formatted: St Martin's Courtyard, Slingsby Pl, London

venues.vicinity: St Martin's Courtyard, Slingsby Pl, London

reviews.text: I had never been to a Bill’s before but I am so happy I stumbled across this place. There are so many delicious options on the menu that I had trouble deciding but I ended up picking the Big Breakfast plate on their weekend brunch menu. We were served by Beata who was so kind and informative-we would come back just for her service again! To top it all off the atmosphere here is to die for. It’s very homey and cute-fairy lights and umbrella type vibe. This was definitely one of the better restaurants I’ve been to in recent months.

Food was absolutely amazing, quick to the table and presented beautifully. Coffee was one of the best tasting I've had in a long time and and the tea came in a pot. Our server Dana was sweet and caring. Would go again in a heartbeat.

Absolutely delicious breakfast. I was initially drawn to Bill's because of the pancakes, but ended up trying a savory dish instead - squash, spinach, and feta on sourdough with two poached eggs. So different and really tasty. Service was a delight, Dana was warm and accommodating. Would love to return for lunch or dinner.

The customer service was excellent — super helpful and friendly, we felt welcomed from the start. Our server Marianna was especially sweet and attentive. The English breakfast was generous, tasty, and reasonably priced. The place itself is absolutely beautiful inside and out. If I had to nitpick, the only downside would be the cleanliness of the toilet.

We ordered the Dubai chocolate pancakes, berry pancakes, and triple chocolate pancakes. Everything was delicious, and the atmosphere is nice, however I thought it would've been nicer if the Dubai chocolate pancakes had a kunefe element (maybe as a filling?) to add some crunch. The service was a bit slow to be honest, the waiter didn't come back to take our order for quite a long time, and then he never brought tap water after we asked so I had to find someone else to ask for it. The tea pot was also steaming hot so it was difficult to pour.

venues.name: KOZZEE Cafe Soho | Brunch, Coffee & Desserts
venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: I had a lovely experience at this English breakfast spot. The food was hearty and satisfying, but what really made my visit special was the service. Our server, NAV, was exceptionally friendly and attentive from start to finish. They made sure everything was perfect and added such a warm, welcoming touch to the meal. I would definitely recommend asking for Nav if you visit—great service makes the breakfast even better!

I really enjoyed the English breakfast here! The portions were generous and well-balanced, with every element cooked perfectly. The coffee was also a highlight smooth, rich, and exactly to my taste. On top of that, the staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better. A wonderful start to the day, highly recommended!
Excellent breakfast and service. Lovely staff. Would recommend reserving ahead, as we were lucky to take their last available table. So much choice and will definitely return.

Our breakfast and tea, very nice service.
Avocado Toast, Generous portion of avocado, well seasoned with chili flakes, black sesame, pumpkin seeds, and topped with rocket.
Full English Breakfast Plate: Scrambled eggs look fluffy and bright.
•	Crispy bacon, a good-sized sausage, baked beans, roasted cherry tomatoes, mushrooms, tater tots, and toast with butter.
•	Balanced portioning, not greasy — feels slightly more modern than a traditional greasy spoon fry-up.

I was starving and so this place lured me in with their delicious looking food, I thought my taste buds were going to have a good time but…no. Tasted of disappointment and broken dreams.
